Mix chicken breasts, egg whites, 1 teaspoon cornstarch, salt and 1 tablespoon rice wine or rice vinegar. Marinade for half an hour to overnight. Mix together and set aside, broth, 1 tablespoon cornstarch and soy sauce.
Put small amount of oil in skillet. Fry garlic until brown. Remove and set aside. Fry chicken just until done, but very light brown. Drain and set aside. Drain water, chestnuts, and bamboo shoots. Add vegetables to skillet (along with garlic) and stir 3 to 5 minutes until crisp and tender. Add chicken and broth mixture. Heat through until thick. Sprinkle with cashews and serve immediately over steamed rice.

name: Cashew Chicken
author: Rachael Schlosser

ingredients.name: whole chicken breasts, skinned, and boned
large sweet red pepper, cubed, or 2 to 3 small red hot peppers, shredded

instructions: Cut chicken into 1 inch squares. Mix soy sauce, chicken broth, cornstarch, sugar, and MSG (optional) in a plastic bag or bowl. Add chicken cubes and marinate about fifteen minutes. Heat oil until it reaches 176.7° C and saute cashews until golden, about 30 seconds; remove and set aside. Add marinated chicken cubes and stir fry for 3-4 minutes or until chicken turns white; remove from pan and set aside. Add onion, green pepper, and red pepper to pan; cook about 1 minute. Return nuts and chicken to pan. Mix thoroughly. Cook 1 minute and serve.

name: Chicken Tetrazzini
author: Louise Alderman

ingredients.name: can of cream of chicken soup (undiluted)

instructions: In a large pan melt butter and add soups. Remove from heat and add rest of ingredients except cheese. Pour into greased casserole dish and sprinkle with cheese. Bake uncovered at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes or until bubbly. If made ahead and refrigerated, it will take longer to bake.

name: Chicken Tetrazzini
author: Shelly Dohogne
instructions: Boil chicken and cut into bite-size pieces. Cook noodles and drain. Spray 9 x 13 inch pan with Pam. Layer noodles, then chicken. Mix chicken broth and mushroom soup and then pour over chicken. Saute peppers for next layer. Top with cheese. Bake at 250° for 20 minutes or 350° for 10 minutes.

name: One Pot Chicken Tetrazzini
author: Shirley Boham
instructions: Saute onion and celery in butter. Arrange chicken in layer over onion and celery. Add spaghetti and rest of ingredients. Cover and bring to a boil, simmer for 15 to 20 minutes. Garnish with grated Parmesan cheese and paprika.

name: Country Chicken with Creamy Gravy (Chicken)
author: Rebecca Hooper

ingredients.name: (4 oz.) skinned, boned chicken breast halves

instructions: Place cereal, paprika, poultry seasoning, thyme, salt, and pepper in a shallow dish, stirring well to combine. Pour eggs in a shallow bowl or dish. Dip chicken breast halves in eggs to coat. Dredge in cereal mixture. Place coated chicken in a 11 x 7 x 2 inch baking dish with thickest portions towards outside of dish. Cover with wax paper, and microwave at high for 12 minutes or until chicken is done. Rotate dish a half turn every 4 minutes. You can also bake chicken in the oven at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes. Spoon Creamy Gravy evenly over chicken. Serve immediately.

name: Country Chicken with Creamy Gravy (Gravy)
author: Rebecca Hooper

ingredients.name: c. plus 2 tsp. canned chicken broth

instructions: Combine butter and flour in saucepan on top of stove. Over low heat gradually add milk, and broth stirring until smooth. Cook until thickened. Add salt and pepper. Add chives if desired. Serve over chicken.

name: Oven Fried Chicken
author: S.P.
instructions: Mix bread crumbs, cheese, salt and pepper. Dip chicken in butter. Roll in bread crumb mixture. Place in baking dish, sprinkle with paprika. Bake at 350° for 1 hour. Do not turn chicken while cooking. It will brown on both sides.

name: Great Tasting Chicken Nuggets
author: Ramona Glastetter

ingredients.name: Shake 'n Bake seasoning and coating mixture

instructions: Cut chicken breasts in 1/2 to 2 inch pieces. Shake chicken pieces with coating mixture; discard any remaining mixture. Bake at 400° for 10 to 15 minutes or until cooked through.

name: Chicken Puffs
author: S.P.
instructions: Melt butter in 1/4 cup boiling water. Add flour and dash of salt; stir vigorously. Cook and stir mixture until dough forms a ball that doesn't separate. Remove from heat and cool slightly. Add egg and beat vigorously until smooth. Stir in cheese. Drop dough onto greased baking sheet, using level teaspoon of dough for each puff. Bake at 375°.

name: Baked Chicken Breast
author: Helen Cox
instructions:
Combine sour cream, lemon juice, Worcestershire sauce, celery salt, salt, paprika, garlic, salt, and pepper. Add chicken to sour cream mixture coating each piece. Let stand overnight. Heat oven to 35°. Roll chicken in crumbs, coating evenly. Arrange in large shallow pan in single layer. Cover with sour cream mixture. Bake for approximately 1 hour.
Along with the above I bake in casserole dish, 1 can beef consomme soup, 1 cup rice, 1 can rice, 1 can water and 1 stick margarine for 1 hour. Serve with chicken or separately.

name: Crock-Pot Chicken and Rice Casserole
author: C. Allen Collier

ingredients.name: small can cream of chicken soup
small can cream of celery soup
small can cream of mushroom soup

instructions:
Mix in crock-pot the 3 cans of soup and rice. Place the chicken on top of the mixture, then add the diced celery. Cook for 3 hours on high or 4 hours on low.
More rice, about 1/2 cup, and 2 additional chicken breasts may be added to make 6 servings.

name: Busy Day Chicken
author: Lori Reinagel
instructions: Grease 9 x 12 x 2 inch pan on bottom and sides. Sprinkle rice over bottom. Warm soup with milk in microwave for 2 minutes. Stir. Pour over rice and arrange chicken pieces over this. Sprinkle with onion soup mix. Cover and bake at 350° for about 1 1/2 to 2 hours.

name: Honey Mustard Chicken
author: R.P.
instructions: Place chicken in glass dish. Squeeze lemon over chicken. Mix mustard, honey, paprika, and basil. Spread over chicken and marinate for 1 hour. Turn and baste all over. Bake at 350° for 45 to 60 minutes.

name: Rotel Chicken Casserole
author: S.P.

ingredients.name: chicken breasts, stewed, boned, cut in small pieces

instructions: Place a layer of crushed chips in bottom of 9 x 13 inch dish. Mix together soups, Rotel, broth, and chicken (a whisk works well). Pour 1/2 mixture over chip layer. Sprinkle 1/2 of the cheese over soup mixture. Repeat chip layer. Pour remaining soup mixture over chips. Repeat cheese layer. Cover top with light layer of crushed chips. Bake 30 minutes at 350°.

name: Taco Chicken
author: Don and Clara Essner Family
instructions: rumble Doritos chips and layer at the bottom of a 9 x 12 inch dish. Next layer is your deboned chicken. Mix together soups and Rotel tomatoes until they start boiling. Pour over the chicken layer. Cover dish with Saran Wrap and microwave for 25 minutes. Take off Saran Wrap and sprinkle cheese on top. Microwave until cheese is melted.

ingredients.name: medium whole chicken breasts, skinned and boned
chicken-flavor bouillon cube or envelope or 1 teaspoon chicken flavor stock base

yield.name: Spread chicken breasts flat; fold cheese and ham slices to fit on top. Fold breasts over filling and fasten edges with toothpicks. On waxed paper, mix flour and paprika; use mixture to coat chicken pieces. In a 12-inch skillet over medium heat, in hot butter or marga- rine, cook chicken until browned on all sides. Add wine and bouillon. Reduce heat to low; cover and simmer 30 minutes or until fork-tender; remove the toothpicks. In cup, blend cornstarch and cream until smooth; gradually stir into skillet. Cook, stirring constantly, until thickened. Serve over chicken.

name: Chicken Perigord-Style
author: Annita Layton

ingredients.name: whole chicken breasts, skinned and boned

instructions: In 12-inch skillet or 6-quart Dutch oven over medium-high heat, in 6 tablespoons hot butter or margarine, cook chicken, a few pieces at a time, until browned on all sides. Set chicken aside. In drippings, over medium heat, in remaining 2 tablespoons butter, cook mush- rooms until golden, about 5 minutes. With slotted spoon, remove mushrooms to small bowl. Into drippings, over medium heat, stir flour and salt until blended. Gradually stir in chicken broth and half- and-half and cook, stirring constantly, until mixture is thickened. Place chicken and mushrooms in sauce. Reduce heat to low; cover and simmer 25 minutes.

name: Chicken Stew
author: Dale Schlosser
instructions: Pressure chickens until done. Strain the broth into 30 gallon kettle. Debone the chicken and cube it. Then add all vegetables and other ingredients and cook until done.

name: Buttermilk Pecan Chicken
author: Annita Layton

ingredients.name: to 3 lb. boneless, skinless chicken breasts

instructions: Place butter in large shallow roasting pan in oven until melted. Remove and set aside. Mix buttermilk and egg; set aside. Combine flour, pecans, paprika, salt and pepper in medium bowl. Coat chicken in buttermilk mixture, then in flour mixture. Place in roasting pan, turn to coat with butter. Bake at 375° about 45 minutes to 1 hour until chicken is a deep golden brown.

name: Evelyn Kluesner's Chicken Casserole
author: Louise Alderman

ingredients.name: can cream of mushroom or cream of chicken soup

instructions:
Cook Rice-A-Roni according to box directions adding 1/2 cup extra liquid. Stir in soup mixing thoroughly, then add chicken meat. Pour into casserole and top with crushed potato chips. Bake at 350° 15 to 20 minutes.
I have used chicken broth instead of water when fixing.

name: Chicken Casserole
author: Louise Alderman

ingredients.name: pkg. Uncle Ben's Long Grain wild rice

instructions:
Make the rice ahead as directed on package. Prepare other ingredients. Mix altogether and place in 9 x 13 inch pan. Bake at 300° for 45 minutes.
This can be made the day before and refrigerated or frozen. It may take longer to bake if cold.

name: Corn Dogs
author: Zachary Estes
instructions: Mix cornmeal with flour, sugar, baking powder and salt. Add egg and milk; blend in melted shortening. Mix well. Dip wieners in Zachary Estes batter. Fry in deep fat.

name: Beer Wieners
author: Maris P.
instructions: Cut each hot dog into four pieces. Boil all the hot dogs in the beer. When hot dogs are done, add ketchup and brown sugar. Bring to boil and cook on medium heat for 30 minutes until mixture is thick.

name: He-Man Quiche
author: Maris P.

ingredients.name: small pkg. Monterey Jack pepper cheese
pkg. chopped broccoli, cooked and drained

instructions: After preparing ingredients, pour into a big bowl and stir well. Cover with pie crust strips like an apple pie. Do not pack mixture down. Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.

name: Ham and Cheese Quiche
author: Karen
instructions: Cook, drain and chop broccoli. Layer half of broccoli, ham and cheese in shell. Repeat with second half. Sprinkle onion over it and set aside. Gradually stir milk into eggs and add seasonings. Pour into pastry shell and bake at 450° for 10 minutes. Reduce heat to 325° and cook 35 minutes. Let stand a few minutes before serving.

name: Quiche Lorraine
author: M.E.

ingredients.name: c. (7 oz.) Swiss cheese, natural, coarsely shredded

instructions: Bake pastry shell at 425° until lightly browned. Cool. Fry bacon until crisp, let cool, crumble. Saute mushrooms. Place bacon into pas- try shell. Sprinkle cheese and mushrooms over the bacon. Mix season- ings and sprinkle over cheese. Beat eggs and half-and-half together. Pour over cheese and bacon. Bake 45 minutes or until lightly browned and knife inserted into the center comes out clean.

name: Karen's Cornbread Dressing
author: Karen Marie

ingredients.name: to 4 c. Pepperidge Farm Stuffing Mix

instructions: Mix together cornbread, eggs, and buttermilk. Add onions and celery. Pour into greased skillet and bake 1 hour at 350°. Remove from skillet and let cool. Crumble cornbread. Add remaining ingredients. Pour into greased 9 x 13 inch pan. Bake at 350° an additional 45 to 50 minutes.

name: Brunch Eggs
author: Shirley Drury

ingredients.name: (1 lb.) pkg. Wilson's pork sausage, browned and drained
slices white bread, cubed, without crusts

instructions: Mix eggs, milk, and mustard. Gently add other ingredients to the mixture. Salt and pepper to taste. Pour into a greased 9 x 13 inch cake pan. Refrigerate overnight. Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.

name: Breakfast Casserole
author: Anna Rose Bles
instructions: Put bread in the bottom of a greased casserole dish. Mix together other ingredients and pour over bread. Refrigerate overnight. Bake 45 minutes at 350°. Variation: Mushrooms, green peppers, and onions can be added.

name: Egg Casserole
author: Rebecca Hooper

ingredients.name: lb. bacon or ham, cooked and drained

instructions: Mix together in 9 x 13 casserole dish and cover. Store in the refrigerator overnight. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.

name: Macaroni and Egg
author: In Memory of Mrs. Theon (Ella) Schlosser, Charlotte Hooper
instructions:
Boil macaroni until done. Drain well. Place margarine in skillet and melt. Add macaroni and eggs. Cook until eggs are done.
This recipe is from Mrs. Theon (Ella) J. Schlosser Sr. We as a family used it a lot on the farm especially during Lent and on Fridays

name: Reuben Sandwich
author: Clint Estes
instructions: Place corned beef, then sauerkraut, Miracle Whip and cheese on 4 slices of bread. Top with other bread slices. Spread butter on outside of bread. Grill in skillet or on griddle until browned and cheese melts.

name: Canning Tomatoes
author: Sister Henrica Huck
instructions: Sterilize jars and lids. Blanche tomatoes and peel. Fill jars with whole or parts of tomatoes. Add sugar and salt but no water. Seal tight. Place jars on cookie sheet in 250° oven for 1 hour. Do not pre-heat oven. Leave in oven overnight.

name: Corn Relish
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Combine ingredients in a large kettle and cook for 20 minutes Pour in jars and seal at once.

name: Vegetable Pizza
author: Jennifer Clark
instructions: Press the crescent rolls into a 15 x 10 x 1 inch baking sheet to form a crust. Bake in 350° oven for 12-15 minutes. Combine cream cheese, mayonnaise and ranch dressing mix. Spread thinly over cooled crust. Top with cheese and vegetables.

name: Easy Vegetable Pizza
author: Rebecca Hooper

ingredients.name: pkg. dry Hidden Valley Ranch Dressing

instructions: Add dry dressing to sour cream and stir. Smear the mixture, evenly over the pizza crust. Clean and cut the vegetables then add them to the top. Also add the cheese. Serve or refrigerate until needed.

name: Egg Rolls
author: Annita Layton

ingredients.name: pkg. Spring egg roll wrappers, square
fairly large head of cabbage, cut like slaw
lb. pork sausage (ground pork shoulder, etc.)
pkg. fresh mushrooms or 1 large can

instructions: Brown pork, mushrooms, onion and garlic until lightly brown; drain. Blanche cabbage and carrots by putting them in boiling water and bringing the water to a boil again. Boil for 30 to 60 seconds more until done but still crunchy. Drain and run cold water over them. Pick up handfuls and squeeze ALL water out. Put in bowl and mix seasonings to taste. Add 1 egg and 1 egg white. Beat egg yolk and add 1 Tbsp. water. Set aside. Put a wrapper in front of you, like a diamond. Put 1/4 cup of mixture on bottom half. Roll up halfway. Fold corners in and spread yolk on rest. Roll up. Fry in skillet with plenty of grease. Can freeze. Thaw well before frying.

name: Fried Rice
author: C.A.
instructions:
In hot nonstick skillet, scramble egg; remove from skillet and cut up into tiny pieces. Set aside. Stir cooked onions, celery and carrots in the same skillet until slightly softened. Stir in rice. Add soy sauce. Cook at high heat for 3 minutes, stirring constantly. Stir in scrambled egg, remove form heat and serve immediately.
Variation: Add 1/4 cup chicken, diced.

name: Fried Rice
author: Rebecca Hooper

ingredients.name: c. chopped cooked meat *Meat can be chicken, pork, beef, shrimp, lobster, sausage, or bacon.

instructions: Saute onion in hot oil until golden brown. Add rice; heat thor- oughly, stirring often. Stir in beaten eggs, pepper, beef flavor base and soy sauce. Saute 3 minutes, continuing to stir. Add meat and continue heating until mixture is steaming hot.

name: Fried Rice
author: Annita Layton
instructions:
Prepare eggs as for scrambled eggs. Remove and set aside. Melt butter; add onion and saute 2 to 3 minutes. Add pepper and carrots; stir fry for 1 to 2 minutes. Add seasonings and soy sauce to taste. Add rice and eggs. Heat through.
Variation: One small can of drained, cooked salad shrimp may be added with seasonings.

name: Soy Fried Rice
author: Christine Estes

ingredients.name: bunch green onions and tops, sliced
(14 oz.) box Minute rice, cooked as directed or 1 c. regular rice, cooked and drained
c. cooked, diced shrimp or 1 c. cooked, diced

instructions: Heat oil; add eggs, mixing constantly while breaking up with fork. Add eggs and onions to rice with soy sauce to color rice brown. Blend very well and serve hot. (Can be reheated in oven at 350° for 30 minutes.) If desired, stir in 1 cup cooked, diced shrimp or 1 cup cooked, diced pork tenderloin.

name: Spanish Rice
author: C. Allen Collier
instructions:
In bacon drippings, cook rice, onion and green pepper until onion is tender. Add bacon and other ingredients. Cover and simmer over low heat about 30 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid absorbed.
Note: For quick cooking rice, add 2.5 cups Minute rice after all other ingredients are addded. Remove from heat and let stand 5 minutes. Fluff with fork

name: Sweet Rice
author: Catrina Stone
instructions: Cook rice in water until done. Drain. Add sugar, butter and milk. Cook until thick. Serve with cinnamon sprinkled on each serving.

name: Macaroni and Cheese
author: S.P.

ingredients.name: c. (8 oz.) sharp process American cheese

instructions: Cook the macaroni in boiling salted water until tender; drain. In saucepan, melt butter; blend in flour, salt and pepper. Add milk; cook and stir until thick and bubbly. Add cheese, cubed, stir until melted. Mix cheese sauce with macaroni. Turn into 1/2 quart casserole. Bake at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes, or until heated through.

name: Macaroni and Cheese
author: Caleb Estes

ingredients.name: or 2 lb. Velveeta cheese *American cheese can also be used instead of Velveeta. Use about 8 slices.

instructions:
American cheese can also be used instead of Velveeta. Ue about 8 slices.
Mix all ingredients together and cook until cheese is melted. May need more cheese or milk to your taste.

name: Macaroni Imperial
author: Vernita Bles

ingredients.name: c. uncooked macaroni, broken in pieces

instructions: Cook macaroni in large amount of boiling salt water until done. Then drain. Combine bread crumbs, butter, red and green peppers, onion, salt and cheese. Add hot milk over egg yolks, stirring well. Add macaroni then fold in egg whites. Pour into well greased casserole. Bake in a moderate oven 325°, until firm.

name: Onion Roasted Potatoes
author: Donna Stamp

ingredients.name: envelope Lipton Onion Recipe Soup Mix
lb. all purpose potatoes, cut into large chunks

instructions: Preheat oven to 450°. In large plastic bowl or bag, add all ingredients. Close bag and shake, or toss in bowl, until potatoes are evenly coated. Empty potatoes into shallow baking or roasting pan; discard bag. Bake, stirring occasionally, 40 minutes. Or until potatoes are tender and golden brown. Garnish, if desired, with chopped parsley.

name: Onion Roasted Potatoes
author: Germaine Robert

ingredients.name: envelope Lipton Recipe Secrets onion soup mix
lb. unpeeled potatoes, cut into large chunks

instructions: Preheat oven to 450°. In large plastic bag, add all ingredients. Close bag and shake until potatoes are evenly coated. Empty potatoes into shallow baking pan. Bake stirring occasionally, 40 minutes or until potatoes are tender and golden brown.

name: Deluxe Mashed Potatoes
author: Rita Koeppel

ingredients.name: Instant potato mix and ingredients needed for serving of 12

instructions: Prepare instant potatoes as directed on box for 12. Mix cream cheese and sour cream into potatoes. Put in 9 x 13 pan and sprinkle top with paprika. Can drizzle a little melted butter on top. Bake at 375° for 45-60 minutes. May also be seasoned with garlic salt and parsley if desired. Dish may be prepared early and stored in refrigerator.

name: Seasoned Potatoes
author: Shelly Dohogne
instructions: Wash unpeeled potatoes and cut into wedges. Place in crock pot. Combine remaining ingredients and brush over potatoes. Cook on high for 2 to 4 hours until tender, stirring frequently to coat mixture over potatoes.

name: Easy Potatoes
author: Sara Hooper

ingredients.name: to 1 stick of margarine or butter

instructions: Fill 9 x 13 glass pan with potatoes, add milk. Slice butter or margarine into pats and lay on top of the potato slices. Sprinkle Lawry's seasoning salt over the potatoes. Bake at 400° until potatoes are done, approximately 1 hour.

name: Potatoes
author: Tina Schlosser
instructions: Wash potatoes and quarter, leave peeling on. Mix soup, oil, and water. Pour over potatoes. Bake 1 hour at 400°. Stir 3 times.

name: Parmesan Baked Potatoes
author: Linda Menz

ingredients.name: medium, red, unpeeled potatoes, cut lengthwise

instructions: Pour butter into 9 x 13 pan. Sprinkle cheese. Place potatoes face down. Bake uncovered at 400° for 40 to 45 minutes.

name: Twice Baked Potatoes
author: Becky Essner
instructions:
Peel potatoes, cut in chunks, and boil until soft enough to mash. Drain. Mix with 3 Tbsp. margarine, salt and pepper to taste, and enough milk to make them just slightly runny. (Just a little more than if you were serving regular mashed potatoes.) Chop onions in small pieces and saute in 2 Tbsp. margarine. Add to potatoes and mix well. Stir in about 2/3 bag of Velveeta. (Use more if you like cheese.) Bake at 350° in 9 x 13 buttered pan for 20 to 30 minutes or until potatoes are bubbly.
This recipe can be made ahead of time and frozen. Thaw before baking.

name: Cheese Potatoes in Foil
author: C. Allen Collier

ingredients.name: large baking potatoes, pared cracked or coarsely ground

instructions: Slice potatoes onto a large piece of foil. Sprinkle with pepper and salt. Crumble bacon over potatoes. Add onion and cheese. Dot with butter. Wrap loosely and seal well with double fold. Cook in 350° oven for about 1 hour or until done, turning occasionally.

name: Cheese Potatoes
author: Tina Blattel

ingredients.name: lb. potatoes, boiled, cooled, peeled and cubed
medium onion, chopped and sauteed in butter

instructions: Mix all ingredients together, except cheese. Add cheese to top of potato mixture. Cover and refrigerate overnight. Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes in 9 x 13 dish with foil covering top. Make this a day ahead of time and bake just before serving.

name: Champion Cheese Potatoes
author: R.G.
instructions: Pierce potatoes with a fork several times. Bake in a preheated 350° oven for 11/2 hours. Cut in half lengthwise and scoop out insides into a medium bowl. Mash with a fork. Add cheese and onion. Mix well. Spoon equal amounts of mashed potato back into the skins. Re- turn to oven and bake 10 minutes.

name: Russian Scalloped Potatoes
author: Sara Hooper

ingredients.name: c. ham, cut into thin strips

instructions:
Simmer the onions in half the butter until soft, but not brown. Add the flour; cook 5 minutes, then add consomme, sour cream, Worcestershire sauce and Tabasco sauce. Continue cooking 10 min- utes longer over low heat. Slice potatoes thin and saute in remaining butter about 5 minutes.
Trim fat from ham and cut ham into strips about 1 x 1/2-inch. Peel the pickles and slice very thin. Mix all ingredients with the onion sauce carefully, using a fork. Place all together in a 9 x 9-inch baking dish. Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese and bake at 350° for about 20 minutes to 1?2 hour. Good with cucumber salad and pumpernickel bread.

name: Scalloped Potatoes
author: Martha J. Hamm
instructions: Cook potatoes for about 10 minutes in boiling salted water. Drain, reserving 1 cup water. Place potatoes in baking dish. Saute onion in 4 Tbsp. of melted butter in a saucepan; blend in flour. Add reserved water and milk. Cook, stirring until thick. Remove from heat; add cheese, salt and pepper to taste. Stir. Pour over potatoes. Bake for 30 minutes at 350°.

name: Scalloped Potatoes
author: Charlotte Hooper
instructions: Cook potatoes, 1/2 c. water and salt for 5 minutes. Drain and pour into well oiled 1 1/2 quart baking dish. Heat milk, butter and cheese. Make a thin paste using the flour and 3 Tbsp. water. Add to milk mix- ture and bring to boil. Bake in 350° oven for 50 minutes.

name: Super Scalloped Taters
author: R.G.

ingredients.name: baking potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced

instructions: Bring milk in a saucepan to boiling over medium-high heat. Add potatoes and butter or margarine. Cover and lower heat to simmer. Cook 15 minutes. Pour potatoes and milk into a greased casserole. Add 1/4 cup of each cheese. Mix well. Sprinkle remaining cheese on top. Bake in a preheated 325° oven 1 hour.

name: Spicy Oven-Fried Potato Wedges
author: S.P.

ingredients.name: baking potatoes, cut into thin wedges

instructions: Preheat oven to 450°. Spray nonstick baking sheet with Pam. Pour oil over potatoes and arrange on baking sheet. Bake 10 minutes. Turn potatoes and bake 10 minutes longer, until lightly browned. Sprinkle with spices and mix well.

name: Potato Casserole
author: Marilyn Friend

ingredients.name: (32 oz.) or 2 (10 oz.) pkg. frozen hash browns
(12 oz.) pkg. grated Cheddar or American cheese

instructions:
Place partially thawed potatoes in a greased casserole dish. Mix next 7 ingredients and pour on top of potatoes. Sprinkle corn flakes and remaining butter on top. Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Variations: You may use 5 cups boiled and cubed potatoes instead of hash browns. Some prefer 1 (8 ounce) carton sour cream instead of two. Others prefer using 1 (8 ounce) package cream cheese in place of sour cream. This is a great potluck dish by adding 1 cup diced ham.

name: Potato Casserole
author: Revella Schlosser
instructions: Boil potatoes, cool and grate. Melt butter, add sour cream, cheese, soup and onion. Add to grated potatoes and mix well. Pour into 9 x 13 inch baking dish that has been greased. Top with buttered crumbs if desired. Bake at 325° for 45 minutes.

name: Potato Casserole
author: Anna Bollinger
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°. Pour 1/2 c. melted margarine into 9 x 12 baking dish. Add 1/2 pkg. of frozen hash browns. Mix soup, sour cream, milk, and green onions in separate bowl. Pour 1/2 mixture over hash browns. Sprinkle 1 c. grated cheese on top. Add remainder of mixture and hash browns on top. Sprinkle remaining cheese on, then cover with crushed corn flakes. Drizzle 2 Tbsp. melted margarine on top. Bake for 45 minutes.

name: Hash Brown Casserole
author: Rebecca Hooper
instructions: Mix all ingredients together and put in a 3 quart oblong baking dish. Bake at 350° for 1 1/4 hours.

name: Spinach-Bacon Casserole
author: Shirley Efting

ingredients.name: c. shredded Provolone or Mozzarella cheese

instructions: Dice bacon; fry and drain. Cook spinach. Beat eggs slightly, then add milk and salt. Stir in spinach, bread crumbs, bacon and half of cheese. Place in 11/2 quart casserole dish. Sprinkle remaining cheese over casserole. Bake at 375° for 30 to 35 minutes.

name: Spinach Casserole
author: Christine Estes
instructions: Lightly cook the spinach and drain. Mix the cream cheese and soup together and add to the spinach in a 9 x 13 baking dish. Also add 1/2 can of Durkee onions, reserving the other 1?2 as topping for the last 5 minutes of baking. Bake for 30 minutes at 350°.

name: Spinach Casserole
author: Jeanne Barbatti

ingredients.name: (10 oz.) can cream of celery soup

instructions: Cook ground beef and drain. Cook rice. Mix all ingredients together, put in casserole dish and top with Mozzarella cheese slices. Bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes.

name: Sweet Potato Casserole
author: Tina Blattel
instructions: Combine above, bake at 300° for 10 minutes.

name: Sweet Potato Casserole Topping
author: Tina Blattel
instructions: Mix and sprinkle over sweet potatoes. Bake again at 350° for 20 minutes.

name: Reba McEntire's Sweet Potato Casserole (Potato Mixture)
author: Helen Kluesner
instructions:
You may substitue 6 fresh medium-size sweet potatoes, boiled and peeled
Preheat oven to 350°. In a large bowl, mash potatoes. Add remaining casserole ingredients and mix well. Pour into buttered 1 quart casserole dish.

name: Reba McEntire's Sweet Potato Casserole (Topping)
author: Helen Kluesner
instructions: Mix topping ingredients thoroughly and sprinkle evenly over potato mixture. Bake for 30 minutes.

name: Pecan Sweet Potatoes
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Cook sweet potatoes in boiling salt water until tender. Peel and cut in half lengthwise. Place in 1 1/2 quart shallow casserole one layer thick. Sprinkle with sugar and pecans. Pour on orange juice, rind and Sherry. Dot with butter. Cover and bake in preheated oven, 350° for Shirley Drury 45 minutes or until juice has cooked into potatoes.

name: Sweet Potatoes and Marshmallows
author: Charlotte Hooper
instructions: Stir in sugar. Pour into casserole. Mash potatoes with butter. dish. Sprinkle on marshmallows. Bake in oven until marshmallows are melted and brown.

name: Old-Fashioned Candied Yams
author: Rebecca Hooper
instructions: Peel and cut yams in quarters. Sprinkle with sugar and nutmeg; add butter. Add vanilla, salt and water. Cover and simmer over medi- um heat until liquid forms a syrup. Remove from heat and serve.

name: Corn Casserole
author: Helen Kluesner
instructions: Melt margarine and add it to the eggs. Mix all ingredients and bake in 350 degrees oven for 50 to 60 minutes.

name: Corn Casserole
author: Donna Scherer

ingredients.name: box Chicken in a Biskit crackers

instructions: Crush crackers and mix with margarine. Combine half of cracker mixture with remaining ingredients in a casserole dish. Top with remaining crackers. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.

name: Corn Casserole
author: Donna Menz, Denise Menz
instructions: Mix all together except cheese and put into 9 x 13 pan. Bake at 350° for 1/2 hour. Can put part of the cheese inside with the corn.

name: Creamed Corn Casserole
author: RB and LM Blankenship
instructions: Bake in 350° oven for 30 minutes. Ramona Bess and Louise Maria's favorite.

name: Canned Green Beans
author: In Memory of Ella I. Schlosser
instructions: Put green beans in prepared jars. Add 1/2 teaspoon salt to a pint jar and 1 teaspoon salt to a quart jar. Fill with water and seal. Place in pressure cooker. Let them come to 10 pounds of pressure for 20 minutes.

name: Green Bean Casserole
author: R.F.

ingredients.name: (10 3/4 oz.) can cream of mushroom soup
(10 3/4 oz.) can cream of celery soup

instructions: Mix all ingredients together except onion rings. Bake at 325° for about 45 minutes, sprinkling onion rings on top for last 15 minutes of cooking time.

name: Green Bean Casserole with Onion Rings
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Mix beans and mushroom soup. Pour into buttered baking dish. Bake 1 hour at 300° until bubbling. Sprinkle onion rings over top of beans and bake 15 minutes.

name: Kelso Copper Pennies
author: Ramona Glastetter
instructions: Cook carrots in salted water about 10 minutes. Drain, put the vegetables in a large bowl. Combine rest of ingredients and pour over vegetables. Let stand several hours or over night. Keeps a long time.

name: Edna Margen's Cool Carrots
author: Revella Schlosser

ingredients.name: medium onion, thinly sliced and separated into large rings

instructions: Cook carrots in boiling salted water for 5 minutes or until crisp tender. Drain. Combine carrots, green pepper and onion in a 13 x 9 x 2 inch pan. Toss until mixed. Combine soup, sugar, oil, vinegar, and mustard; stir until combined. Pour soup mixture over carrot mixture, cover and marinate in refrigerator for 8 hours or overnight.

name: Glazed Carrots
author: Ramona Glastetter
instructions: Wash, pare and cut into sticks, as many as needed. Cook in a small amount of water until tender, about 15 minutes. Add butter and sugar and cook over low heat until the carrots are glazed and shiny.

name: Zesty Carrot Bake
author: Kristie Milam

ingredients.name: lb. carrots, cut into 1/2 inch slices

instructions: On stovetop or microwave oven, cook carrots until tender. Place in a 1 quart baking dish; set aside. In a small bowl combine the next 5 ingredients; mix well. Pour over carrots. Combine bread crumbs and butter; sprinkle on top. Bake uncovered at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes. Sprinkle with cheese. Return to oven for 2 to 3 minutes or until cheese melts.

name: Marinated Carrots
author: Laurie Essner
instructions: Boil carrots until done. Mix all ingredients, except carrots. Let set 1 hour. Pour over the cooked and drained carrots.

name: Fried Green Tomatoes
author: Janet Welter
instructions: Cut tomatoes into 1/4 inch slices. Season with salt and pepper; coat in the corn meal. Heat bacon drippings in a heavy skillet; add tomatoes and fry slowly until brown, turning once.

name: Batter Fried Vegetables
author: Lori Bles
instructions: Combine flour, egg, milk, baking powder, and salt to make bat- ter. Beat until smooth. Cover; let stand at least 15 minutes before using. Cut desired amount of vegetables. Dip the cut pieces into the batter; let surplus drain off. Deep fry at 350° until brown and crisp.

name: Zucchini Rice-a-Roni
author: Marilyn Friend
instructions: Prepare box of chicken Rice-a-Roni. Add the zucchini, carrot, and onion. Mix chicken soup, sour cream, and oleo together for the topping. Add the topping to the rice mixture and bake 35 to 40 minutes at 350° or until veggies are tender.

name: Zucchini Casserole
author: Sister Angela Eichenseer
instructions: Mix all ingredients. Pour into 9 x 9 inch pan. Bake at 350° for 45 minutes or until golden brown and crusty.

name: Squash Patties
author: Helen Menz
instructions: Mix all ingredients together and drop by teaspoon in a little grease or oil, just enough oil in a skillet to brown on one side, then turn over and brown the other side.

name: Baked Squash
author: Marilyn Friend
instructions: Wash squash and cut into small pieces. Cook in salted water until tender. Drain. Mash the squash and add the butter, salt, pepper, and onions. Combine the milk and eggs. Mix well with squash. Put in baking dish. Top with melted butter and cracker crumbs. Bake 20 to 25 minutes.

name: Stove Top BBQ Beans
author: Janet Welter
instructions: Fry bacon until crisp, remove from skillet and crumble. Add onion and green pepper to bacon drippings; fry until soft. Add crumbled bacon, pork 'n beans, brown sugar, BBQ sauce and mustard. Bring to a boil on medium heat; cook 15 minutes, stirring occasionally to keep from sticking.

name: Broccoli and Corn
author: Emma Nichols, Donna Menz

ingredients.name: (12 oz.) can sweet corn with red and green peppers, drained
(10 oz.) frozen chopped broccoli, thawed and drained

instructions: Melt oleo and saute corn and broccoli. Cook until heated and tender, then add seasoning and heat.

name: Broccoli Cheese Casserole
author: Charlotte Hooper
instructions: Melt the margarine and mix with all other ingredients. Pour into 9 x 13 greased baking dish. Bake 1 hour at 350°. Stir about 3 times while baking.

name: Broccoli Rice Casserole
author: Shirley Drury

ingredients.name: (10 3/4 oz.) can cream of chicken soup
can cream of mushroom soup (10 3/4 oz.)

instructions: Cook broccoli until tender. Drain. Saute onions and celery in butter. Add soups, broccoli, rice and cheese. Save some cheese to put on top. Pour into buttered casserole and sprinkle cheese on top. Bake at 350° for about 20 minutes. Use 2 quart casserole dish or a long baking dish.

name: Broccoli Casserole
author: M.E.
instructions: Steam broccoli until it separates. Cook rice according to direc- tions. Mix warm broccoli and rice with remaining ingredients. Put into greased 2 1/2 quart casserole and bake at 350° for 30 minutes.

name: Broccoli Casserole
author: Nancy Weissmueller
instructions: Saute onion in margarine. Add cream of mushroom soup, cream of celery soup, Velveeta, milk, rice and broccoli while still over low heat. Pour heated mixture into casserole dish. Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.

name: Cauliflower Morocco
author: Rebecca Hooper

ingredients.name: garlic, basil, salt and pepper to taste

instructions: Saute mushrooms and onion in butter with juice of 1 lemon. Saute cauliflowerets in butter with garlic, basil, salt and pepper to taste. Mix all ingredients and put in greased casserole. Cover and bake at 350° for 30 minutes.

name: Sour Cream Cucumbers
author: Donna Menz
instructions: In a bowl, combine the cucumbers and onions. Combine remaining ingredients and pour over cucumbers. Mix well. Chill.

name: Asparagus Casserole
author: Annita Layton
instructions: Drain asparagus, reserve 1/2 cup of juice. Add asparagus to 1/2 cup milk and soup and heat. Butter 2 quart casserole and put a layer of cracker crumbs on the bottom. Add or layer 1 can asparagus, 1 1/2 eggs (sliced), half of cheese, half of soup, and a little salt and pepper. Repeat layer of asparagus, eggs, cheese, and soup. Put cracker crumbs on top. Dot with butter. Bake uncovered in 350° oven for 30 minutes.

name: Grilled Asparagus (No Cholesterol)
author: Sister Sylvia Birke
instructions:
Wash asparagus; snap off the woody ends. Brush well with olive oil. Sprinkle with garlic and rosemary. Move the spears to distribute the herbs evenly. Sprinkle with salt and pepper. Let asparagus marinate for 10 to 15 minutes. Place spears over a charcoal or gas grill fire. Let cook about 3 minutes. Turn asparagus. Cook for and equal length of time. Remove from fire. The recipe serves four, unless you really like asparagus. Then it serves two.
Approximate nutrition information per serving: 57 calories; 3.5g fat (50 percent calories from fat); no cholesterol; 3g protein; 5g carbo- hydrate; 2.5g fiber; 2 mg sodium.

name: Fried Apples
author: Charlotte Hooper
instructions: Wash, quarter and core apples. Cut each slice in half again. Place in large skillet with water. Cook until soft and most of water is gone. Add butter and sugar. Turn to medium heat. Cook until apples and sugar mixture become like caramel. Serve hot.

name: Beanie Weenies
author: Zachary Estes

ingredients.name: small can Showboat pork 'n beans, drained

instructions: Slice hot dogs and add all other ingredients in saucepan. Cook slowly stirring often until hot dogs are done.

name: Cabbage and Celery Casserole
author: Annita Layton
instructions: Cook vegetables in salted waster until crunchy. Drain and mix vegetables. Butter casserole. Layer half of the vegetables, half the soup (may need more), half the cheese and sprinkle with salt and pep- per. Repeat with another layer of vegetables, soup, seasoning, and cheese. Top with buttered bread crumbs (French fried onion may be used for topping). Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.

name: Josephine Messmer's Pickled Beets
author: Louise Alderman
instructions: Drain beets. Heat to boiling, everything but beets. Remove from heat and add beets.

name: Beets
author: Hazel Leubbers
instructions: Boil beets in their jackets. When tender, peel beets. Mix remain- ing ingredients together. Slice the beets into the mixture and bring to a boil for about 10 minutes. Put in jars and seal.

name: Kraut
author: Martha Hamm
instructions: Bring to a boil and set aside to cool. Pack shredded cabbage tight in jars. Pour liquid over cabbage, seal.

name: Kraut Dumplings
author: Ginny Robert
instructions: Empty sauerkraut into a 3 quart sauce pan. Heat to boiling point. Meanwhile saute onions in margarine until done. Mix Bisquick and milk until a soft dough forms. Drop by teaspoons into boiling kraut. Cook uncovered over low heat 10 minutes. Cover and cook 10 minutes more. Carefully remove with large spoon to platter and top dumplings with onions. Serve with roast pork.

name: Homemade Bread
author: St. Augustine Cafeteria
instructions: Mix yeast, 2 cups warm water and 2 tablespoons of sugar; set aside. Mix dry milk, salt, 1 cup sugar and 3 of the flour together. Add water, yeast mixture and shortening. Mix well. Then add rest of the flour. Knead and let rise until double. Makes about 9 (2 pound) loaves. Bake at 400° for 15 minutes, 350° for 45 minutes.

name: Homemade Bread
author: Janet Welter
instructions: Dissolve yeast in warm water in large bowl. Let set for 5 minutes. Add sugar, shortening, egg, salt and 1/2 of the flour. Beat at low speed with mixer until smooth. Gradually stir, by hand, enough remaining flour to make a soft dough. Place dough in a well greased bowl, turning to grease top. Place covered in a warm place and let rise for 1 hour or until double in size. Punch down, turn out on a lightly floured board and knead 4 or 5 times. Shape into a loaf, place in a greased bread pan. Cover and let rise. Bake 20 minutes at 350° or until bread has a hollow sound when tapped. Remove from pan and cool on a wire rack.

name: Coffee Can Bread
author: Charlotte Hooper
instructions: Mix together in a bowl, yeast, warm water and 1 Tbsp. sugar. Place the bowl in a sink of warm water for 15 minutes or until mixture begins to bubble. Stir in remaining sugar, salt, oil and milk. Using an electric mixer, fold in 3 cups of flour. Mix well after each cup. Remain- ing flour can be folded in with a wooden spoon until mixture is no longer sticky. The dough will be heavy. Place dough on floured board. Divide dough in half. Spray coffee cans and lids with non-stick cooking spray. Put half of dough in each can and put the lids on. At this point, the cans can be placed in the freezer. For baking, set can in a warm place until the lid pops off. Take the lids off and bake at 350° for 45 minutes (or 325° convection for 30 minutes) or until golden brown and loaf slides out of can easily.

name: Freezer Bread Dough
author: Donna Stamp
instructions: In large mixing bowl, combine 2 1/2 c. of the flour and the yeast. In saucepan, heat together the milk, butter or margarine, sugar, and salt just till warm (115° to 120°), stirring constantly till butter or margarine almost melts. Add liquid to dry ingredients in mixing bowl along with eggs. Beat at low speed of electric mixer for 2 minutes, scraping sides of bowl constantly. Beat 3 minutes at high speed. Stir in as much of the remaining flour as you can mix in with a spoon, Turn out onto a lightly floured pastry sheet. Knead in enough of the remaining flour to make a stiff dough that is smooth and elastic (6 to 8 minutes total). Divide dough into thirds. Shape each of two portions into loaves. Store in container with a double thickness of waxed paper between. Divide remaining dough into 16 portions. Shape each into a smooth ball. Arrange the 16 balls 1 inch apart in a cold cut keeper. Apply seal; freeze firm. To conserve on freezer space, transfer frozen ball to smaller container. When ready to bake, let dough rise until double in size. Bake at 375° until done. You can place dough in refrigerator to thaw overnight.

name: Irish Soda Bread
author: Fr. Oliver Clavin
instructions:
Put all dry ingredients into bowl and mix. Rub in the margarine with fingertips. Make a well in the center and pour in the buttermilk. Mix well and knead lightly. Roll into a ball, using a little flour. 
Place dough in a deep round floured 8 inch cake pan or iron skil- let (a loaf pan can be used). With a floured knife, make a deep cross across the top of the bread. Bake in 400° oven for 40 minutes. Remove the bread from the pan immediately and wrap in a towel. Stand it on its edge to cool.
Delivious plain or toasted, with butter and orange marmalade.

name: Ice Box Yeast Rolls
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Dissolve yeast in lukewarm water. Let stand. Mix together sug- ar, oil, salt and eggs. Add yeast mixture and milk. Add flour until dough is thick. Knead well. Place in oiled bowl and cover with plastic wrap. Put in refrigerator. Remove dough 3 hours before baking. Shape into rolls and place into greased pans. Let rise until double. When dough is ready to bake, top with well drained fruit or pie filling. Sprinkle the crumb mixture on rest. Bake at 350° until done.

name: Ice Box Yeast Rolls (Crumb Mixture)
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Mix all ingredients together to make crumbs.

name: Yeast Bread
author: Shirley Drury
instructions:
Lukewarm liquid could be milk, water or potato water.
Mix water, sugar, salt and yeast together in large mixing bowl. Stir until yeast is well dissolved. Add oil and mix. Then add flour in two additions using the amount necessary to make dough easy to han- dle. Knead the dough. Place in greased bowl, turning once to bring greased side up. Cover with damp cloth and let rise until doubled. Shape into loaves and place in greased bread loaf pans. Let rise again and bake at 425° for 25 to 30 minutes.
This basic dough can be used for nut, date or raisin bread.

name: Notre Dame High School Bread Dough
author: Charlotte Hooper
instructions:
Mix yeast and sugar with water. Stir until dissolved. Add butter, salt and dry milk. Stir well. Then add flour, beating after each cup. When mixed, knead dough for 3 minutes. Divide dough into 3 parts. Shape into French style loaves and place on greased cookie sheets. Let rise until double in size. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Great for spaghetti dinner or French style sandwiches.

name: Mexican Dip
author: Anita Essner
instructions: Spread refried beans on platter. Mix taco seasoning and sour cream. Spread on beans. Put jalepeno peppers on next layer, then salsa on next layer. Top with shredded cheese. Serve cold with corn chips or tortilla chips.

name: Lime Pickles
author: Hazel Luebbers
instructions: Slice the pickles and cover with lime and water. Let the pickles soak in the solution for 24 hours. Rinse solution from vegetables. Let them stand in clean cold water for 3 more hours. Drain. Mix all other ingredients, add pickles and let sit overnight. Bring mixture to a boil for 35 minutes. Can add alum, if desired. Put in jars and seal.

name: Broccoli Cauliflower Salad
author: Denise Menz, Donna Menz
instructions: Pour over cut up vegetables. Refrigerate.

name: Incredible Egg Macaroni Salad
author: Anna Bollinger

ingredients.name: (17 1/4 oz.) pkg. Macaroni and Cheese dinner

instructions: Prepare macaroni and cheese dinner as directed on the package. Add peas, tomatoes, salad dressing, celery, onion and seasonings. Chop 5 eggs, add to dinner mixture. Mix lightly. Chill. Stir in additional salad dressing before serving, if desired. Garnish with remaining egg, sliced

name: Zesty Saltine Meatloaf
author: S.P.

ingredients.name: lb. ground beef, turkey or deer

instructions: In large mixing bowl, combine ground beef, turkey or deer with milk, 1⁄2 cup cracker crumbs, onion, Worcestershire sauce, catsup, egg, salt and pepper; blend thoroughly. Place mixture on a large piece of waxed paper. Cover with another piece of waxed paper and roll out to rectangle about 9 x 15 inches. Remove top sheet of paper. Combine remaining cracker crumbs and cheese. Sprinkle over meat mixture. Roll up. Place in pan and bake at 350° for 1 hour and 15 minutes.

name: Enchiladas Casserole
author: Ramona Bess Blankenship
instructions: Brown meat and add onion, garlic cloves, vinegar, tomato juice, chili powder, salt and pepper. Mix well and bring to a boil. Reduce heat and cook for 20 minutes. Stir in flour and cook over low heat until thick. Remove and put in 2 quart dish. Put a layer of crackers, meat, cheese, etc. Bake at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes.

name: Homemade Pizza Dough
author: Becky Essner
instructions: Dissolve yeast in warm water. Let this sit for 5 minutes. Add salt, sugar, oil and flour. Mix well with large spoon until dough is smooth. Divide in half and roll out with rolling pin. Place on greased pizza pans.

name: Homemade Pizza Sauce
author: Becky Essner
instructions: Mix with tomato sauce, oregano, garlic salt, and Parmesan cheese to taste. (Approximately 1/8 teaspoon each of oregano and garlic salt. Approximately 1/4 cup Parmesan cheese.) Or, you can use purchased spaghetti sauce of your choice. Spread on dough.

name: Homemade Pizza Meat
author: Becky Essner
instructions: Brown meat and drain. Again, add the seasonings to taste and cook over low heat for about 2 to 3 more minutes. Sprinkle meat over sauce. May also add pepperoni slices, slivers of onion, sliced green peppers, mushrooms, olives and other toppings. Top with cheese. Bake in preheated 425° oven for 20 to 25 minutes.

name: Spicy Bean and Beef Pie
author: Kristie Milam

ingredients.name: (11 1⁄2 oz.) can condensed bean with bacon soup, undiluted
(16 oz.) jar thick and chunky picante sauce, divided
(16 oz.) can kidney beans, rinsed and drained
(16 oz.) can black beans, rinsed and drained
Pastry for double crust pie (10 inches)
(2 1/4 oz.) can sliced ripe olives, drained

instructions: In a skillet, cook beef and garlic until beef is browned; drain. In a large bowl, combine soup, 1 cup picante sauce, cornstarch, parsley, paprika, salt and pepper. Mix well. Fold in beans, 1 1/4 cup of cheese, 1/2 cup onion and the beef mixture. Line pie plate with bottom pastry; fill with bean mixture. Top with remaining pastry; seal and flute edges. Cut slits in the top crust. Bake at 425° for 30 to 35 min- utes, or until lightly browned. Let stand for 5 minutes before cutting. Garnish with sour cream, olives and remaining picante sauce, cheese and onions.

name: Chicken Dinner with Sour-Cream Gravy
author: Annita Layton

ingredients.name: (2 1/2 to 3 lb.) broiler fryer, cut up

instructions: In 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat, in hot salad oil, cook chicken pieces until browned on all sides. Sprinkle chicken with salt and pepper. Add water and heat to boiling. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 20 minutes. Add celery and carrot slices. Cover and simmer 15 minutes more or until chicken and vegetables are fork- tender, stirring occasionally. Meanwhile, prepare rice as label directs. Spoon onto warm platter and keep warm. With slotted spoon, arrange chicken and vegetables on cooked rice. To prepare sour-cream gravy, spoon fat from drippings remaining in skillet. Into drippings, stir sour cream. Over medium heat, heat through, scraping any bits from bottom of pan. Do not allow mixture to boil or sour cream will curdle. Pour sour cream gravy over chicken and vegetables and serve immediately.

name: Fried Sweet Potatoes
author: Charlotte Hooper

ingredients.name: sweet potatoes, peeled and cut into eighths

instructions: Boil potatoes in water until done. Drain well. Melt butter in skillet. Pour in potatoes and top with sugar. Cook until syrup like and golden brown.

name: Homestyle Tuna Pot Pie
author: Anna Bollinger

ingredients.name: pkg. refrigerated all-ready pie crusts (2 crusts)
(12 1⁄2 oz.) can chunk light tuna, drained
(10 oz.) pkg. frozen peas and carrots
(10 3/4 oz.) can cream of potato or mushroom soup
tsp. poultry seasoning or dried thyme

instructions: Line 9 inch pie pan with 1 crust; set aside. Combine remaining ingredients. Add salt and pepper to taste. Pour filling in pie pan. Top with second crust. Seal and crimp edges. Slit top of crust to vent and bake at 375° for 45 to 50 minutes or until golden brown.

name: White Bread
author: In Memory of Ella I. Schlosser
instructions: Soften yeast in warm water. Combine sugar, salt, shortening and water. Combine nonfat milk solids and 2 cups flour. Add to the above mixture. Add softened yeast. Beat until smooth. Add remaining flour gradually to make a soft dough. Turn out on a lightly floured pastry cloth and knead until surface of dough is smooth. Place in a greased bowl. Turn once to bring greased side up. Cover. Let rise in a warm place until double in bulk, about 45 minutes. Turn out on a pastry cloth. Knead. Shape into a loaf pan 8 1/2 x 5 x 2 1/2 inches. Cover and let rise until double in bulk, about 30 minutes. Bake in a moderate oven (350°) for about 40 minutes.

name: Hot Rolls for Notre Dame High School
author: Juanita Dannenmueller
instructions: Mix well and add as much flour that is needed so dough is not sticky and comes away from sides of mixer. Place in large dishpan. Let rise until double. Shape into rolls and let rise until double again. Bake in 8x10 pans at 350° for 30 minutes.

name: Hot Rolls
author: Rita Jansen
instructions: Mix together, yeast, 1 teaspoon sugar and 1/4 cup warm water and let stand. Heat until lukewarm, 1/2 cup sugar, buttermilk, margarine and salt. Then, add mashed potatoes, eggs, and 1 quart water to the milk and yeast mixtures. Add enough flour until dough is satiny. Place in well greased bowl and let rise until double. Then shape into rolls and let rise until double. Bake at 350° until done.

name: Southern Corn Bread
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Mix all ingredients together and place in cornsticks or muffin pan. In 450° oven, bake for 10 to 15 minutes for corn sticks or muffins; 20 to 25 minutes for corn bread. Makes 12 muffins, corn sticks, or pieces.

name: Magic Biscuits
author: Sara Hooper
instructions:
Mix dry ingredients; cut in shortening. Add buttermilk and yeast that has been dissolved in hot water. Put in oiled bowl in refrigerator. You don't have to wait for rising. Roll out and cut with biscuit cutter. Bake at 425° for 10 minutes.
Notes: These biscuits taste even better the second day. Use only the amount needed. Batter will keep up to a week in the refrigerator.

name: Biscuits
author: Donna Menz
instructions: Mix flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt and sugar in a mix- ing bowl. Cut in the oleo until mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Add buttermilk. Mix quickly to make a soft dough. Turn out onto a lightly floured surface. Knead a few times to make a soft dough, don't over knead or the biscuits will turn hard and dry. Roll out a 6 x 6 square and place on an ungreased baking sheet. With a knife, cut dough into 12 even portions. Do not separate. Bake at 400° until golden about 15 minutes. Serve piping hot with butter or honey.

name: Red Lobster Inspired Garlic Cheese Biscuits
author: Brian Hulshof
instructions:
(Note: You may use all purpose (regular) flour, however biscuits will not rise as much and have a denser texture. Flavors should be about identical. Can substitute 3 packets of Sweet and Low for the sugar. Original recipe does not say, but I would think you will want to shred the cheese.)
In a 1 1⁄2 quart mixing bowl, combine the milk, mayo, sugar, and flour. Beat on high speed with electric mixer for almost a minute, until smooth and completely combined. Using scraper streak the dough with the cheese. Batter should not be thin enough to pour, if necessary add only enough additional flour so batter will 'drop' from spoon. Drop batter into 10 paper lined muffin tins or a greater number of tiny muffin cups. Muffins tend to triple in size when baked. Fill lightly. Melt butter, mix in garlic and brush on top of dough after they are baked. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes or until golden. Cool in pan or rack and hot. for 30 minutes. These definitely should be served freshly baked and hot

name: Red Lobster Biscuits
author: Don and Clara Essner Family, Rachael schlosser
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°. Combine the Bisquick, milk and Cheddar cheese together with a wooden spoon until soft dough forms. Beat vigorously for 30 seconds. Drop dough by heaping tablespoons into an ungreased cookie sheet. Bake 8 to 10 minutes until golden brown. Combine melted butter or margarine with the garlic powder and brush it over the warm biscuits before removing them from the cookie sheet. Serve warm.

name: Golden Potato Rolls
author: Donna Essner
instructions:
Dissolve yeast in water, set aside. In a sauce pan, combine milk, margarine and potatoes. Cook over low heat just until margarine is melted. Remove from heat. In a large bowl mix potato mixture, sugar, salt and 2 c. four. Add yeast mixture and eggs, mix well. Cover loosely and allow to stand for 2 hours.
After 2 hours, stir in enough of the remaining flour to make a soft dough. Knead until smooth and elastic, about 6 minutes. Place in a bowl sprayed with Pam and spray top of dough with Pam. Cover and let rise until double, about 1 hour.
Punch dough down and divide into thirds. Roll out each portion into a 12 inch circle. Cut into 12 pie shape wedges. Beginning at wide end, roll up. Place rolls on greased cookie sheets and let rise 30 minutes, or until doubled in size. Bake at 250° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Can be used for coffee cakes. Mix and divide into thirds as above. Roll out until about 1/2 inch thick, spread a fruit glaze over dough and roll up in jelly roll fashion. Place in a 9 inch pie plate with seam down, in a circle. Pinch edges together. Let rise until double in size. Bake at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes. Let cool and then frost with icing.

name: Piping Hot Potato Rolls
author: Annita Layton
instructions: Combine one cup of water with yeast; set aside. In large bowl, combine remaining water with shortening, sugar, salt, eggs, baking powder, potatoes and 3 cups of the flour. Add dissolved yeast to mixture. All ingredients should be at lukewarm temperature. Let stand in warm place for 30 minutes. When light, work in enough of the remaining flour so dough may be handled and kneaded. The more you knead the dough, the finer and nicer the texture of rolls. Cover and set in warm place for about 2 hours. Punch down and let rise again. Punch down again and form into rolls or desired shape (crescents). Allow to rise again for about 15 minutes. Put into a cold oven and turn temperature to 400°. Bake for approximately 25 minutes.

name: Butterhorn Rolls
author: Kay Stull
instructions: Break the yeast in warm water. Stir until dissolved. Beat the eggs and add sugar, salt, milk, butter and flour. Mix all together and let rise until double in bulk. Then divide into two parts. Roll to 1/4 inch thickness. Spread with melted butter and cut each piece in 16 wedges. Roll beginning at large end. Place in greased pan, two inches apart. Let rise until light. Bake in 400° oven for about 15 minutes.

name: Swedish Tea Ring
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Scald milk and stir in sugar, salt and fat. Cool to lukewarm. Put warm water in mixing bowl and stir in yeast until dissolved. Add to the lukewarm milk the eggs and about half of the flour. Beat until smooth. Add remaining flour and beat until dough leaves sides of bowl. Turn out on lightly floured cutting board and knead until dough is satiny, springy and smooth. Return to bowl, cover and let rise to double in warm place. Punch down and turn out on lightly floured board. Shape according to desired type. Let rise. Roll dough into oblong 9 x 18 inch shape. Spread with the raisin-cherry mixture. Roll up tightly, beginning at wide side. Seal well by pinching edges of roll together. Then, place sealed edge down in ring on lightly greased baking sheets (size 17 by 14). Join ends of ring, seal. With scissors, make cuts 2/3 of the way through the ring at inch intervals. Turn each section on its side. Let rise and bake in moderate oven at 375° for 12 to 15 minutes until golden brown. Frost while warm and decorate with nuts and cherries.

name: Swedish Tea Ring (Raisin-Cherry Mixture)
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Mix all ingredients together.

name: Basic Sweet Dough
author: Ginny Robert
instructions: Scald milk and cool to lukewarm. Add yeast, 1 cup of sugar and 2 cups of flour. (This is your sponge.) Let rise 30 minutes. In large bowl sift in rest of flour, salt and sugar. With fingertips work butter into dry ingredients. Add egg yolk and sponge. Stir, then work with hands until quite thick. Knead dough on board, sprinkled with flour until smooth (you may have to add flour). Cover and let rise 1 to 1 1/2 hour. Punch down and knead again for a few minutes. Cover and let rise 30 minutes.

name: Extra Good Cinnamon Rolls
author: Shelly Dohogne

ingredients.name: c. flour (more or less to make soft dough)

instructions: Dissolve yeast and sugar in 21/2 c. water. Let stand a while. Add 2 c. water, salt, sugar, eggs and flour. Beat, let stand until it bubbles. Add shortening and flour until soft dough is achieved. Let rise until double. Roll out and spread with butter and 1?2 of a 1 pound box of brown sugar and 4 tsp. cinnamon. Roll up dough and cut into rolls. Place in pan. Let rise until light. Bake at 375° for about 20 minutes. Drizzle warm rolls with a glaze made from powdered sugar and milk.

name: Cinnamon Rolls
author: In Memory of Celena Blattel
instructions: Combine, yeast, water and 2 teaspoon sugar. Stir and let stand for 10 minutes. Then add milk, shortening, 1/2 cup sugar and salt. Let mixture cool until lukewarm. Then, add eggs and 2 cups flour. Beat with spoon to make batter. Add remaining flour a little at a time. Knead it like bread. Put in bowl. Let rise to more than double. Roll dough out to 1/2 inch thick. Spread melted butter over dough. Sprinkle with sugar, cinnamon and nut mixture. Roll like a jelly roll and cut in 1 inch thick slices. Put in greased pan and let rise until doubled. Bake at 375° until done.

name: Sweet Rolls
author: Charlotte Hooper
instructions: Dissolve yeast in lukewarm water. Heat milk and shortening until lukewarm. Beat eggs and add sugar and salt to this. Pour in milk and shortening. Add flour to make a thick batter like cake. Add the yeast mixture. Add more flour until smooth and satiny. Let rise for 2 hours. Roll out on floured board, about 1/4 inch thick. Melt 1 1/4 stick margarine and pour over dough. Then sprinkle sugar and cinna- mon over the dough. Roll like a jelly roll. Slice into rolls about 1/4 inch thick and place on greased pan. Let rise for 1 hour. Bake in 400° to 425° oven for around 10 to 12 minutes. Top with icing.

name: Sweet Rolls (Icing)
author: Charlotte Hooper
instructions: Mix Crisco and dry cake mix. Add powdered sugar, water and flavoring. Mix well until smooth.

name: Cinnamon Twists
author: In Memory of Anna Diebold
instructions: Heat cream to lukewarm. Add sugar, soda, and salt. Crumble yeast into mixture. Stir well. Add eggs, shortening, and flour. Fold until smooth. Roll in oblong pan. Cut. Twist. Let rise about 1 hour. Bake at 375°.

name: German Twists
author: In Memory of Helen T. Schlosser

ingredients.name: Granulated sugar to roll twist in

instructions: Dissolve yeast in warm water. Combine boiling water and short- ening, blend well. Add sugar and salt. Stir until lukewarm. Blend in yeast, milk and eggs. Gradually stir in enough flour to make a soft dough. Turn onto lightly floured board. Knead until smooth and satiny (about 7 minutes). Place in lightly greased bowl, turnover to grease top. Cover. Let rise in a warm place until doubled, about 1 and 1 1/2 hours. Turn dough onto floured surface. Roll to 1/2 inch thickness. Cut into 8 x 11/2 inch strips. Fold in half, cross ends of stick over each other to form twist. Pinch to secure ends well. Cover, let rise 30 minutes. Fry in deep fat. Drain on paper towel. Roll in sugar.

name: Caramel Rolls
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Ingredients should be to warm yeast temperature. Dissolve yeast in water. Add milk, lump butter, sugar, egg and salt. Add 1 1/2 cup flour and mix well. Then, add 1 3/4 cup flour and mix by hand until dough is satiny. Let rise for 30 minutes. Then mix brown sugar, butter, corn syrup and cinnamon together. Pour in 9 x 13 pan. Drop dough by teaspoon into caramel mixture. Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate over night. Bake at 350° for 15 minutes.

name: Butter Quick Coffee Cake
author: Annita Layton
instructions: Sift flour, sugar, baking powder and salt into bowl. Add butter, egg and milk. Beat hard for 2 minutes. Pour into large oblong pan that has been greased and floured. Sprinkle with mixture of 1/4 cup soft butter, 1/4 cup flour, brown sugar, coconut or chopped nuts, and cinnamon (Mix with pastry blender or fork). Bake at 350° for 35-45 minutes.

name: Sharen's Coffee Cake
author: Maris

ingredients.name: 21 oz.) can cherry pie filling Pam

instructions: Preheat oven to 375°. Spray two 9 inch round cake pans with Pam. Cream butter and sugar. Beat in eggs until mixture is very light and fluffy. Add extract. Combine flour and soda. Add to creamed mixture alternately with sour cream. Divide batter evenly in pans, spreading fruit filling on top. Sprinkle streusel topping over pie filling. Bake 25 to 35 minutes until cake tests done.

name: Sharen's Coffee Cake (Streusel Topping)
author: Maris
instructions: Combine flour, sugar and cinnamon; cut in butter until crumbly.

name: French Coffee Lace (Dough Mixture)
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Dissolve yeast in lukewarm water. Let stand. Beat eggs and sug- ar together. Add milk, salt and oil to the egg mixture. Add the yeast mixture and flour to make a soft dough. Knead the dough. Place in greased bowl and let rise until double. Punch down and let rise again. Roll out dough into rectangle 14 x 8 inch. Place on greased heavy baking sheet. Spread fruit filling down center of dough covering space about 3 inches wide. At each side of filling, make cuts 2 inches apart and 2 inches long into dough. This makes 7 strips on each side. Take a strip on each side and cross them at center of the filling. Pull strips down, keeping ends inside. Continue to lace opposite strips, tucking last ends underneath. Cover with damp cloth and let rise until double. Bake until golden brown. Frost with favorite icing.

name: French Coffee Lace (Filling Mixture)
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Mix all ingredients and let boil for one minute. Let cool.

name: Monkey Bread
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Cut each biscuit in fourths. Melt the margarine. Combine cinna- mon and sugar together in small bowl. Drop biscuits into the melted margarine and roll in cinnamon-sugar mixture. Place in greased glass pie pan and bake at 350° for 20 minutes or until done.

name: Monkey Bread
author: Ruth Schlosser
instructions:
Cut biscuits into fourths. Roll in sugar and cinnamon mixture. (I use plastic bag to shake them in.) Place in ungreased Bundt pan. Bring to a boil, the butter and brown sugar. Add a little water to make syrup. Add remains of sugar and cinnamon mixture to syrup. Pour syrup over biscuits. Bake at 350° for 40 to 45 minutes.
Note: You might want to place a piece of foil over pan after 15 minutes so it does not burn. Let cool 10 minutes. Turn over on plate.
Great for breakfast while still warm. I have sprinkled nuts in pan along with biscuits.

name: Soft Pretzels
author: Anna Rose Bles
instructions: Measure warm water in large mixing bowl. Sprinkle on yeast and stir until it looks soft. Add salt, sugar, and flour. Mix and knead dough. Roll and twist into letters, numerals, snakes, etc. Grease cookie sheets. Brush pretzels with beaten eggs and sprinkle with salt. Bake at 425° for 12 to 15 minutes.

name: Glazed Potato Doughnut
author: In Memory of Aunt Bert Dumey
instructions: Dissolve yeast in warm water. Combine milk, shortening, sugar and salt. Cool until lukewarm. Stir in yeast, potatoes and eggs. Gradually add enough flour to make soft dough. Turn onto floured surface; knead until smooth and satiny. Place in lightly greased bowl; turn over to grease top. Cover. Let rise in a warm place until doubled, 1 and 1/2 hours. Roll out to 1?2 inch thickness, cut with donut cutter. Cover; let rise until doubled (about 30 minutes). Meanwhile, stir confec- tioners sugar, water and vanilla together. Fry donuts in deep hot fat (375°). Drain on absorbent paper towel. Drop hot donuts in glaze.

name: Small Donuts
author: In Memory of Anna Diebold
instructions: Heat milk and sugar to boiling. Add 2 cups flour. Let cool. Add eggs, a little salt, water and yeast. Add 2 cups more flour. Mix and ut in ice box. Keep in ice box until used. Cut and fry or use big spoon and drop in hot grease.

name: Donuts
author: Janet Welter
instructions: Dissolve yeast in warm water. Add sugar, shortening, salt, egg and 2 cups of flour. Mix with mixer until smooth. Add the other 2 cups of flour and mix by hand. Cover and let rise, in a warm place, until double in size. Punch down, roll out on lightly floured board and cut into donuts. Place on a cooke sheet, cover and let rise again. Deep fry in shortening at 375°. Drain on paper towels.

yield.name: Bring the water and sugar to a boil. Take off burner and stir in the powdered sugar (sift in). Dip fried donuts. Drain on a wire rack.

name: Ramona's Drop Doughnuts
author: Ramona Glastetter
instructions: Cream sugar and eggs, add other ingredients. Drop from a teaspoon in hot lard or Crisco until brown.

name: Ramona's Drop Doughnuts (Glaze)
author: Ramona Glastetter
instructions: Mix well, put in small bowl. Roll drop doughnuts in glaze. Put on wax paper to drain and glaze to dry.

name: Doughnuts
author: In Memory of Bert Dumey
instructions: Soften yeast in water. Scald milk and add sugar and salt. Cool to lukewarm, add flour to make a batter. Mix well. Add softened yeast, eggs and nutmeg. Beat well. Add enough flour to make a soft dough. Place in greased bowl and let rise until double in size. Punch down dough. Roll to 1/2 inch thick and cut with doughnut cutter. Place on towel and let rise until double. Fry in hot oil until golden brown. Dip in icing or powdered sugar.

name: French Breakfast Puffs
author: Annita Layton
instructions: Grease bottom of muffin cups. Mix shortening, 1/2 cup sugar and egg thoroughly. Measure flour by dip-level-pour method. Blend flour, baking powder, salt and nutmeg. Stir in alternately with milk. Fill muffin cups 2/3 full. Bake at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes. Immediately roll in the melted butter, then in sugar and cinnamon.

name: Night-Before French Toast Casserole
author: Shari Landewe

ingredients.name: loaf of French bread or Texas toast

instructions: Grease well a 13 x 9 inch baking dish. Cut bread into 1 inch wide slices. Arrange slices in 1 layer, in bottom of pan. Beat eggs, milk, sugar, salt and vanilla in large bowl. When thoroughly mixed, pour over bread in pan. Bread will float on top of liquid. Cut each pat of butter into 4 pieces. Dot each piece of bread with a piece of butter. Sprinkle with cinnamon. Cover. Refrigerate overnight, or up to 36 hours. Place dish, uncovered, in cold oven. Turn oven temperature to 350° (325° if glass dish) and bake for 45 to 50 minutes or until bread is puffy and light brown. Remove from oven. Allow to set for 5 minutes. Bread will rise to top with a layer of custard on the bottom, similar to a bread pudding. Serve with syrup, sliced strawberries and dust with powdered sugar.

name: My Apricot Muffins
author: Ramona Glastetter
instructions: Mix together flour, baking powder, sugar and salt. Add apricots to flour mixture. Combine egg, milk and oleo. Add to flour, beating only enough to dampen all flour. Bake in greased muffin pans in 425° oven for 25 minutes, or until done. Makes 12 muffins. For plain muf- fins, omit fruit.

name: Refrigerator Muffins
author: Paula Castleman
instructions: Mix together in large bowl, everything except eggs, oil and buttermilk. Then add the eggs, oil and buttermilk. Grease muffin tins or use paper liners. Bake 15 to 20 minutes at 375°. Mixture may be kept in refrigerator for a few weeks.

name: Raisin Bread
author: In Memory of Ella I. Schlosser
instructions: Pour the boiling water over the raisins, oleo and soda. Cool. Add eggs, sugar, cinnamon, salt, nuts and flour. Bake in 3 pound coffee cans, that are greased good to the top. Bake for 1 hour at 350°.

name: Banana Muffins
author: Shelly Dohogne
instructions: Sift flour, baking powder, baking soda and salt together. Cream the brown sugar and margarine with the egg. Mash the bananas with the water and the vanilla. Add the banana and egg mixtures to the dry ingredients. Stir only enough to moisten. Add nuts. Spoon batter into greased muffin pan. Bake at 350° for 25 minutes.

name: Banana Bread
author: Juanita Dannenmueller
instructions: Cream the butter and sugar. Add eggs and vanilla and beat. Add ripe bananas. Mix in sifted dry ingredients. Bake at 350° for 1 hour.

name: Banana Bread
author: Ramona Bess
instructions: Add all ingredients to large mixing bowl. Beat well. Then, pour mixture into well greased loaf pans. Bake at 350° for 40 to 45 minutes.

name: Banana Nut Bread
author: Joan Drury
instructions: Beat shortening and sugar together. Add eggs and beat well. Sift together flour, baking powder, soda and salt. Then add 1/2 bananas and 1/2 flour mixture. Mix well. Add remaining banana and flour mixtures. Mix well. Add chopped walnuts and place in well greased and floured loaf pan. Bake at 350° for 40 to 45 minutes. Remove from pan and cool on rack.

name: Nut Bread
author: Anna Rose Bles

ingredients.name: tsp. baking soda, dissolved in milk

instructions: Mix together well. Bake 1 hour in slow oven (325°).

name: Nut Bread
author: Dale Schlosser

ingredients.name: c. half black walnuts and pecans
c. Gold Medal flour *Do not use self rising flour

instructions: Heat oven to 350°. Grease 9 x 5 x 3 inch loaf pan. Combine bak- ing mix, sugar, flour, egg and milk. Beat vigorously for 30 seconds. Stir in nuts. Pour into pan. Bake for 1 hour or until done.

name: Pumpkin Bread
author: S.B.G.
instructions: Mix dry ingredients together. In separate bowl, blend eggs, sugar, pumpkin, vegetable shortening and vanilla together. To the dry ingredients work in pumpkin mixture, a small amount at a time, and blend well. Put in greased and floured 3 pound coffee cans and bake at 350 degrees for 1 hour. Test to see if done, as it may need 5 or 10 more minutes baking.

name: Zucchini Bread
author: Lorena Essner
instructions: Beat eggs until light and foamy. Add oil, sugar, zucchini, and vanilla. Mix lightly, but well. Add flour, salt, cinnamon, and baking powder, sifted together. Mix until blended. Divide batter into two well greased 9x5x2 loaf pans. Bake at 325° for 1 hour or until loaf tests done. Raisins and nuts may be added if desired.

name: Sharen's Zucchini Bread
author: Ramona Glastetter
instructions: In a large mixing bowl, combine flour, sugar, cinnamon, soda, baking powder, oil, vanilla and eggs. Beat at medium speed until well mixed. Stir in zucchini, raisins and nuts. Pour into greased 13x9x2 inch pan. Bake at 350° for 50 minutes.

name: Zucchini Bread
author: Shelly Dohogne
instructions: Mix oil, eggs and zucchini. Combine dry ingredients. Add zucchini mixture and blend well. Add nuts. Pour into two greased and floured loaf pans. Bake at 325 degrees for 1 hour. Let stand about 15 minutes and remove from pan.

name: Zucchini Bread
author: Shirley Drury

ingredients.name: c. zucchini squash (raw grated with peel)

instructions: Beat eggs and add oil, squash, sugar and vanilla. Mix well. Sift dry ingredients and combine with liquid mixture. Mix well. Bake at 325° for 1 hour.

name: Zucchini Muffins
author: Helen Raines
instructions: Combine sugar, oil, eggs, vanilla and zucchini. Add remaining ingredients; stir until moistened. Pour in muffin cups. Fill 14 full. Bake 18 minutes at 400°.

name: Brownie Muffins
author: Sr. Rose Marie
instructions: Melt butter, chocolate, butter flavoring and nuts in a double boiler. In separate bowl, combine remaining ingredients. Combine the two mixtures and bake in muffin tins 25 to 30 minutes at 350°. The muffins should be chewy the top being a lighter brown than the rest of the muffin. They will be kind of crackly.

name: Crusty Garlic Bread
author: Rebecca Hooper

ingredients.name: tsp. chopped fresh marjoram or 3/4 tsp. dried marjoram
small (4 oz.) loaves Italian or French bread

instructions: Preheat oven to 350°. In a small bowl, combine the garlic and oil; mix well. In another small bowl, combine parsley, thyme, marjoram, and paprika. Add Parmesan; mix well. Cut each loaf crosswise into diagonal slices, without cutting all the way through. Brush cut sides of slices with garlic oil. Sprinkle herb mixture between slices. Wrap each loaf in foil; place on a baking sheet. Bake until heated through, about 10 to 15 minutes. Unwrap the loaves and place them on a breadboard or in a basket. Serve immediately.  Per serving: Calories 72 (20 % from fat) Carbohydrates 12g Protein 2g Sodium 139mg Fat 1g Cholesterol 0mg.

name: Pizza Crust
author: Kristie Milam
instructions: Mix all ingredients. Gather together and press into a ball. Knead dough in bowl 10 times to make smooth. Roll out dough. Top with your favorite toppings. Bake at 425° for 20 to 30 minutes.

name: Pizza Crust
author: Charlotte Hooper
instructions: Add yeast to warm water. Stir to dissolve. Add flour, salt, and oil. Beat vigorously. Turn the dough onto lightly floured surface. Knead until smooth for 30 seconds. Cover with wax paper and then a towel. Let set 20 minutes. Divide dough into 3 parts; roll each por- tion to fit 12 inch pan (Makes 3-12 inch pizzas). Place on greased pan. Press dough to make the edges of circle slightly thick. Add favorite sauce, meat, toppings and cheese. Bake at 425 for 15 to 20 minutes.

name: Homemade Noodles
author: Charlotte Hooper
instructions: Mix eggs and flour until mixture becomes very stiff. If it is too moist, more flour must be added. Roll dough, when ready to cut, cut with a pasta noodle maker. When done, separate and let dry completely. Then they can be put in bags and froze.

name: Strawberry Bread
author: Anna Rose Bles

ingredients.name: (10 oz.) frozen or 3 c. fresh berries

instructions: Mix the berries, eggs and oil together. Blend in rest of ingredients. Pour into 2 loaf greased and floured pans or greased pans with waxed paper. Bake at 350° for 1 to 1 1/2 hours. Top with strawberry butter.

name: Strawberry Bread (Butter)
author: Anna Rose Bles
instructions: In blender combine strawberries, butter, and sifted powdered sugar. Cover and blend until smooth. Keep in refrigerator to store. Slice strawberry bread thin and spread butter on.

name: Strawberry Bread
author: Zachary Estes
instructions: Blend butter, sugar, vanilla, salt and juice; beat in eggs one at a time. Dissolve soda in sour cream. Add to egg mixture. Fold in flour, nuts, preserves and food coloring. Pour batter into 2 large greased loaf pans. Bake at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes or until bread pulls away from pan.

name: Turnovers
author: Annita Layton
instructions: Mix flour, sugar, salt, and shortening in large bowl until crumbly. Dissolve yeast in water. Add milk, egg and vanilla. Mix and add to dry ingredients. Take small amounts of dough and roll out in pow- dered sugar. Cut out with a 2 pound coffee can. Put 1 tablespoon fruit pie filling in center of dough. Dot with butter. Fold in half and press edges together with fork to seal. Cut 2 slits in top. Sprinkle with sugar and cinnamon. Place on cookie sheets and bake at 350° for 20 minutes. Drizzle with powdered sugar icing while warm.

name: Cherry Scones
author: Annita Layton

ingredients.name: c. snipped dried sweet cherries or raisins

instructions: Place dried cherries or raisins in a bowl. Add enough boiling water to cover fruit. Let stand for 5 minutes; drain well. Sift together flour, brown sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a large mixing bowl. Using a pastry blender, cut in butter or margarine until mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
