Toss cherries or raisins and orange peel with flour mixture. Make a well in center. Stir together sour cream and egg yolk. Add all at once to flour mixture. With a fork, stir until combined (mixture may seem dry.) Turn out onto lightly floured surface. Quickly knead by gently folding and pressing for 10 to 12 strokes or until dough is nearly smooth. Pat or lightly roll dough into a 7 inch circle. Cut into 12 wedges. Arrange 1 inch apart on an ungreased baking sheet. Bake in 400° oven for 10 to 12 minutes or until light brown. Cool on a wire rack 10 minutes. Drizzle with Orange Glaze. Serve warm.

name: Cherry Scones (Orange Glaze)
author: Annita Layton
instructions: Stir together. Stir in more orange juice, a teaspoon at a time, until glaze is of drizzling consistency.

name: Angel Food Cake
author: Annita Layton
instructions: Measure and sift together 3 times cake flour and 3?4 cup plus 2 tablespoon sugar. Beat together with wire whip until foamy egg whites, cream of tarter, and salt. Beat in two tablespoons at a time 3?4 cup sugar (beat about 10 seconds after each addition). Beat until stiff peaks form. Sift three tablespoons flour mixture at a time over whites and fold in (8 to 10 folds). Fold in 1 1/2 teaspoons vanilla (about 10 folds). Fold 8 to 10 more times. Ease batter into pan and cut through with a knife. Bake at 375° 30 to 35 minutes. Invert and cool. Chocolate Angel Food Cake: Substitute 1/4 cup cocoa for 4 cup flour.

name: Homemade Angel Food Cake
author: Revella Schlosser
instructions: Sift together flour and powdered sugar 3 times. Set aside. Beat egg whites, cream of tarter, and salt until foamy. Gradually add 1 tablespoon of sugar at a time and beat until very stiff. Fold in vanilla and almond. Sift 1/4 of flour and powdered sugar at a time and fold in gently. Pour in pan. Bake at 375° for 30 to 35 minutes.

name: Julie's Famous Angel Food Cake
author: Donna Essner
instructions: Sift flour and 1 cup sugar, set aside. Beat until foamy egg whites, cream of tartar and salt. Gradually add sugar while mixer is beating egg whites. When egg whites are stiff, add vanilla. Fold in flour and sugar mixture in small amounts. Place in ungreased tube pan. Bake at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes. Cool upside down.

name: Yellow Angel Food Cake
author: In Memory of Ella I. Schlosser
instructions: Beat yolks of eggs thick and lemon colored. Add water and beat about 4 minutes. Add flour, baking powder and salt sifted together. Beat whites stiff, adding cream of tarter. Fold whites into batter and pour in ungreased angel food pan. Bake in oven that is slow at first, 300. After 15 minutes increase heat to moderate oven, 350°. Then, bake for another 30 to 35 minutes.

name: Cherry-Nut Angel Food Cake
author: S.B.G

ingredients.name: box angel food cake mix as directed on box

instructions: Mix cake mix as directed on box. Add other ingredients and beat on low speed for about 15 seconds. Bake at 350 degrees for 40 to 45 minutes until top is deep golden brown. Do not under bake. Turn angel food pan upside down until completely cool. Remove from pan and ice with glaze icing or cream cheese frosting.

name: Cherry Nut Angel Food Cake
author: Charlotte Hooper

ingredients.name: pkg. (2 step) angel food cake mix

instructions: Mix angel food cake as directed. When finished fold cherries and pecans. Pour into tube cake pan and bake according to package directions. When done you can add the icing of your choice. It is also good without icing.

name: Angel Food Cake Roll Up (Cake)
author: Shirley Eftink
instructions: Prepare an angel food cake mix as directed on the box. Pour batter into a 12 x 16 inch cookie sheet lined with waxed paper. Bake until edges are golden brown or cake springs back when touched in the center. While cake is still hot, turn over onto a towel sprinkled with powdered sugar. Peel off waxed paper. Carefully roll towel and cake from wide end. Cool completely.

name: Angel Food Cake Roll Up (Filling)
author: Shirley Eftink
instructions: Cream powdered sugar, cream cheese and vanilla. Stir in Cool Whip. Unroll cake and fill with filling. Re-roll. Refrigerate until ready for use.

name: Fresh Apple Spice Cake
author: Juanita Dannenmueller
instructions: Cream margarine and sugars with electric mixer until light and fluffy. Add eggs, one at a time beating after each addition. Sift togeth- er the flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt and 2 teaspoons of cin- namon. Add sifted dry ingredients and milk in thirds alternately, beating until smooth after each addition. Fold in apples, spread batter in 9 x 13 x 2 inch pan. Sprinkle sugar, cinnamon and nuts on top. Bake at 300° for about 1 hour and 15 minutes.

name: German Apple Cake
author: Marian M. Essner
instructions: Peel apples and thinly slice. In a bowl, toss apple slices with 5 tablespoons sugar and cinnamon and let set while mixing other ingredients. Grease and flour a 10 inch tube pan or Bundt pan. Preheat oven to 350°. In a large bowl, mix together sugar, eggs, oil, vanilla. Beat well. Add dry ingredients; flour, salt, baking soda, baking powder. Mix thoroughly. Add orange juice. Blend for 1 minute on low speed, then increase speed to medium for 3 minutes. You will have a very thick batter. Fill prepared pan with alternating layers of batter and apple mixture, making a total of 3 batter layers and 2 apple layers. Start and finish with batter. (Be sure not to make apple layers too thick or cake will not hold together.) Bake for 1 1/2 to 1 3/4 hours or until knife comes out clean. Cool on rack for 10 minutes. Allow cake to cool completely on rack. Then invert cake and remove from pan.

name: Apple Cake
author: Shelly dohogne
instructions: Cream shortening, sugar, and eggs. Sift together dry ingredients. Add pecans and apples. Press into lightly greased 9x13 inch pan. Bake at 350° for 50 minutes.

name: Grandma Meyer's Fresh Apple Cake
author: Tina Schlosser
instructions: Pour one cup of sugar over apples and let stand for one hour. Mix together dry ingredients. Cream margarine, brown sugar and eggs. Alternate apples and flour mixture until it is all used up. Fold in the coconut and nuts. Put in greased baking pan and bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes.

name: Fresh Apple Cake
author: Donna Menz
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°. In large bowl, stir together apples and sug- ar. Add dry ingredients, stir well. In separate bowl beat eggs, oil and vanilla. Stir egg mixture into apple mixture, blending until thoroughly moistened. Stir in pecans. Pour into greased 9 x 13 inch pan. Bake 50 minutes or until cake springs back. Serve with apple dessert sauce or Cool Whip.

name: Fresh Apple Cake (Dessert Sauce)
author: Donna Menz

ingredients.name: c. heaving cream or evaporated milk

instructions: Place all ingredients in saucepan; stir. Bring to boil over medium heat and cook for 3 minutes. Serve warm over cake.

name: Applesauce Cake
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Mix together sugar, shortening and vanilla. Beat in eggs. Add applesauce. Add flour, spices, baking soda and salt. Mix in nuts and raisins. Grease and flour an angel food cake pan. Pour batter into pan and bake for 1 hour at 350°.

name: Apple Crumb Cake
author: Gale Ledure

ingredients.name: box yellow or white cake mix

instructions: Mix cake mix and butter until crumbly with mixer. Take out 2/3 cup of mixture and set aside. Put 1/3 cake mix in pan for the first layer. For second layer, arrange apples on top. Beat sour cream and egg pour over apples for third layer. Mix together remaining together and cake mix, brown sugar, cinnamon and sprinkle on top. Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes. Refrigerate and reheat leftovers.

name: Crunchy Apricot Cake
author: Ramona Glastetter

ingredients.name: (1 lb. 6 oz.) can apricot pie filling
pkg. (1 layer size) white cake mix

instructions: Spread pie filling in bottom of 9 x 9 x 2 inch baking dish. Com-bine cake mix, the water, and the egg. Using electric mixer, beat 4 minutes on medium speed. Pour over pie filling; sprinkle with coconut and pecans. Drizzle butter or margarine over top. Bake in moderate oven, 350°, for 40 minutes. Serve warm.

name: Banana Cake
author: Doris Moore, In Memory of Ella I. Schlosser

ingredients.name: c. cake flour, sift before measuring

instructions: Preheat oven to 350°. Sift cake flour, baking powder, baking soda and salt. Cream butter and add sugar, mixing until very light. Beat in eggs one at a time. Mix together bananas and vanilla and buttermilk or yogurt. Add the flour mixture to the butter mixture in about 3 parts, alternating with thirds of the banana mixture. Stir the batter after each addition until smooth. Bake in greased pans for about 1/2 an hour. When cool, place between the layers: 2 sliced ripe bananas and spread the cake with a white icing.

name: Fiesta Banana Nut Cake
author: Revella Schlosser

ingredients.name: c. sifted Swan's Down cake flour
c. mashed bananas (2 or 3 fully ripe)
c. minus 2 Tbsp. sour milk (with butter, margarine, or lard)*

instructions: *With vegetable or another shortening use 1/2 c. sour milk. Measure flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and sugar into the sifter. Measure shortening into mixing bowl. Measure sour milk and vanilla into cup. Have bananas, eggs, and nuts ready. Stir shortening just to soften. Stir in dry ingredients. Add 1/4 cup of milk and the bananas and mix until all of the flour is dampened. Then beat 300 strokes by hand or 2 minutes with the mixer at low speed. Add remaining milk, nuts, and eggs. Beat 150 strokes by hand or 1 minute with mixer. Bake at 375° for 25 minutes in 2 greased 9 inch pans.

name: Banana Nut Cake
author: Juanita Dannenmueller
instructions: Heat oven to 350°. Grease and flour 13 x 9 x 2 inch or two 9 inch or three 8 inch round baking pans. Measure all ingredients into large mixer bowl. Blend 1/2 minute on low speed, scraping bowl constantly. Beat 3 minutes on high speed, scraping bowl occasionally. Pour into pan(s). Bake oblong cake 45 to 50 minutes, layers 35 to 40 minutes or until wooden pick inserted in center comes out clean. Cool. Frost with Mock Whip Icing.

name: Ramona's Carrot Cake
author: Ramona Glastetter
instructions: Beat eggs for 10 minutes. Add sugar and hot water and mix well. Add oil slowly. Add remaining ingredients. Blend well. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes. Ice with cream cheese frosting.

name: Ramona's Carrot Cake (Cream Cheese Frosting)
author: Ramona Glastetter
instructions: Cream together cream cheese and butter. Add confectioners' sugar, vanilla and chopped pecans.

name: Carrot Cake
author: In Memory of Ella I. Schlosser
instructions: Mix sugar and oil. Add eggs and beat. Add dry ingredients to sugar mixture. Add carrots. Bake at 300° for 40 to 50 minutes.

name: Carrot Cake (Icing)
author: In Memory of Ella I. Schlosser
instructions: Beat with mixer and spread on cake.

name: Carrot Cake
author: Tina Blattel
instructions: Beat eggs well. Add sugar and hot water. Mix well. Add oil slowly. Add balance of ingredients and blend well. Bake 1 hour at 350°.

name: Carrot Cake
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Mix sugar and oil. Add eggs. vanilla. Mix in carrots and nuts. for 40 to 50 minutes.

name: Carrot Cake (Icing)
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Beat well. Frost cake. Mix well. Add dry ingredients and Bake in three 9 inch pans at 300°

name: French Carrot Cake
author: Joan Drury

ingredients.name: C. firmly packed dark brown sugar

instructions: Preheat oven to 350°. Grease two 9 inch round cake pans. In th bowl of an electric mixer, cream butter with sugars. Add eggs and vanilla and beat until mixture is light and fluffy. Sift together flour, baking soda, salt, and cinnamon. Add these ingredients to batter; mix well. Fold in carrots and walnuts. Pour batter evenly into pans; bake for 40 to 45 minutes, until tester inserted in center comes out clean. Remove from oven to racks and cool completely before frosting. (Up to this point the recipe may be made in advance and placed in the freezer. Defrost and decorate with frosting.) Ice the tops of the layers Joan Drury and then assemble the cake. Frost the sides with remaining frosting. Decorate top of cake with carrot designs made from green and orange frosting or sprinkle the top with chopped walnuts and serve.

name: Sharen's Blue Ribbon Carrot Cake
author: Sharen
instructions: Combine eggs, oil, buttermilk, sugar, and vanilla. Beat until smooth. Stir in flour mixture, pineapple, carrots, coconut, and chopped nuts. Pour batter into 2 greased and floured 9-inch round cake pans. Bake at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes or until a wooden pick inserted in center comes out clean. Cool in pan 15 minutes. Remove and let cool completely. Use Cream Cheese Frosting to frost cake.

name: Cherry Dump Cake
author: Juanita Dannenmueller
instructions: In an oblong pan put cherry pie filling, followed by crushed pine- apple. Sift cake mix over top of cherry pie filling and pineapple. Sprinkle oats and nuts over cake mix and put butter slices on top of the oats and nuts. Bake at 350° for 50 minutes.

name: Chocolate Trifle
author: Donna Stamp

ingredients.name: baked angel food cake, torn into bite-size pieces
small pkg. fat free chocolate pudding
Skor candy bar or 1 Butterfinger candy bar

instructions: Mix pudding according to package directions. In a punch bowl layer 1/2 angel food cake pieces, 1?2 mixed pudding, 1?2 container Cool Whip, and 1?2 crushed candy bar. Repeat layers ending with crushed candy bar on top. Chill until ready to serve.

name: Neiman Marcus Cake
author: Donna Menz
instructions: Mix cake mix, 2 eggs, oleo and nuts together and spread on a greased 9 x 13 inch pan (will be a stiff dough). Mix 2 eggs, vanilla, cream cheese, and powdered sugar together and spread on top of cake batter and bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes.

name: Miracle Whip Chocolate Cake
author: Karla Essner
instructions: Mix dry ingredients. Stir in Miracle Whip with a spoon. Stir in hot water. Stir in vanilla. Spray 13 x 9 inch pan with nonstick cooking spray. Pour batter into pan. Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes. If desired, recipe makes 36 cupcakes. Spoon 2 tablespoons batter in each baking cup. Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.

name: Upside-Down German Chocolate Cake
author: Shelley Dohogne
instructions: Grease a 9 x 13 inch pan very well. Sprinkle pecans and coconut in bottom of pan. Mix cake according to directions and pour over pecans and coconut. Melt together margarine and cream cheese. Stir in powdered sugar. Spread this mixture over cake batter. Bake for 35 to 45 minutes or until toothpick that has been inserted comes out clean. (Use oven temperature suggested on cake mix.) Let cool in pan 5 to 10 minutes. Flip onto serving platter.

name: 20 Minute Cake
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Sift sugar and flour together. Set aside. Mix oleo, cocoa, and water in saucepan. Bring to a rapid boil. Then pour over sugar and flour mixture and stir until blended. Add remaining ingredients and mix well. Pour into greased 11 x 16 inch pan. Bake 20 minutes at 400°. Begin making icing 5 minutes before cake is done.

name: Five Minute Chocolate Cake (Mixes In Five Minutes)
author: Donna Stamp
instructions: In large bowl of mixer, combine dry ingredients. Add eggs, milk, oil, and vanilla; beat at medium speed 2 minutes. Remove from mixer; stir in boiling water. (Batter will be thin). Pour into two greased and floured 9 inch round pans, three 8 inch round pans, or one 13 x 9 inch pan. Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes for round pans, 35 to 40 min- utes for 13 x 9 inch pan, or until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean. Cool 10 minutes on rack. Remove from pans; cool completely. Frost cooled cake. Chocolate icing is great but peanut butter frosting is the best!!

name: Peter Paul Mound Cake
author: Guess who?

ingredients.name: box Duncan Hines chocolate cake mix

instructions: Mix cake mix as directed on box. Add oil and one box pudding. Bake in a 9 x 13 inch greased and floured pan at 350°.

name: Peter Paul Mound Cake (Icing)
author: Guess who?
instructions: Heat marshmallows, milk, and sugar until melted. Add coconut and vanilla. Mix Coca-Cola, margarine and cocoa. Heat to boiling and add powdered sugar. Spread over cake by spoonfuls. Allow to cool.

name: Mississippi Mudd Cake
author: Guess who?
instructions: Cream sugar and butter; add eggs; mix well. Add other ingredients. Pour into a greased 9 x 13 inch pan and bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes. While hot spread with marshmallow creme.

name: Mississippi Mudd Cake (Icing)
author: Guess who?
instructions: Mix all ingredients together and spread on cake.

name: Chocolate Caramel Filled Cake
author: Karen M.
instructions: Melt caramels and butter in large saucepan over low heat. Remove from heat; stir in Eagle brand milk until smooth. Prepare cake mix according to package directions. Pour 2 cups of batter into a 9 x 13 inch baking pan, coated with cooking spray. Bake at 350° for 15 minutes. Spread caramel mixture over cake; pour remaining cake batter over caramel mixture, top with nuts. Continue to bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes or until done. Cool and cut into squares to serve.

name: Ron's Turtle Cake
author: R.P.
instructions: Prepare cake mix as directed on box. Pour 1/2 of the batter into a greased and floured 9 x 13 inch pan. Bake at 350° for 15 minutes. Remove from oven and let cool. Combine caramels, milk, and butter. Melt ingredients and pour over the cake. Then sprinkle chips and pecans over caramel mixture. Pour remaining batter over caramel mixture and sprinkle with 1?2 cup of pecans. Return cake to oven and bake for 15 minutes.

name: Turtle Cake
author: Helen Kluesner
instructions: Prepare cake mix as on package. Pour half of batter into a greased 9 x 13 inch pan and bake at 350° for 15 minutes. Melt caramels with milk and butter in a sauce pan over low heat stirring constantly. After the 15 minutes of baking pour melted caramels, 1 cup nuts, and chocolate chips over the cake. Pour remaining batter over this filling and sprinkle with remaining nuts and bake about 30 minutes longer.

name: Turtle Fudge Cake
author: Ruth Schlosser
instructions: Prepare pudding as directed on the package. Blend cake mix into hot pudding. Pour in oblong 13 x 9 1/2 inch pan. Sprinkle with coconut, chocolate chips, and nuts. Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes. Serve warm with whipped cream.

name: Spice Cake
author: In Memory of Anna Diebold

ingredients.name: tsp. cornstarch mixed with 1/2 c. flour

instructions: Cream butter and vanilla until light. Add beaten egg and mix well. Add milk, soda, nutmeg, cinnamon, cloves and flour. Bake in a moderate oven.

name: Cocoa Spice Cake
author: Lorena Essner
instructions: Cream together sugar and shortening. Add eggs. Then add dry ingredients and milk alternately. Bake in a moderate oven until done.

name: Glazed Chocolate Cherry Cake
author: Anna Rose Bles
instructions: Combine all ingredients, stirring until blended (batter will be thick). Spread evenly in a greased and floured 13 x 9 x 2 inch pan. Bake at 350° for 25 minutes. Cool in pan on wire rack 15 minutes.

name: Glazed Chocolate Cherry Cake (Icing)
author: Anna Rose Bles
instructions: Melt together butter, milk, and chocolate chips. Stir in powdered sugar. Pour on cake.

name: Chocolate Cream Dream
author: Don and Clara Essner Family

ingredients.name: pkg. 12 oz. semi sweet chocolate chips
angel food cake broken into pieces

instructions: Melt chocolate chips over low heat. Beat in water until smooth. Beat in egg yolks one at a time. Cook over medium heat until thickened. Pour into large bowl and cool 15 minutes. Beat egg whites until frothy, then beat in sugar, 1 tablespoon at a time. Beat until stiff peaks form. Fold whipped cream, egg whites, and nuts into chocolate mixture. Arrange cake pieces in a buttered 9 x 13 inch dish. Pour chocolate mixture over cake. Sprinkle nuts over top of cake and refrigerate.

name: Chocolate Sheet Cake
author: Nancy Weissmueller
instructions: Mix together and bring to a boil the margarine, cocoa, and water. Mix together the flour, sugar, and baking soda. Add dry mixture to liquid mixture. Stir in the milk, eggs, and vanilla. Bake on large, greased, and floured cookie sheet in 350° oven for 20 minutes.

name: Chocolate Sheet Cake (Frosting)
author: Nancy Weissmueller
instructions: Mix together and bring to a boil the margarine, cocoa, and buttermilk. Stir in the powdered sugar, vanilla, and pecans. Pour over warm cake.

name: Chocolate Chip Cake
author: Annita Layton
instructions: Grease and flour 9 x 13 inch pan or 2 round layer pans. Sift flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt into bowl. Add shortening, milk, and vanilla. Beat 2 minutes on medium speed. Scrape sides and bot- tom of bowl constantly. Add egg whites. Beat 2 more minutes. Care- fully fold in chocolate chips. Pour into prepared pans. Bake at 350° 30 to 35 minutes for layers and 40 to 45 minutes for oblong.

name: Chocolate Chip Cake
author: Donna Stamp, Donna Essner

ingredients.name: oz. pkg. (1 cup) semi-sweet chocolate chips

instructions: Heat oven to 350°. Grease (not oil) 13 x 9 inch pan in large bowl, blend first 9 ingredients at low speed until moistened. Beat 3 minutes at medium speed. Pour half of batter (about 2 1/2 cups) into prepared pan. In small bowl, combine 1?2 cup sugar and cinnamon. Sprinkle half of sugar mixture and chocolate chips over batter. Repeat with remaining batter, sugar mixture, and chocolate chips. Bake at 350' for 35 to 40 minutes or until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean.

name: Fast Fixin' Chocolate Chip Cake
author: Sister Dorothy Reinhold

ingredients.name: (18.25 oz.) box devil's food cake mix
(4 serving size) pkg. chocolate instant pudding mix

instructions:
Preheat oven to 350°. You don't need bowl. Pour oil into a 13 x 9 x 2 inch pan. Tilt pan until bottom is covered with oil. Put cake mix, eggs, water, pudding mix, and chocolate chips into pan; stir with a fork or spoon until blended, about 2 minutes. Scrape sides; spread batter evenly in pan. Bake 35 to 45 minutes, until tooth pick inserted near center comes out clean. Cooled cake may be sprinkled with pow- dered sugar. Use a knife to loosen cake from sides; cut and serve directly from pan. Store leftover cake loosely covered.
Variation: Prepare pan as directed, using 1/4 cup oil. Add cake mix, 2 eggs, 1/2 cup water and 1 (20 to 23 ounce) can cherry pie filling. Mix, bake, and serve.

name: Championship Cupcakes
author: Shari Landewe
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°. Line 18 muffin cups with paper baking cups. In a large bowl, combine pecans, butter, chocolate, and vanilla. Set aside. Mix the sugar, flour, salt, and eggs. Stir into the chocolate mixture, blending well. Pour into prepared tins, filling each slightly more than half. Bake 25 to 30 minutes.

name: Surprise Cupcakes
author: Louise Maria
instructions: Mix cake according to directions. Mix together cream cheese, egg, and sugar. Add chocolate chips. Fill cupcake paper 1/4 to 2/3 full of cake mix. Put 1 teaspoon full of cheese mixture on top of each. Bake according to package directions.

name: Coconut Cake
author: Louise Maria
instructions: Prepare cake mix as directed on box. After cake is baked, bring milk, sugar and coconut to a boil. With a fork, punch holes in cake and pour the mixture over cake. Refrigerate. Let set overnight. Top with Cool Whip and coconut.

name: Italian Creme Cake
author: Sharen
instructions: Cream margarine and shortening; add sugar and beat until mixture is smooth. Add egg yolks and beat well. Combine flour and baking soda and add to creamed mixture alternately with buttermilk. Stir in vanilla. Add coconut and nuts. Fold in egg whites. Pour batter into 3 greased and floured 8 inch cake pans. Bake at 350° for 25 minutes or until cake tests done; cool.

name: Italian Creme Cake (Frosting)
author: Sharen
instructions: Beat cream cheese and margarine until smooth. Add sugar and mix well. Add vanilla and beat until smooth. Spread on cake. Sprinkle with chopped pecans.

name: Easy Cake
author: In Memory of Helen Schlosser
instructions: Mix all ingredients together and beat well. Pour into well greased pan and bake at 350° until done.

name: Fruit Cocktail Cake
instructions: Sift in a large bowl the flour, soda, salt, and 1 1/2 cups sugar. Add fruit cocktail (juice and all), eggs, and vanilla. Beat well and pour into a 13 x 8 inch baking pan. Over top of batter sprinkle a mixture of brown sugar and nuts. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes or 325° for 50 min- utes. While cake is baking cook together 1 cup sugar, margarine, and evaporated milk. Cook above ingredients together for 5 minutes. Then add coconut, nuts, and vanilla. Mix together and pour over cake while it is still warm.

name: Ooey Gooey Butter Cake
author: Charlotte Hooper

ingredients.name: pkg. yellow cake mix (Aldi brand makes best)

instructions: Melt butter, add cake mix and 2 eggs. Mix well and pat into pre- pared cookie sheet. Soften cream cheese and add powdered sugar and 2 eggs. Beat well. Pour on top of cake mixture. Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes or until top is cracked.

name: Gooey Butter Cake
author: Beverly Essner
instructions: Mix together cake mix, 1 egg, and margarine and press into greased 9 x 13 inch pan. Blend cream cheese, 2 eggs, vanilla, and powdered sugar. Pour mixture over cake and bake for 30 to 35 minutes at 350°. Sprinkle with powdered sugar.

name: Honey Bun Cake
author: Beverly Essner
instructions: Mix together cake mix, sour cream, milk, eggs, oil, and pudding. Beat very well. Spread of batter in a 9 x 13 inch greased pan. Mix brown sugar with cinnamon. Sprinkle over batter. Pour remaining batter over this. Swirl batter with knife. Bake at 350° for 40 minutes. Remove from oven. Pour powdered sugar glaze over top while hot.

name: Honey Bun Cake (Powdered Sugar Glaze)
author: Beverly Essner
instructions: Mix together.

name: Hummingbird Cake
author: Maris Elizabeth
instructions: Combine flour, sugar, baking soda, and cinnamon. Add eggs and oil. Stir until moist. Do not beat. Stir in vanilla, pineapple, bananas and 1 cup nuts. Bake in 3 greased and floured 9 inch cake pans at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes. Cool 10 minutes. Remove from pans and cool completely. Frost with cream cheese frosting.

name: Hummingbird Cake (Cream Cheese Frosting)
author: Maris Elizabeth
instructions: Combine cream cheese and margarine. Cream until smooth. Add powdered sugar. Beat until light and fluffy. Add vanilla. Spread frosting between layers, sides, and top. Sprinkle with remaining cup of pecans.

name: Irish Trifle
author: Fr. Oliver Clavin

ingredients.name: Custard or instant pudding, about 3 pt.
Strawberries or other fruit for topping

instructions: Mix gelatin with boiling water. Let cool. In the meantime, soak pieces of cake in sherry in bottom of glass bowl. Spread cake with a layer of jam. Pour cooled gelatin on top of soaked cake. Chill. Drain the can of fruit and pour fruit on top of gelatin. Prepare instant pud- ding or custard, and pour over the fruit. Chill. Before serving, top with the whipped cream and cherries, strawberries, peaches or fruit of choice.

name: Jam Cake
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Cream shortening and sugar together. Add eggs. Sift all dry ingredients together. Add alternately with buttermilk. Add jam. Bake in 350° oven.

name: Jam Cake (Caramel Icing)
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Melt butter. Add brown sugar. Cook 2 minutes. Add milk, bring to a boil. Take off fire, cool, then beat in powdered sugar and spread.

name: Light Golden Cake
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Sift together flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt. Add shorten- ing. Mix together milk and flavoring. Pour a little over half of milk and flavoring mixture into above mixture. Beat 2 minutes. Add remaining milk and beat 2 minutes. Pour into greased and floured pans. Bake at 350° until cake tests done. Cool. Finish with filling or frosting as desired.

name: Oatmeal Cake
author: Juanita Dannenmueller
instructions: Pour boiling water over quick oats. Let stand for 20 minutes. Cream shortening, sugar, and brown sugar. Add eggs and beat. Add oats, flour, salt, baking powder, cinnamon and nuts. Bake in oblong pan for 35 minutes at 350°.

name: Oatmeal Cake (Topping)
author: Juanita Dannenmueller
instructions: Mix together. Spread on cake. Place under broiler until brown.

name: Oatmeal Cake
author: Juanita Dannenmueller
instructions: Pour water over oats and let stand 20 minutes. Cream sugars and shortening. Add eggs. Beat well. Add oat mixture, dry ingredients and vanilla. Bake at 350° until done. Sprinkle with additional topping.

name: Oatmeal Cake (Topping)
author: Juanita Dannenmueller
instructions: Mix ingredients together, pour over cake. Broil in broiler until brown.

name: Oatmeal Cake
author: Annita Layton
instructions:
Mix oatmeal and boiling water: let cool. Cream butter and sug- ars. Add eggs, vanilla and oatmeal. Sift flour, soda and salt. Fold into mixture, then add cinnamon and raisins. Bake about 40 minutes at 350°.
For Chocolate Oatmeal Cake: Same as above except: add 1 1/2 c. sugar, 1 c. flour, 1?2 c. cocoa, 1?2 tsp. salt and omit cinnamon and raisins.

name: Oatmeal Cake
author: Ramona Glastetter
instructions: Pour boiling water over oats. Let stand for 20 minutes. Add all other ingredients. Bake at 350° for 35 minutes.

name: Oatmeal Cake (Icing)
author: Ramona Glastetter
instructions: Mix icing over a warm burner and it will cover the cake better. Then put it under the broiler and let it brown and it will bubble. Bake in 9 x 13 inch pan. Serve warm or cold.

name: Cotton Pickin Cake
author: Iva Welter

ingredients.name: box Duncan Hines cake mix (buttery kind)
c. Wesson oil (no other kind) 1 can mandarin oranges-juice and all

instructions: Blend cake mix, eggs, oil and oranges in mixer. Bake in 3 layers at 325° or until pick comes out dry. Completely cool.

name: Cotton Pickin Cake (Icing)
author: Iva Welter
instructions: Mix with spoon. Cover layers, sides, and top. Keep covered and store in refrigerator.

name: Better Than Sex Cake
author: Guess Who?
instructions: Bake 1 box yellow cake mix as usual. Cook 1 can crushed pine- apple and 1 cup sugar until dissolved. Put on top of cool cake. Add 1 box of vanilla pudding, mix according to directions. Put on top of pineapple. Cool. Add Cool Whip, maraschino cherries, and coconut if desired. Refrigerate overnight.

name: Mandarin Orange Cake
author: Helen Kluesner
instructions: Mix all together. Bake in a 350° oven for 20 to 25 minutes. Cool.

name: Mandarin Orange Cake (Topping)
author: Helen Kluesner

ingredients.name: small can crushed pineapple 1 box coconut instant pudding

instructions: Mix all together and spread over cooled cake. Refrigerate.

name: Pina Colada Cake
author: Shirley Eftink
instructions: Bake cake mix according to directions on box. Remove from oven. Poke holes in cake with fork. Pour can of pina colada and juice from pineapple over cake. Cover cake with pineapple. Put on whipped topping. Sprinkle with coconut.

name: Pineapple Cream Cake
author: Dorothy Glastetter

ingredients.name: Nuts, coconut, or cherries if desired

instructions: Mix and bake cake as directed on package in a 9 x 13 inch pan. Let cool. Beat softened cream cheese with 1/2 cup milk until smooth. Add 1 1/2 cup milk and pudding mix. Beat on low speed until well blended. Let stand 5 to 10 minutes. Spread this over the cooled cake, then spread the drained pineapple over the pudding mixture. Next spread Cool Whip on top. Sprinkle with nuts, coconut or cherries. Chill and serve.

name: Pineapple-Banana Cake
author: Irene Blattel
instructions: Measure dry ingredients, dice bananas and cover with flour. Mix well with rest of dry ingredients. Add oil, nuts, vanilla, eggs, and pine- apple. Blend by hand. Bake at 350°. Serve warm with whipped topping or ice with your favorite frosting. This cake freezes very well.

name: Zucchini-Pineapple Cake
author: Revella Schlosser
instructions: Drain zucchini well, pressing between layers of paper towel. Set aside. Beat eggs at medium speed with electric mixer until thick and pale. Gradually add sugar, beating well. Stir in grated zucchini. Combine flour and next 4 ingredients, gradually stir into zucchini mix- ture. Stir in pecans, raisins, and pineapple. Pour into 3 greased and floured 8 inch round cake pans. Bake at 325° for 35 minutes or until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool in pans on wire racks for 10 min- utes. Remove from pans and cool completely on wire racks. Spread Pineapple Cream Cheese frosting between layers and on top of cake. The frosting is soft and recipe works better if sides of cake are left unfrosted. Cover and refrigerate.

name: Zucchini-Pineapple Cake (Pineapple Cream Cheese Frosting)
author: Revella Schlosser
instructions: Place pineapple in a wire mesh strainer. Press with back of spoon against the sides of the strainer to squeeze out liquid. Set pineap- ple aside and discard liquid. Beat cream cheese and butter at medium speed with an electric mixer until fluffy. Gradually stir in powdered sugar and pineapple. Frosting will be soft and may be refrigerated 1 hour before spreading over cake.

name: Lemon Pudding-Pound Cake
author: Ramona Glastetter

ingredients.name: pkg. (2 layer size) yellow cake mix
(3 3/4 or 3 5/8 oz.) pkg. instant lemon pudding

instructions: Beat eggs until thick and lemon-colored. Add cake mix, pudding (dry), water, and oil: beat at medium speed, 10 minutes. Pour into ungreased 10-inch tube pan with removable bottom. Bake at 350° about 50 minutes. Remove hot cake, on pan bottom, from pan. Using a 2-tined fork, prick holes in top of cake: drizzle glaze over top and spread on sides of cake. For Glaze: Combine lemon juice and confectioners sugar; heat to boiling.

name: Pumpkin Pie Cake
author: Donna Essner
instructions: Mix together pumpkin, eggs, spice, vanilla, Milnot, salt and sugar. Pour mixture into a 9 x 13 inch baking pan. Sprinkle yellow cake mix over top. Drizzle over top, the melted oleo. Sprinkle chopped pecans. Bake at 350° oven for 60 minutes or until done.

name: Pumpkin Roll
author: R.L.
instructions: Beat eggs for 5 minutes. Add sugar and other ingredients. Mix thoroughly. Spread batter in a large greased cookie sheet with sides. Sprinkle with one cup nuts. Bake at 375° for 15 minutes. Dust dish towel with powdered sugar. Turn cake out onto powdered sugar and roll up. Let cool rolled up.

name: Pumpkin Roll (Filling)
author: R.L.
instructions: Mix above ingredients together. Chill, then unroll cake and spread on filling. Reroll cake and keep refrigerated.

name: Pumpkin and Cream Cheese Roll-Up
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Preheat oven to moderate 375°. Grease a 15 x 10 x 1 inch jelly roll pan. Line with wax paper. Grease and flour the wax paper. Sift flour, baking powder, cinnamon, pumpkin pie spice, nutmeg, and salt onto wax paper. Beat eggs and sugar in large bowl until thick and fluffy; beat in pumpkin. Stir in sifted dry ingredients all at once. Pour into prepared pan; spread evenly with rubber spatula. Sprinkle with nuts. Bake in preheated moderate oven (375°) for 15 minutes or until center springs back when lightly touched with fingertip. Loosen cake around edges with a knife. Invert onto clean damp towel dusted with confectioners sugar peel off wax paper. Trim 1/4 inch from all sides. Roll up cake and towel together from short side. Place seam-side down on wire rack; cool completely. Unroll cake. Spread with Cream Cheese Filling. Reroll cake. Refrigerate until ready to serve.

name: Pumpkin and Cream Cheese Roll-Up (Cream Cheese Filling)
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Beat together until smooth.

name: Punch Bowl Cake
author: Charlotte Hooper
instructions: In large punch bowl, cube 2 of the pound cake. Mix 1 package pudding with 1 1/2 cup milk. Then pour over cake cubes. Slice 3 bananas and add to top. Then add 1 can crushed pineapple and top with 1 can of cherry pie filling. Repeat layers and top with 1 large Cool Whip. Can be decorated with maraschino cherries and nuts. Refrigerate well before serving.

name: Eggless Raisin Cake
author: Lorena Essner

ingredients.name: c. raisin juice (add water if needed)

instructions: Boil raisins until tender. Cream sugar and lard. Add spices. Dis- solve soda in juice of raisins. Stir in the flour, then add raisins last. Bake in a loaf or layer and put together with caramel or coconut icing.

name: Orange Raisin Cake
author: Ramona Bess
instructions: Cream sugar, butter, and eggs. Dissolve soda in sour milk and add to egg mixture. Grind orange (rinds and juice) and raisins. Add to mixture. Glaze with powdered sugar and orange juice.

name: Red Velvet Cake
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Mix together above ingredients.

name: Red Velvet Cake (Icing)
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Mix together and pour on cake.

name: Rhubarb Cake
author: Annita Layton
instructions: Mix 1/2 of sugar with rhubarb, let stand until shortening is creamed. Mix all ingredients together well then add rhubarb, stir well. Pour into greased and floured pan. Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes. Prepare topping and pour on cooled cake.

name: Rhubarb Cake (Topping)
author: Annita Layton
instructions: Mix all together and bring to a boil. Cook for three minutes.

name: Shortcake
author: Annita Layton
instructions: Put dry ingredients into bowl. Cut in butter with pastry blender or fork. Add milk to moisten so dough is consistency of biscuits. Spread into greased 8 inch square pan. Drizzle with melted butter. Bake at 425° for 20 minutes. Serve with strawberries and whipped cream.

name: Shoofly Cake
author: Shirley Drury

ingredients.name: Whipped cream or vanilla ice cream (optional)

instructions: Stir together flour, sugar, soda, and salt. Cut in shortening until mixture resembles fine crumbs. Stir together hot water and molasses. Add to crumb mixture in bowl. Stir just until blended. Turn batter into a greased 9 x 1 1/2 inch round cake pan. Sprinkle reserved crumbs over top. Bake in 350° oven for 25 to 35 minutes or until cake proves done when tested with a wooden toothpick. Serve warm or cool with whipped cream or ice cream if desired.

name: Jean-Ann's Cake--Sock-It-To-Me
author: In Memory of Ella I. Schlosser

ingredients.name: box Duncan Hines golden butter mix

instructions: Mix together cake mix, oil, sugar, eggs, and sour cream. Then mix brown sugar, cinnamon, and nuts. Starting with sugar mixture, alternate these two mixtures until all is gone into a tube pan. Bake at 350° for 1 hour.

name: Snicker Cake
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Melt 8 bars with 1 stick butter. Cream 1 stick butter with sugar. Add eggs, flour, baking soda, milk, and vanilla. Fold in Snicker mixture. Set oven on 300° and bake for 1 hour.

name: Snicker Cake (Icing)
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Melt Snickers and butter together. Add milk and enough powdered sugar to make the consistency you desire.

name: Sponge Cake
author: In Memory of Ella I. Schlosser
instructions: Beat egg yolks and water until foamy. Add sugar 1 tablespoonat a time. Then add flour and baking powder. Add vanilla. Bake in moderate 375° oven for 30 minutes.

name: Sponge Cake Roll
author: Ginny Robert
instructions:
Lightly grease 15 1/2 x 10 1/2 x 1 inch jelly roll pan. Line bottom with waxed paper and grease again. Set aside. In mixing bowl beat egg whites, cream of tartar and salt at high speed until stiff but not dry, just until whites no longer slip when bowl is tilted. In large bowl, beat egg yolks at high speed until thick and lemon-colored, about 5 minutes. Gradually beat in confectioners sugar and vanilla. Gently but thoroughly fold flour and whites into yolk mixture. Pour into prepared pan, spreading evenly.
Bake in preheated 400° oven until top of cake springs back when touched lightly with finger 10 to 12 minutes. Cover a clean towel with waxed paper. Sprinkle paper lightly with confectioners sugar. Loosen cake from sides of pan with spatula and invert onto prepared towel. Carefully pull waxed paper off bottom of cake and discard. Trim all edges. Starting from narrow edge, roll up cake, rolling sugared waxed paper in with cake. Wrap in towel and place seam-side down on wire rack until cool, about 30 minutes.
To prepare cake roll, carefully unroll cake and spread with whipped cream, jelly or other filling. Reroll. Place on serving plate. Chill. Just before serving dust with confectioners sugar, if desired.
Chocolate Sponge Roll: Combine 4 cup cocoa with 1 cup confectioners sugar. Add to beaten egg yolks and proceed as directed above.
Note: If prepared in advance, cake may be frozen without filling. Wrap well with aluminum foil or plastic wrap. To thaw, let wrapped cake stand at room temperature 1 hour.

name: Pound Cake
author: Ginny Robert
instructions:
Sift together flour, salt and nutmeg. Set aside. In large mixing bowl, beat together butter and 1 1/2 cups sugar at medium speed until light and fluffy. Add yolks all at once and beat until thoroughly blended. Gradually blend flour mixture, 3/4 cup at a time, into butter- yolk mixture. Set aside.
Wash and dry beaters. Beat egg whites and cream of tartar at high speed until foamy. Gradually add remaining 1/2 cup sugar, 1 tablespoon at a time, beating constantly until sugar is dissolved and whites are glossy and stand in soft peaks. Beat in vanilla. Gently but thoroughly fold egg whites into flour mixture. Pour 4 cups batter into each of two greased and floured 9 x 5 x 3 inch loaf pans. Spread evenly. Bake in preheated 325° oven until cake tester inserted in center comes out clean, 55 to 60 minutes. Cool on wire racks 10 minutes. Remove from pans and cool completely.

name: Sally's Strawberry Upside Down Cake
author: Sally Deevers
instructions: Mix strawberries and sugar and let stand 1 to 1 1/2 hours. Put mini marshmallows in bottom of 9 x 13 inch pan. Make white cake mix following directions on box. Pour over marshmallows. Pour strawberries over cake mix. Sprinkle Jell-O on top. Bake at 350° for 35 to 45 minutes. Serve upside down with Cool Whip.

name: Strawberry Cake
author: Sister Celest Compas
instructions: Mix all ingredients thoroughly except eggs. Add eggs beating well after each addition. Bake in a greased and floured 13x9x2 inch pan. Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes.

name: Strawberry Cake (Icing)
author: Sister Celest Compas
instructions: Mix well and pour over hot cake.

name: Strawberry Cake
author: Charlotte Hooper

ingredients.name: pkg. white or yellow cake mix

instructions: Bake cake mix as directed on box. Dissolve Jell-O in water. After cake is cooled, poke holes and pour Jell-O mixture over cake. Refrigerate for 1 hour. Then add the topping. Variations: Use lemon cake and lime Jell-O with lemon pudding.

name: Strawberry Cake (Topping)
author: Charlotte Hooper
instructions: Mix pudding and milk together until smooth. Add Cool Whip and mix well. Spread on cooled cake.

name: Sunshine Cake
author: In Memory of Ella I. Schlosser
instructions: Beat whites until stiff and flaky. Then sift in 1/2 the sugar. Combine yolks and white mixture, then sift in flour and cream of tartar that have been sifted together. Bake 50 to 60 minutes in a slow oven using an angel food cake pan.

name: Sharen's Yum Yum Cake
author: S. & R.P.
instructions: Mix together. Pour in oblong cake pan. Bake at 350° for 40 to 50 minutes.

name: Sharen's Yum Yum Cake (Icing)
author: S. & R.P.
instructions: Put ingredients in saucepan. Bring to a boil and boil for 2 minutes. Remove from heat and add nuts, coconut, and vanilla. Pour immediately over cake while hot.

name: Icing for Sweet Rolls, Cakes or Cookies
author: Charlotte Hooper
instructions: Mix Crisco and cake mix. Add powdered sugar, water and flavoring. Mix well until smooth. Use on rolls, cakes or cookies.

name: Butter-Cream Vanilla Frosting
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Combine butter, salt, vanilla and 1 cup sugar. Add milk and remaining sugar. Mix until smooth. Add sugar to thicken, milk to thin.

name: Butter Cream Icing
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Beat together until smooth.

name: Chocolate Frosting
author: Shirley Drury

ingredients.name: c. Crisco shortening (or butter or margarine)

instructions: Beat together until smooth.

name: Chocolate Frosting
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Add milk if necessary to make a soft spreading.

name: Quick Fudge Frosting
author: Shirley Drury

ingredients.name: c. (3 sticks) soft butter or margarine

instructions: In mixing bowl mix thoroughly powdered sugar, cocoa, and salt. Add boiling water, vanilla, and butter to first mixture. Blend, then beat with mixer or spoon until smooth and thickened. If you wish to speed up thickening, set bowl in ice water while beating. If frosting stiffens too quickly while spreading, just stir in a few drops of hot water. Makes about 2 cups--enough to frost tops and sides of two 8 or 9 inch layers.

name: No Cook Marshmallow Frosting
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Beat egg whites and salt with beater until soft peaks form. Add sugar, about 1 tablespoon at a time, beating until smooth and glossy. Continue beating and add Karo syrup, a little at a time, beating after each addition, until frosting peaks. Fold in vanilla. Makes enough to frost two 9 inch layers.

name: Marshmallow Creamy Icing
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Cook the milk and flour in a double boiler. Set aside to cool. Beat the margarine and sugar about 8 minutes. Add the vanilla and beat about 4 minutes more. Add the marshmallow cream, sugar, milk mixture and beat 4 more minutes.

name: Fast Creamy Peanut Butter Frosting
author: Donna Stamp
instructions: Blend Crisco and peanut butter thoroughly. Alternately add milk and sugar. Frosts two 9 inch layer cakes or one 13 x 9 inch cake.

name: Smooth 'N Creamy Frosting
author: Martha J. Hamm

ingredients.name: pkg. (4 serving size) instant pudding, any flavor
container (8 oz.) Cool Whip non-dairy whipped topping, thawed

instructions:
Combine pudding mix, sugar, and milk in small bowl. Beat slow- ly with rotary beater or at lowest speed of an electric mixer until well blended, about 1 minute. Fold in whipped topping. Spread on cake at once. Makes about 4 cups or enough for two 9-inch layers.
Note: Store frosted cake in refrigerator.

name: Whip Cream Icing
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Cook the milk and flour in a double boiler and set aside to get cold. Beat the oleo and sugar for 8 minutes. Add vanilla and beat 4 more minutes. Add flour and milk mixture and beat more minutes. Note: 1/2 c. drained crushed pineapple, 1⁄2 c. coconut, or 2 c. chopped nuts may be added into mixture as a final step.

name: Mock Whip Cream Icing
author: Juanita Dannenmueller
instructions: Mix flour and milk and stir. Cook until thick. Set aside to cool. In mixer beat oleo, shortening, and sugar until creamy. Add paste, vanilla, and salt. Mix all together and beat until creamy.

name: Frosted Banana Bars
author: Jennifer Kenkel
instructions: In a mixing bowl, cream butter and sugar. Beat in eggs, bananas and vanilla. Combine the flour, baking soda and salt; add to creamed mixture and mix well. Pour into a greased 15 x 10 x 1 inch baking pan. Bake at 350° for 25 minutes or until bars test done. Cool.

name: Frosted Banana Bars (Frosting)
author: Jennifer Kenkel
instructions: Cream butter and cream cheese in a mixing bowl. Gradually add confectioners sugar and vanilla; beat well. Spread over bars, when cool.

name: Streusel Bars
author: Lorena Essner
instructions: Combine flour, brown sugar, and salt. Cut in butter or margarine with pastry blender until mixture is crumbly. Stir in oats. Save 1 1⁄2 cups of crumbly mixture for topping. Press remaining mixture evenly over bottom of oblong baking pan (13 x 9 x 2). Spread jelly, jam, or preserves over crumbs and top with remaining crumb mixture. Press down lightly. Bake in moderate oven at 375° until lightly browned about 25 minutes. Cool. Cut into bars 3 inches long and 1 inch wide.

name: Brickle Bars
author: Louise Alderman
instructions: Mix together cake mix, butter and 1 egg. Press in bottom of 13 x 9 inch pan. Mix together condensed milk, egg, vanilla and add pecans and brickle bits. Pour over mixture in pan. Bake at 350° for 25 to 35 minutes.

name: Ramona's Apricot Brownies
author: Ramona Glastetter
instructions: Melt chocolate and butter over low heat, stirring constantly until all of chocolate is melted. Remove from heat; stir in brown sugar, eggs and vanilla until blended. Set aside. In another bowl, mix flour, baking powder and salt. Stir in chocolate mixture. Combine apricots, almonds, and coconut; stir half into the batter. Pour into a greased 9-inch square baking pan. Sprinkle remaining apricot mixture on top. Bake at 350° for 25 minutes or until golden brown. Cool.

name: Black Forest Cherry Cobbler
author: Linda Shelton
instructions: Spread cherry pie filling in 9 x 13 inch pan. Prepare brownie mix as directed on package. Pour over pie filling and bake at 350° for 30 minutes. Serve warm with ice cream.

name: Swirl Brownies
author: Donna Stamp
instructions: Prepare brownie mix as directed on package. Combine cream cheese and sugar, mixing until well blended. Blend in egg and vanilla. Reserve 1⁄2 cup of batter; spread remaining batter onto bottom of greased 13 x 9 inch baking pan. Cover with cream cheese mixture, spoon on reserved batter. Cut through batter with knife several times for marbled effect. Bake at 350°, 35 to 40 minutes or until cream cheese mixture is lightly browned. Cool; cut into squares.

name: Easy Brownies
author: Donna Stamp
instructions: Put all ingredients, except nuts, in large mixing bowl. Mix well with large spoon. Add nuts and stir. Spread in 9 x 13 inch pan. Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes.

name: Fudge Brownies
author: M.E.
instructions: In mixing bowl combine sugar, margarine, eggs, and vanilla; beat on medium speed until thoroughly combined. Stir in fudge topping, stir in nuts, flour, cocoa and baking powder until combined. Pour into a greased 13 x 9 inch pan. Bake at 350° for 50 minutes or until toothpick comes out clean. Cool on wire rack, cut.

name: Brownies
author: Ruth Schlosser
instructions: Cream sugar and margarine, beat in eggs each seperately. Add syrup, flour, salt, vanilla and nuts mixing thoroughly. Bake in 13 x 9 inch pan at 350° for 25 minutes.

name: Texas Brownies
author: Donna Menz
instructions: In a large bowl combine the flour and sugar. In a saucepan com- bine oleo, shortening, water and cocoa. Stir and heat to boiling. Pour boiling mixture over the flour and sugar. Add the buttermilk, eggs, baking soda and vanilla. Mix well using a high speed mixer. Pour in a well buttered 17 1⁄2 x 11 inch jelly roll pan. Bake at 400° for 20 minutes or until brownies test done in the center.

name: Texas Brownies (Frosting)
author: Donna Menz
instructions: While brownies bake, prepare the frosting. In a saucepan combine the oleo, cocoa and milk. Heat to boiling, stirring constantly. Mix in the powdered sugar and vanilla until frosting is smooth. Pour warm frosting over brownies as soon as you take them out of the oven. Cool and cut into bars.

name: Caramel Nut Bars
author: Louise Alderman
instructions: Combine the first six ingredients; sprinkle 1 cup into a greased 13 x 9 inch baking pan, (do not press). Bake at 350° for 10 minutes. In the top of a double boiler over boiling water, cook and stir caramels and milk until caramels are melted. Pour over crust. Top with chocolate chips and nuts. Sprinkle with remaining oat mixture. Bake at 350° for 10 minutes. Cool on a wire rack. Refrigerate to set the caramel.

name: Chocolate Peanut Butter Treats
author: Vernita Bles
instructions: In a large saucepan or microwave safe bowl, melt butter and marshmallows. Remove from the heat, stir in peanut butter. Gradually add cereal. mix until well-coated. Spread and press into a greased 9 x 13 inch pan, set aside. In a microwave safe bowl or the top of a double boiler over simmering water, melt the chips. Spread over cereal mixture. Cover and freeze for 15 to 20 minutes or until chocolate is set.

name: Double Chocolate Crumble Bars
author: D.S.G.
instructions: Cream together margarine and sugar. Add eggs and vanilla, mixing well. Add flour, cocoa, baking powder and nuts. Spread on greased 9 x 13 inch pan and bake 350° for 15 minutes. Remove from oven and sprinkle marshmallows over top. Return to oven for three minutes. In large sauce pan melt chocolate chips with peanut butter. Add crisp rice cereal and spread over top of baked mixture. Refrigerate or put in a very cool place. Then cut in bars.

name: Hello Dolly Cookies
author: Charlotte Hooper
instructions: Mix butter and crumbs until well coated. Pat into large cookie sheet. Top with coconut, chocolate chips and nuts. Then pour milk evenly over layers. Bake at 350° for 15 minutes or until mixture is bubbly.

name: Seven Layer Cookies (Hello Dollies)
author: K.S.
instructions: Melt butter in bottom of pan. Add as listed above in order on top of butter. Bake 30 minutes at 350°.

name: Lemon Bars
author: Donna Menz
instructions: Sift together 2 cups of flour and powdered sugar. Cut in butter or oleo until mixture clings. Press into a 13 x 9 inch pan and bake at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes or until brown. Cool. Beat together eggs, sugar and lemon juice. Sift together the 1/4 cup of flour and baking powdered, stir into egg mixture. Pour over oven baked crust. Bake at 350° for 25 minutes. Sprinkle with additional powdered sugar, cool and cut into bars.

name: Mud Hen Bars
author: Helen Menz and Donna Menz
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°. Cream oleo and sugar. Beat in the whole egg and 2 egg yolks. Sift flour, baking powder and salt together. Com- bine the 2 mixtures, blend thoroughly. Spread into a 9 x 13 inch pan. Sprinkle nuts, chocolate chips and marshmallows over batter. Beat 2 egg whites stiff, fold in brown sugar. Spread over top of cake. Bake 30 to 40 minutes. Cut into bars.

name: Payday Cake Bars
author: Shari Landewe
instructions: Step one, mix cake mix, melted butter and egg in mixing bowl. Spread in 9 x 13 inch ungreased cake pan. Bake at 300° for 15 minutes. Step two, spread marshmallows over baked cake and bake for 3 more minutes. Step three, melt corn syrup, chips, and vanilla. Add peanuts and Rice Krispies. Spread over marshmallow layer. Let cool and cut into bars.

name: Peanut Butter Cups
author: Rita Koeppel
instructions: Crush graham crackers. Can use food processor, or can use rolling pin with crackers in a bread bag. Mix crackers, sugar, butter and peanut butter. Pat in a 9 x 13 inch pan. Melt chocolate chips and spread over cracker mixture. Let chocolate partially harden and then cut into pieces.

name: Peanut Butter Cornflake Bars
author: Gale Ledure
instructions: Over low heat mix syrup and sugar until sugar dissolves. Add peanut butter until syrupy texture. If dry add a little butter. Pour over cornflakes and mix well. Press firmly into buttered pan. Cut before they harden.

name: Peanut Butter Cornflake Bars
author: Charlotte Hooper
instructions: Mix sugar and corn syrup in microwave safe bowl. Microwave on high for 4 minutes. Stir well. Then cook another 4 minutes on high. Softened peanut butter. Add peanut butter to syrup mixture. Stir well. Pour over cornflakes and mix well. Pour in buttered cookie sheet. Let cool and cut in squares.

name: Double Peanut Cookie Bars
author: Annita Layton

ingredients.name: c. plus 2 Tbsp. margarine or butter
pkg. (12 oz.) peanut butter flavored pieces

instructions: Preheat oven to 350°. Mix crumbs and butter and press into 13 x 9 inch pan with greased sides. Pour sweetened condensed milk over crumbs. Sprinkle with peanut butter chips, chocolate chips and pea- nuts. Press peanuts gently into mixture. Bake 25 minutes or until edges are golden brown. I use less peanut butter chips (1 1⁄2 cups to 1 3/4 cups) and slightly more peanuts (1 1/4 cups to 1 1⁄2 cups). This is always better the next day.

name: Pecan Pie Bars
author: Shirley Eftink
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°. Reserve 2/3 cup cake mix. Combine remaining mix with oleo and 1 egg. Mix well. Pour in greased 9 x 13 inch pan. Bake 15 to 20 minutes until golden brown. Combine 2/3 cup cake mix with brown sugar, syrup, vanilla and 3 eggs. Mix well. Pour over baked crust. Sprinkle with pecans. Bake 40 minutes.

name: Strawberry Pizza Pie (Crust)
author: Louise Alderman
instructions: Mix and press in two pizza pans. Bake at 325° for 10 minutes.

name: Strawberry Pizza Pie (Filling)
author: Louise Alderman
instructions: Mix together and spread on cool crust.

name: Strawberry Pizza Pie (Topping)
author: Louise Alderman
instructions: Cook until thick. Cool. Add strawberries. Spread on top of cream cheese and top with Cool Whip.

name: Fruit Pizza
author: Rebecca Hooper

ingredients.name: doz. sugar cookies (home made or store bought)
pkg. Strawberry Glaze Whipped cream, optional

instructions: Roll cookies out on a cookie sheet. Bake, then let cool. Top with a mixture of cheese, sugar and vanilla. Top with strawberry glaze and any kind of fresh fruit. Then add nuts and whipped cream if desired.

name: Vanilla Chip Fruit Tart
author: Rebecca Hooper
instructions: Beat the butter and powdered sugar until fluffy. Add the flour. Press into a 12-inch pizza pan. Bake in a preheated 300° oven for 20 to 25 minutes or until browned. While this is baking, combine milk chips and whipping cream and microwave until smooth. Beat in the cream cheese. Pour this mixture on the cooled cookie crust. Mix sugar and cornstarch in a saucepan. Stir in pineapple and lemon juices. Cook and stir until thickened. While this is cooking, peel, clean and arrange fresh fruit on top of the cream cheese mixture on the crust. Now drizzle the cooled cornstarch mixture over the fresh fruit and serve.

name: Vanilla Chip Fruit Tart (Crust)
author: Annita Layton

ingredients.name: c. (1 1/2 sticks) butter or margarine, softened

instructions: Heat oven to 300°. In small mixer bowl, beat butter and powdered sugar until smooth; blend in flour. Press mixture onto bottom and up side of 12 inch round pizza pan. Flute edge, if desired. Bake 20 to 25 minutes or until lightly browned; cool completely.

name: Vanilla Chip Fruit Tart (Vanilla Filling)
author: Annita Layton
instructions: In microwave safe bowl, place milk chips and whipping cream. Microwave at HIGH 1 to 1 1⁄2 minutes or until chips are melted and mixture is smooth when stirred vigorously. Beat in softened cream cheese. Spread on cooled crust. Refrigerate.

name: Vanilla Chip Fruit Tart (Fruit Topping)
author: Annita Layton
instructions: In small sauce pan, stir together sugar and cornstarch; stir in juices. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly until thickened; cool. Meanwhile, arrange fruit on top of filling; carefully pour or brush juice mixture over fruit. Cover, refrigerate assembled tart until just before serving.

name: Skillet Cookies
author: Anna Rose Bles
instructions: Melt oleo in skillet; add brown sugar, chopped dates, egg and vanilla. Boil for 2 minutes. Take off stove; add chopped nuts and Rice Krispies. Mix well. Let cool enough to handle. Drop by teaspoonfuls into coconut; turn to coat. Place on wax paper to cool.

name: Layered Fruit Bars
author: Karla Essner
instructions:
Cream margarine, brown sugar, and vanilla in large bowl at medium speed of electric mixer until light and fluffy. Mix in flour and salt. Reserve 1⁄2 cup of mixture and 1 cup of quick rolled oats. Press remaining mixture evenly in ungreased 13 x 9 inch pan. Bake at 375° for 10 minutes.

Fillings
Lime-Cream Cheese: Beat 8 ounces of cream cheese, 2 table- spoons of lime juice, 1 egg and 1⁄2 cup granulated sugar until smooth. Spread over baked crust.
Cherry or Blueberry: Spread 1 can (21 ounces) desired flavor pie filling over baked crust.
Pineapple-Coconut: Combine two 8 ounces ounces cans crushed pineapple, 1⁄2 cup granulated sugar and 1 tablespoon cornstarch in medium saucepan. Cook on medium heat until thickened, stirring constantly. Stir in 1/4 cup chopped pecans, 1⁄2 cup flake coconut and 1 teaspoon lemon juice. Spread over baked crust.
Combine reserved mixture and rolled oats, mixing until crumbly. After filling is spread over baked base, sprinkle topping over filling. Bake at 375° for 15 minutes. Cool. Cut into bars, about 2 1⁄2 x 1 inches. Refrigerate.

name: Almond Butter Cookies
author: In memory of Hazel Monsignor Ray Orf's housekeeper
instructions: Beat well, margarine, cream cheese, baking powder, salt and 1/2 cup sugar. Add 1 teaspoon almond extract and flour. Then mix well. Mix remaining sugar and almost extract together, set aside. Roll the dough rectangle shape about 1/4 thick. Sprinkle with sugar and fold in half again. Continue until you are left with a small rectangle. Slice and bake 350 degrees for 10 to 12 minutes.

name: Lemon Bars
author: Shari Landewe
instructions: Mix together cake mix, oil, and 1 egg until crumbly. Reserve 1 cup for topping. Press the rest into a greased 13 x 9 inch pan. Bake at 350° for 12 minutes. In a separate bowl, beat cream cheese, 1/3 cup sugar, lemon juice and 1 egg. When crumb mixture is done, spread cream cheese mixture over the top. Mix 1/3 cup of sugar with reserved crumb mixture. Sprinkle on top of cream cheese and bake 12 minutes more. Let cool, then chill before cutting.

name: Orange Slice Bars
author: Ginny Robert

ingredients.name: lb. orange slices, cut in small pieces

instructions: Mix orange slices, flour and salt. Add remaining ingredients and mix well. Pour in greased cookie sheet pan and bake in 350° oven about 35 minutes or until brown.

name: Angel Crisps
author: In Memory of Aunt Mary Welter
instructions: Cream sugar, shortening and vanilla. Add sifted dry ingredients. Form into balls size of walnut. Dip top half in water, then in white sugar. Press dough in center with finger. Place on ungreased baking sheet. Bake at 425° for 8 to 10 minutes.

name: Applesauce Cookies
author: In Memory of Ella I. Schlosser
instructions: Cream together lard and sugar. Stir in egg. Sift together flour, baking powder, salt, soda, cinnamon, cloves and nutmeg. Mix in raisins and oats. Add to creamed mixture in 3 portions alternating with applesauce in 2 portions. Beat well. Drop from teaspoon. Bake at 375° for 10 to 15 minutes.

name: Bits 'O Brickle Cookies
author: Ellen R.
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°. In a small bowl mix Bits 'O Brickle with liquid shortening until evenly coated, then stir in 6 tablespoons of flour until well coated; set aside. In a large bowl, combine butter, sugar and brown sugar and vanilla; beat until creamy. Beat in egg. Gradually add salt, baking soda and flour, mix well. Stir in coated Bits. Drop to 12 minutes. Makes 50 cookies. by rounded teaspoons onto greased cookie sheets. Bake at 325° for 10 to 12 minutes.

name: Cake Mix Cookies
author: Donna Essner
instructions: Mix all ingredients. Chill in refrigerator for a couple of hours. Roll in balls and then in powder sugar. Bake at 350° for 9 to 10 minutes.

name: Louise's Cake Mix Cookies
author: Louise Maria Blankenship

ingredients.name: pkg. of your favorite cake mix

instructions: Mix all ingredients together. Drop by teaspoonfuls of dough about 2 inches apart on ungreased cookie sheets. Place in an oven that has been preheated to 350°. Bake for 10 minutes, then cool.

name: Caramel Apple Cookies
author: Shirley Drury

ingredients.name: c. apple juice or orange juice

instructions: Cream shortening, sugar and egg until light and fluffy. Sift together dry ingredients and add to creamed mixture. When well blended, stir in remaining ingredients. Drop by level tablespoons 3 inches apart onto greased baking sheet. Bake in moderate oven at 350° about 12 minutes.

name: Caramel Apple Cookies (Frosting)
author: Shirley Drury

ingredients.name: Tbsp. dairy half and half or light cream

instructions: Combine butter and brown sugar in saucepan. Cook until sugar is dissolved about three minutes. Add confectioners sugar, salt and light cream. Beat until smooth. Spread on cooled cookies.

name: Cherry Winks
author: Shirley Drury

ingredients.name: c. chopped cherries or maraschino cherries, quartered

instructions: Sift dry ingredients together. Set aside. Blend Crisco and sugar, creaming well. Add eggs. milk and vanilla, beating well. Blend in the dry ingredients gradually. Mix thoroughly. Add pecans, dates, and cup of cherries. Mix well. Drop by teaspoonful into crushed cornflakes. Roll into balls. Place on greased baking sheet. Top each cookie with 1/4 cherry. Bake in 375° oven for 12 to 15 minutes.

name: No Bake Cookies
author: Donna Essner
instructions: Combine sugar, milk, margarine and cocoa in sauce pan and bring to a boil. Boil one minute. Remove from heat, beat in quickly oats, peanut butter and vanilla. Spread in a cookie sheet pan and let cool. Cut into bars.

name: Chocolate Drop Cookies
author: In Memory of Ella I. Schlosser
instructions: Place butter, sugar and egg in bowl and beat until creamy. Add melted chocolate. Add dry ingredients, alternately with milk. Chill for a few minutes. Drop from a spoon on a greased cookie sheet. Bake 400° for 10 minutes or less.

name: Chocolate Covered Cherry Cookies (Cookie Dough)
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Cream butter and sugar until light. Add egg and vanilla. Mix in dry ingredients. Shape dough into 1 inch balls, using a heaping tea- spoon of dough for each. Place 2 inches apart on ungreased cookie sheet. Push one cherry halfway in each ball. When cookies are molded and cherries are pushed in, prepare frosting and use immediately. Frost each cherry by spreading 1⁄2 teaspoon over each cherry. Bake frosted cookies at 350° for 8 to 10 minutes until puffy.

name: Chocolate Covered Cherry Cookies (Frosting)
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: In a small heavy sauce pan, over low heat, melt chocolate pieces with condensed milk, stirring constantly. Remove from heat, add remaining ingredients, stir until smooth.

name: Chocolate Kiss Cookies
author: Rachael Schlosser
instructions: Heat oven to 375°. In a large bowl, combine 1/2 cup sugar, brown sugar, shortening and peanut butter until creamy. Add egg, milk and vanilla, blend well. Mix flour, soda and salt. Roll small spoonfuls of dough into 1 inch balls, then roll balls in sugar. Place on ungreased cookie sheet and bake for 10 to 12 minutes or until golden brown. As soon as they come out of the oven, press a chocolate kiss into the center. Cool and eat.

name: Reese's Chewy Chocolate Cookies
author: Louise Alderman
instructions: Heat oven to 350°. Grease 15 1⁄2 x 10 1/2 x 1 inch jelly roll pan. In large bowl, beat butter and sugar until fluffy. Add eggs and vanilla; beat well. Stir together flour, cocoa, baking soda and salt. Gradually blend into butter mixture. Stir in peanut butter chips. Spread batter into pan. Bake 20 minutes or until set. Cool completely in pan on wire rack. Cut into bars.

name: Chocolate Chip Cookies
author: Juanita Dannenmueller
instructions: Heat oven to 375°. Mix thoroughly shortening, butter, sugars, eggs and vanilla. Blend in remaining ingredients. Drop dough by rounded teaspoonfuls 2 inches apart onto ungreased baking sheet. Bake 8 to 10 minutes or until light brown. Cool slightly before removing from baking sheet.

name: Chocolate Chip Treasure Cookies
author: Mary Ann Lumsden

ingredients.name: pkg. (12 oz.) semi-sweet chocolate chips (2 cups)

instructions: Heat oven to 375°. In small bowl, mix graham cracker crumbs, flour and baking powder. In large bowl, beat sweetened condensed milk and margarine until smooth. Add graham crumb mixture. Mix well, Add coconut, chocolate chips and nuts. Drop by rounded table- spoons onto ungreased cookie sheets. Bake 9 to 10 minutes or until lightly browned. Store loosely covered at room temperature.

name: Chocolate Chip Cookies Made With Betty Crocker Cake Mix
author: Martha J. Hamm
instructions: Heat oven to 375°. Beat eggs, vanilla, shortening and about 1⁄2 of the cake mix (dry) until light and fluffy. Stir in remaining cake mix, the chocolate chips and nuts. Drop dough by teaspoonfuls about 2 inches apart onto ungreased baking sheet. Bake 10 to 12 minutes at 375°. (Cookies will be soft in centers when done.) Cool slightly before removing from baking sheet. Makes about 5 dozen cookies. Our fami- ly favorite is to substitute peanut butter chips for the chocolate chips and use German Chocolate Cake Mix to make very good cookies. Suggested cake mixes: Yellow, Devil's Food, White, Butter Rec- ipe, Sour Cream, Chocolate Fudge, Chocolate Fudge Supreme.

name: Chocolate Chip Cookies
author: S.M.
instructions: Cream butter, sugars, eggs and vanilla. Add dry ingredients and mix well. Then add chocolate chips, Hershey bar and nuts. Drop by teaspoonfuls onto ungreased cookie sheet. Bake 5 to 6 minutes at 375°.

name: Blue Ribbon Chocolate Chip Cookies
author: Ruth Schlosser
instructions: Mix in large bowl, first 5 ingredients with electric mixer until creamy. Add salt, baking soda and flour, mixing well. Add chocolate chips and nuts. Drop by VERY OVERLOADED teaspoons onto ungreased cookie sheet. Bake in 350° oven for 12 minutes. Cool on aluminum foil. Other varieties of chips can be used as desire. THIS WON A BLUE RIBBON AT THE SOUTHEAST MISSOURI STATE FAIR.

name: Cinnamon Disks
author: Anna Rose Bles
instructions: Cream margarine, sugar and vanilla. Add egg. Cream. Add dry ingredients. Mix well Roll in balls. Roll in cinnamon and nut mixture. Bake at 375° until done.

name: Coconut Macaroons
author: Dorothy Glastetter

ingredients.name: pkg. (16 oz.) Angel Food Cake Mix

instructions: Preheat oven to 350°. Mix cake mix, almond extract and water together for 3 minutes on medium speed. Stir in coconut. May need to add small about of flour. Drop by scant teaspoon onto foil lined cookie sheets, which are sprayed with non stick cooking spray. Bake 7-9 minute or until edges are light brown. Cool completely before removing from foil. Best made with the one-step cake mix.

name: Coconut Oatmeal Cookies
author: Irene Blattel
instructions: Sift flour, baking powder, salt and soda. Cream butter, add sug- ars gradually, cream until fluffy. Add vanilla and eggs; beat well. Add flour mixture gradually, beating until smooth after each addition. Mix in oats and coconut; add butterscotch chips, if desired. Drop from tea- spoon onto ungreased cookie sheets. Bake at 375° for 9 to 12 minutes.

name: Coconut Balls
author: Annita Layton
instructions: Mix together and chill. Roll in small balls and chill again. Melt 12 ounce bag chocolate chips and 1/4 pound paraffin wax. Dip balls and put on waxed paper to harden.

name: Coconut Macaroons
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Beat the egg whites until fluffy. Stir in sugar, salt and vanilla. Blend in the coconut. Drop by teaspoonfuls 2 inches apart on ungreased wrapping paper on baking sheet. Bake until set and deli- cately browned. They spread during baking, so when they come from oven, shape into mounds by gathering in edges with fingers. Bake at 325° for 15 to 18 minutes.

name: Coconut Cookies
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Mix all ingredients together. Drop by teaspoonful on to well greased cookie sheet. Bake at 350° for 10 to 12 minutes.

name: Cowboy Cookies
author: Juanita Dannenmueller

ingredients.name: pkg. chocolate chips or butterscotch chips

instructions: Cream margarine and sugars. Add eggs, vanilla. Add dry ingre- dients to mixture. Mix in oats, then chips and coconut. Bake at 325° for 10 to 12 minutes.

name: Crunch Cookies
author: Donna Scherer
instructions: Cream oleo and sugars. Add eggs and vanilla and mix. Add flour, salt, soda, powder and mix. Add oatmeal, pecans, cornflakes. Drop on ungreased cookie sheet. Bake at 350° for 10 to 12 minutes.

name: Dishpan Cookies
author: Donna Stamp
instructions: Sift together flour, baking soda and salt. Combine sugars, vegetable oil and eggs, one at a time and vanilla in a very large bowl. (Dish- pan) Mix well. Add remaining ingredients and mix until thoroughly blended. Drop by teaspoonful onto a greased cookie sheet. Bake at 325° for 8 to 10 minutes, or until light brown.

name: Funfetti Cookies
author: Linda Menz
instructions: Mix well with fork and roll into balls. Place on greased cookie sheet. Flatten with glass cup dipped in flour. Bake at 375° for 6 minutes. Roll in sugar when cooled, slightly.

name: Hawaiian Drop Cookies
author: Emma Nichols and Donna Menz
instructions: Sift flour, baking powder and salt together. Cream shortening, sugar and extracts thoroughly. Beat in egg until mixture is fluffy. Blend in pineapple and dry ingredients. Drop by teaspoonfuls on ungreased cookie sheet 3 inches apart. Sprinkle with coconut. Bake in a 325° oven for about 20 minutes.

name: Hermits
author: In Memory of Helen T. Schlosser
instructions: Mix eggs, lard, sugar, raisins, cloves and cinnamon. Add just enough flour to make soft. dough. Roll out dough on floured board as thin as possible. Cut and place on greased baking pan. Bake at 350° until done.

name: Jelly Bean Jollies
author: Shirley Drury

ingredients.name: c. firmly packed light brown sugar
c. jelly beans, cut up (gumdrops can be used)

instructions: Cream together shortening and sugars. Beat in egg, baking soda, baking powder, salt and vanilla. Stir in flour and oats until blended. Add jelly beans. Heat oven to 375°. Drop by rounded spoonfuls of bat- ter about 2 inches apart on lightly greased cookie sheet. Bake 10 to 12 minutes or until lightly browned.

name: Lep Cookies
author: Helen Raines

ingredients.name: Tbsp. each nutmeg, cinnamon and cloves

instructions: Mix in following manner: Take molasses and lard and put in large pan on stove and let it get warm. Mix and let cool stirring constantly. Mix sugar and eggs. Take soda and mix in 1⁄2 cup of boiling water and add to previous mixture. Take raisins and nuts and dredge with 1 cup of flour. Mix them in and last add spices, flour and salt. Add enough flour to make soft dough. Roll out on lightly floured board and cut with doughnut cutter. Bake at 300° until light brown. Baking time is about 15 minutes. Recipe makes 5 gallon can full. It takes about 8 pounds of flour to make these cookies. They will be hard when first baked, will keep up to a year and soften as they age. Keep in covered container in which a tea towel has been laid into the bottom and then wrap it around cookies before putting on the lid. This recipe is over 100 years old. It is the recipe of Marylan Diebold's Great Grandmother.

name: Melt In Your Mouth Cookies
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Mix all ingredients together and drop by teaspoon on cookie sheet, flatten with glass dipped in a little oil, then put a little sugar and a pecan on top. Bake 350° for 8 to 10 minutes. These are very light and makes a large batch.

name: Polka Dot Macaroons
author: Annita Layton
instructions: Beat salt and egg whites until foamy. Gradually beat in sugar till stiff peaks form. Fold in vanilla, cornflakes and chocolate chips. Drop by teaspoonfuls onto greased cookie sheets. Bake at 350° 18 to 20 minutes.

name: Molasses Cookies
author: Donna Essner

ingredients.name: c. boiling water or sour milk

instructions: Dissolve baking soda in boiling water or sour milk. Then add other ingredients. Mix and bake at 350°.

name: Molasses Drop Cookies
author: In Memory of Anna Diebold
instructions: Melt lard. Add molasses and eggs. Stir well. Sift flour with bak- ing powder, salt, soda, and spices. Add half the sifted dry ingredients and milk alternately beating well after each addition. Add flavoring. Drop by spoonful and bake at 375° for 8 to 10 minutes.

name: Sandies
author: Anna Rose Bles
instructions: Cream together first 4 ingredients, then add flour and nuts. Chill 4 hours. Shape into balls and bake at 325° about 20 minutes. Cool slightly and roll in powdered sugar.

name: Nut Butter Balls
author: Ryan Hooper Brock
instructions: Cream butter, sugar and salt. Add flour, vanilla and nuts. Mix well. Roll into balls and bake 3 to 5 minutes at 350°. Then roll in powdered sugar while still hot.

name: Oh So Good Oatmeal Cookies
author: Michelle Kenkel Mohney
instructions: Sift flour, salt, baking powder and soda together. Cream shortening and brown sugar. Add beaten eggs and vanilla and beat well. Stir in sifted dry ingredients and oats. Chill dough. Form into little balls the size of a walnut. Roll in powdered sugar until heavily coated. Place 2 inches apart on greased cookie sheet. Put pecan in center of each. Bake at 350° for 10 to 12 minutes.

name: Raisin Oatmeal Cookies
author: Anna Marie Burger
instructions:
Sift dry ingredients into bowl. Add shortening, brown sugar, eggs and vanilla. Beat until smooth about 2 minutes. Stir in quick oats and raisins. Drop by teaspoon on greased cookie sheet. Bake at 350°.
I usually soak the raisins in a little warm water while getting the ingredients together. I make powdered sugar icing and dribble it on the cookies when I take them out of the oven.

name: It's So Easy Oatmeal Cookies
author: Irene Blattel
instructions: Mix until fluffy margarine, sugars, eggs, water, vanilla, baking soda and salt. Add all at once flour, oatmeal and chocolate chips. Drop by teaspoonfuls onto lightly greased cookie sheet. Bake at 350° for 10 minutes.

name: Oatmeal Cookies
author: In Memory of Aunt Mary Welter
instructions: Cream shortening, sugars, eggs and vanilla. Beat well. Add flour, salt and soda. Mix well. Add oats and nuts. Mix, then form into long rolls. Chill, slice and bake. Bake in 350° oven for 10 minutes.

name: Oatmeal Ranger Cookies
author: Anna Rose Bles
instructions: Cream shortening with brown and white sugar. Continue creaming until light and fluffy. Add eggs and vanilla, beat well. Add cornflakes and oats. Sift flour, baking powder, salt, and soda. Add to mixture. Add coconut and nuts. Drop by teaspoon onto lightly greased baking sheets, placing cookies 2 inches apart. Bake in 375° oven about 10 minutes.

name: No-Bake Orange Balls
author: Sister Dorothy Reinhold

ingredients.name: box vanilla wafers, (1 lb. 6 oz.), crushed
oz. Florida frozen concentrated orange juice

instructions: Combine vanilla wafer crumbs, coconut, and undiluted orange juice. Mix well. Form one-inch balls. Roll balls in confectioners sugar. Store in covered container overnight.

name: Orange Balls
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Mix all ingredients together. Chill dough for a little while. Then shape into balls and roll in coconut.

name: Peanut Butter Cookies
author: Donna Essner
instructions: In a large bowl, combine first seven ingredients, blend well. Stir in remaining ingredients, blend well. Shape into 1 inch balls. Place 2 inches apart on ungreased cookie sheet. Flatten in crisscross pattern with fork dipped in sugar. Bake at 350° for 7 to 8 minutes or until golden brown. Immediately remove from cookie sheet.

name: Louise's Peanut Butter Kisses
author: Louise Maria Blankenship

ingredients.name: c. granulated sugar, for rolling cookies

instructions: Combine peanut butter, shortening and sugar. Stir in milk, vanilla, and eggs. Add dry ingredients. Mix thoroughly, using your hands if necessary. Shape dough into 1 inch balls, roll in 1/3 cup granu- lated sugar. Place on ungreased baking sheets. Bake at 350° for 10 minutes. Remove from oven and press a chocolate kiss on the center of each cookie. Remove to rack to cool. Make 6 to 7 dozen cookies.

name: Pumpkin Cookies
author: Christine Estes
