instructions: Mix sugar, pumpkin and shortening in separate bowl. Mix dry ingredients. Stir in nuts. Mix in shortening mixture. Drop dough by teaspoon onto cookie sheets (ungreased) Bake 8 to 10 minutes. Immediately remove from cookie sheet. Cool and glaze with powdered sugar icing.

name: Pumpkin Cookies (Glaze)
author: Christine Estes
instructions: Mix all ingredients together

name: Raisin Nut Cookies
author: In Memory of Ella I. Schlosser
instructions: Boil raisins and water together for five minutes. This should boil down to 1⁄2 cup liquid. Cool, add soda to raisins and liquid. Cream butter, then add salt, cinnamon, nutmeg, allspice, white sugar and brown sugar, cream together well. Then add beaten eggs, vanilla and cooled raisin-soda mixture. Mix well. Sift flour with baking powder and add to first mixture. Mix well. Stir in nuts. Chill dough. To bake, drop by teaspoonful on greased cookie sheets. Bake 10 to 12 minutes at 400°.

name: McKeevers' Famous Refrigerator Cookies
author: Sister Pat McKeever
instructions: Put in sauce pan the sugar, milk and margarine. Boil for one minute, Dump mixture into bowl with the following ingredients: oat- meal, peanut butter, vanilla and chocolate. Mix together well, make spoon size drops on wax paper and refrigerate.

name: Butterscotch Refrigerator Cookies
author: Vernita Bles
instructions: Stir together sugar, shortening and eggs until light. Butter makes fine cookies 1/2 butter, 1⁄2 lard does very well. Sift flour and add with other ingredients. Turn onto large platter and knead into loaf. Set in cool place to chill. Slice off very thin and bake in moderate oven.

name: Russian Teacakes
author: K.H.
instructions: Mix together butter, vanilla and powdered sugar. Sift together flour and salt. Mix in chopped nuts. Chill dough. Roll into one inch balls. Place on ungreased baking sheet (cookies do not spread). Bake until set, but not brown. While still warm, roll in confectioners sugar. Cool. Roll in sugar again. Bake at 400° for 10 to 12 minutes.

name: Amy's Shortbread Cookies
author: Rebecca Hooper
instructions: Cream butter, gradually add powdered sugar, beating until light and fluffy. Stir in flour. (Mixture will be stiff.) Press into 15 x 10 x 1 inch jelly roll pan, prick all over with fork. Chill 30 minutes. Bake at 375° for 5 minutes, reduce heat to 300° and bake 20 minutes more. Sprinkle with sugar.

name: Snickerdoodle Cookies
author: Donna Menz, S.M.
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°. Sift together flour, cream of tarter, baking soda and salt, set aside. In large bowl, with electric mixer on medium, beat shortening until creamy. Gradually beat in the 1 1⁄2 cups of sugar until light and fluffy. Beat in eggs and vanilla. Gradually beat in flour mixture. In small bowl, combine the remaining 1/4 cup sugar and cin- namon. Roll dough into 1 inch balls. Roll balls in sugar-cinnamon mixture. Place on ungreased baking sheet about 2 inches apart. Bake 12 to 15 minutes. Cool completely on wire rack. Makes about 3 1⁄2 dozen cookies.

name: Sugar Cookies
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Beat sugar, butter and eggs until creamy then add rest of ingredients. Chill one hour. Roll out dough and cut with cookie cutters. Bake until done in 375° oven.

name: Grandma's Soft Sugar Cookies
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Beat together white and brown sugars, butter and shortening until light and fluffy. Beat in eggs, vanilla and lemon extract to mix well. Sift together nutmeg, flour, baking powder, cream of tarter, salt and soda. Add alternately with buttermilk to creamed mixture. Drop for 10 minutes. by tablespoons on greased baking sheet, 2 1⁄2 inches apart. Bake at 400°

name: Sugar Cookies
author: Juanita Dannenmueller
instructions: Cream shortening and sugar well. Beat in eggs and vanilla. Gradually blend in dry ingredients which have been sifted together. Chill the dough at least three hours. Roll to 8 or 1/4 inch thickness on a lightly floured pastry canvas. Cut cookies with floured cookie cut- ters. Bake on ungreased cookie sheets at 375° for 8 to 10 minutes.

name: Sugar Cookies (Icing)
author: Laurie Essner
instructions: Add vanilla to confections sugar. Add milk gradually and beat until frosting is of right consistency for decorating or spreading.

name: Sugar Cookie
author: Laurie Essner
instructions: Mix all together. Roll dough on floured board 1/4 inch thick. Bake at 350° for about 8 minutes.

name: Sugar Cookie (Icing)
author: Laurie Essner
instructions: Blend and beat well until light and creamy.

name: Sugar Cookie
author: Charlotte Hooper
instructions: Cream butter and add white sugar and brown sugar. Mix well. Add eggs and vanilla and beat well. Then add cream of tarter, baking soda, and salt. Mix well. Add flour one cup at a time until well blended. Scoop dough into balls with ice cream scoop. Roll in sugar and bake at 375° for 10 to 12 minutes or until golden brown.

name: Zucchini Cookies
author: Helen Raines
instructions: Cream butter and sugar; add egg and vanilla. Add zucchini. Stir in flour, baking powder, cinnamon and salt. Add nuts and chips. Drop dough, using a teaspoon, onto a greased cookie sheet. Bake 15 minutes at 350° until golden brown.

name: Swedish Spritz Cookies
author: Sharen
instructions:
In mixing bowl, beat margarine and sugar until fluffy. Add egg yolk and almond extract, beat well. Beat in flour. Force the unchilled dough through a cookie press onto the ungreased cookie sheet. Bake at 375° for 8 to 10 minutes or until edges are firm but not brown. Cool the baked cookies on wire racks.

Variations:
Nutty Cookies: Stir 1/2 c. ground nuts with the flour, toast nuts before grinding.
Chocolate Cookies: Reduce flour to 2 1/4 cup, add an additional 1/4 cup sugar and 1/4 cup unsweetened cocoa powder. Add powder before flour.

name: Ellen's Vanilla Nut Cookies
author: E.R.
instructions: Mix flour, baking powder and salt. Cream butter thoroughly, add sugars gradually, and cream together until light. Then add eggs, nuts, milk and vanilla. Add flour gradually, mixing well. Shape into rolls, 1 1⁄2 inch in diameter and roll in waxed paper. Chill. Cut into 1/8 inch slices. Bake on ungreased cookie sheet for 10 minutes at 325°.

name: Rock Cookies
author: In Memory of Anna Diebold

ingredients.name: tsp. baking soda dissolved in 1/2 C. warm water

instructions: Mix ingredients together. Add enough flour so cookies fall off spoon. Do not chop nuts. Bake in moderate oven.

name: Splendid Cookies
author: In Memory of Anna Diebold
instructions: Mix ingredients together. Roll out and cut with favorite cookie cutters.

name: Anise Cookies
author: In Memory of Rosa Essner

ingredients.name: Flour, enough to make dough stiff enough to roll out

instructions: Combine eggs and sugar and beat for half an hour. Add butter and continue beating for fifteen minutes. Now add anise oil and beat for another fifteen minutes. Sift hartshorn with 2 cups flour and add to other ingredients. Add sufficient flour to make dough stiff enough to roll and cut cookies. Cut cookies into squares. Place cookies on bread board and let stand in cool room overnight. Bake in slow oven.

name: Gingersnap Cookies
author: Laurie Essner
instructions: Cream shortening until soft; gradually add sugar creaming after each addition until mixture is fluffy. Beat in egg, then add molasses. Measure flour, ginger, soda, cinnamon, and salt into sifter. Sift dry ingredients over creamed mixture and blend well. Form teaspoons of dough into small balls by rolling them lightly one at a time between palms of hands. Roll the dough balls in granulated sugar to cover out- side surfaces. Place 2 inches apart on ungreased cookie sheets. Bake in 350° oven for 12 to 15 minutes or until tops are cracky and lightly browned. Remove from cookie sheets and cool. Store in airtight con- tainers. (Will be best if stored a few weeks to age properly.)

name: Carrot Cookies
author: Marian M. Essner
instructions: Cream oleo. Gradually beat in sugar, salt and vanilla. Beat until fluffy. Add carrots. Sift flour; measure and sift with baking powder. Add to carrot mixture. Drop by teaspoon on lightly buttered cookie sheet. Flatten the cookie dough a little. Bake in preheated 350° oven for 12 to 15 minutes. Frost immediately with orange, orange rind and enough powdered sugar to thicken. Should be thin. These are a healthy cookie.

name: Halloween Cookie Pizza
author: Lorena Essner

ingredients.name: c. Hershey's semi sweet chocolate chips

instructions: Heat oven to 350°. Lightly grease 12 inch round pizza pan. In large mixer bowl, beat sugar and shortening until creamy. Add egg, water, and vanilla; beat well. In separate bowl stir together flour, baking soda and salt. Add to sugar mixture, beating on low speed until well blended. Stir in peanut butter chips. Spread batter in prepared pan to within 1/2 inch of edge. Bake 11 to 13 minutes or until set. Remove from oven. Sprinkle marshmallows, chocolate chips and pecans over top. Bake another 5 to 7 minutes until marshmallows are lightly browned. Can drizzle on top, chocolate and or orange drizzle. Chocolate drizzle: 1/4 cup chocolate chips and 1⁄2 teaspoon Crisco butter flavored, melted. Orange drizzle: 1⁄2 cup powdered sugar and 1 tablespoon water and orange coloring.

name: Chewy Noels
author: Anna Rose Bles
instructions: Melt butter in small baking pan. Beat eggs slightly. Combine sugar, flour, soda and nuts. Stir into eggs and vanilla. Pour into but- tered pan. Do not stir. Bake at 350° for 20 minutes. Cut squares and dust with powdered sugar.

name: Good Neighbor Cookies
author: Ginny Robert
instructions: Beat in eggs and mix well. Gradu- ally add soda, powder and vanilla. Then add salt, oats, cornflakes, coconut and flour. Mix well. Chill dough. Drop by spoonful on greased cookie sheet. Bake 12 minutes at 325°.

name: Caramels
author: Shirley Drury

ingredients.name: c. half and half dairy cream

instructions:
In a 3-quart heavy saucepan, cook sugar, corn syrup, Nulomoline, dairy cream and lecithin. Stir often at the beginning to dissolve the sugar before reaching the boiling point. Bring to a boil on medium to high heat and let cook for about three minutes; add broken pieces of butter and continue to cook on medium to high heat. When temperature reaches 230°, turn heat to medium and begin to stir mixture with a wooden spoon and continue to stir with a steady, even motion until temperature reaches 246°.
Remove from heat and add salt and vanilla, and mix gently with a wooden spoon. If nut caramels are desired, add broken pecan pieces at this point and mix in. Chocolate caramels can also be made by mixing in two squares of melted bitter baking chocolate at this stage.
Caramel mixture can now be poured onto a cool, well buttered or oiled marble surface, framing the caramel with steel bars which have also been buttered or oiled on the side which comes in contact with the hot caramel; or into a well buttered or oiled square or rectangular pan, and placed in a cool place until firm enough to cut. Caramel should be cut into pieces about 3/4 inch square, and either wrapped in wax paper or dipped in chocolate or pastel coating.

name: Buckeyes
author: Anna Rose Bles
instructions: Mix well first three ingredients. Roll into balls the size of buck- eyes, abut 1 inch. Lay on cookie sheet. Chill. Melt chocolate chips and paraffin in double boiler. Coat buckeyes with chocolate. Lay on cook sheet. Chill again.

name: Caramel Candy
author: Lorena Essner
instructions: Melt 1 cup sugar, then add milk. Let cook until all is dissolved. Add remaining sugar and cook until it forms a soft ball in water. Add butter and vanilla and take off stove. Add nuts and beat until creamy, but not too long.

name: Marshmallow Caramel Candy
author: Lorena Essner
instructions: Cook together cream, syrup, sugar, and sweet milk. Cook until it forms a soft ball in water. Cut marshmallows in fourths and roll in cooked filling. Then roll in nuts, coconut or cereal as desired. Place on waxed paper to cool.

name: Coconut Bon Bons
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: In a small pan, heat the corn syrup to quite hot, but do not boil. Then pour into bowl containing the coconut and thoroughly mix the two with a spoon or spatula, then set aside for one hour so the coconut will become well saturated with the corn syrup. Saturated coconut can now be hand rolled into ball, centers for bon bons. It is easier to roll if hands are kept wet while rolling. These centers are not ready for hand dipping in coating. They will however, be easier to dip if set aside for one or two hours after hand rolling. This will let the surface of the ball center dry out and become firm for easy handling. Then dip coco- nut centers in regular chocolate coating.

name: Chocolate Pecan Bark
author: Shirley Drury

ingredients.name: lb. milk or dark dipping chocolate

instructions: Scatter the pecan halves evenly on wax paper on a cookie sheet. Melt chocolate in top section of double boiler as required for hand dipping, then temper. For bark however, it is best to temper the melted chocolate in a bowl by stirring with a spoon or spatula, rather than working with the hand on a flat surface. Place about half of the melted chocolate in a bowl and let stand in a cool area. Cool chocolate down by stirring often until it is a little too cool and stiff to pour freely. Then bring the remainder of melted chocolate from the double boiler into the bowl of cool chocolate, and work constantly with a spoon or spatula until the entire batch of chocolate feels cool to the touch, but is yet in the free-flowing stage. The chocolate is now tempered and is ready for use. Pour over the scattered nuts and spread thin with a knife or spatula, let stand until chocolate sets, then break into irregular pieces. Any chocolate left over can be re-melted and used again. Also other nuts such as cashews, almonds, etc. can be used instead of pecans if desired.

name: Foolproof Dark Chocolate Fudge
author: Rebecca Hooper

ingredients.name: (6 oz.) pkg. semi sweet chocolate chips

instructions: In heavy saucepan, over low heat, melt chips with sweetened condensed milk and salt. Remove from heat; stir in nuts and vanilla. Spread evenly onto wax paper-lined 8 or 9 inch square pan. Chill 2 hours or until firm. Turn fudge onto cutting board; peel off paper and cut into squares. Store loosely covered at room temperature.

name: Turtles
author: Juanita Dannenmueller

ingredients.name: c. chopped pecans or leave whole

instructions: Melt caramel and butter together in microwave, add chopped pecans. Spoon onto buttered cookie sheet or wax paper. Melt chocolate and white bark together. Take hardened caramel pieces and dip in chocolate mixture, set back on cookie sheet until firm.

name: Chocolate Turtles
author: K.M.
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°. On greased baking sheets arrange the pecan halves in groups of 3, flat side down in Y shapes. Place a caramel on top of each cluster, place in the oven until the caramels soften, about 5 to 8 minutes. Remove from oven and flatten the caramels over the pecans with a butter spoon. Cool slightly. Melt the chocolate in the top of a double boiler over simmering water. Dip the turtles into the chocolate and cool on the wax paper. Store in tightly covered containers in a cool place.

name: Low Fat Fudge Surprises
author: Rita Koeppel

ingredients.name: (2 1⁄2 oz.) jar baby food prunes (can't taste them)

instructions: Line a 13 x 9 inch pan with wax paper, extending paper over the edges. Melt butter, stir in sugar and evaporated milk. Bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring constantly. Boil, stirring for five minutes. Remove from heat and slowly stir in chocolate chips until they melt. Stir in remaining ingredients. Spread mixture into prepared pan. Refrigerate until firm. Use the wax paper to lift fudge from pan. Then cut into small pieces.

name: Hard Candy
author: Anna Rose Bles
instructions: Mix the first three ingredients in a saucepan over medium heat until all sugar dissolves. Boil without stirring until temperature reach- es 310°, or until drops of mixture form hard brittle threads in cold water. (This takes quite awhile.) Remove from heat. After boiling has stopped, stir in flavoring and coloring and mix well. Pour onto lightly greased cookie sheet (one with high sides). Cool. Break into pieces. Shake with powdered sugar so the pieces won't stick together. Store in airtight containers.

name: Almond Bark Candy
author: Lorena Essner
instructions: Melt the almond bark. Add rest of ingredients. Drop by teaspoons on foil to cool.

name: Heavenly Hash Candy
author: Annita Layton
instructions: Cut marshmallows in half, melt chips with 2 tablespoons milk. When melted add rest of milk. Pour over marshmallows, add nuts. Press in buttered pan. Cut when cool.

name: Chocolate Coated Cherries (Candy)
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: In a mixing bowl, combine fondant and water. Mix well with spoon. Let set for 5 to 10 minutes. Place fondant in top section of double boiler and melt over very low boiling water. Dip cherries into fondant using the stem or a toothpick. Let set for 5 minutes and re-dip. Let fondant coated cherries set for an hour or two, then hand dip in melted chocolate coating. Place tray of hand dipped cherries in a cool place for two or three days to allow sufficient time for the fondant to convert to a syrup.

name: Chocolate Coated Cherries (Fondant)
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: In a 2 quart saucepan, combine sugar, water and corn syrup cook to 238 to 240°. Stir mixture at the beginning of cooking to be sure the sugar is dissolved before reaching the boiling point. When mixture has cooked to 238 or 240° remove from heat and point to cool. It can be poured on a marble surface, cookie tin or shallow pan, porcelain topped table, or a large platter. Let stand until lukewarm in center of batch and cool at the outside edges.

name: Divinity
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: In saucepan mix first 4 ingredients. Slowly bring to a boil, stirring until sugar dissolves. Cook to 260° (hardball stage). Meanwhile, beat egg whites until stiff. Gradually pour hot syrup into whites, beating constantly. Beat until candy begins to hold its shape. Beat in vanilla and powdered sugar. (This amount of powdered sugar makes a real improvement in texture.) Drop from teaspoon onto waxed paper or pour into buttered pan. Let stand several hours until firm. Store in airtight container.

name: Non-Cook Divinity
author: Shirley Drury

ingredients.name: pkg. Betty Crocker Fluffy White Frosting mix (dry)

instructions: In large bowl combine dry frosting mix, white syrup, vanilla and boiling water. Beat at high speed for five minutes. Add powdered sug- ar, gradually. Beat at low speed. Add pecans. Dip with teaspoon onto waxed paper.

name: Divinity in a Basket
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Chop nuts coarsely, cut up cherries fine. Combine sugar, syrup, water and salt in a pan. Cook without stirring until hard boil stage. Beat egg whites until stiff enough to hold peaks but not stiff enough to cling to bowl. Pour the syrup in a very thin stream, slowly, onto the beaten egg whites, beating constantly. Continue beating until it is so thick you can pick up the mixture on the beater. Then mix in vanilla, nuts, and cherries. Drop from a teaspoon onto waxed paper.

name: Strawberry Divinity
author: Lorena Essner

ingredients.name: (3 oz.) pkg. strawberry Jell-O or any other flavor

instructions: Combine sugar, syrup and water in saucepan. Bring to a boil over medium heat stirring constantly. Reduce heat. Continue to cook without stirring until mixture reaches hard ball stage (252°) or until a small amount forms a hard ball in cold water. Beat egg whites in large bowl until fluffy. Gradually add Jell-O and beat until stiff peaks form. Slowly pour hot syrup into beaten egg whites, beating constant- ly. Beat just until candy loses its gloss and holds its shape. Drop by teaspoon onto wax paper or pour into pan. Cool and allow to set until firm.

name: Mounds Balls
author: Anna Rose Bles
instructions: Mix first 3 ingredients together. Refrigerate 2 hours or longer. Take out and make into walnut size balls. Put back in refrigerator. Melt chocolate chips and paraffin on low heat or in double boiler. Dip coconut balls using 2 forks into chocolate mixture. Place on waxed paper to cool.

name: Peanut Brittle
author: Annita Layton

ingredients.name: c. corn syrup, light or dark

instructions: Combine sugar, syrup, water and salt. Cook and stir until sugar dissolves. When syrup boils, add butter. Stir frequently till thread stage (230°). Add nuts at soft crack stage (280°) Stir until hard crack stage (300°). Remove from heat. Stir in baking soda. Pour into 2 greased cookie sheets.

name: Peanut Brittle
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Boil sugar, water and syrup for 2 or 3 minutes. Add peanuts and cook to hard crack stage (300°). Remove and add butter and soda. Pour out on buttered board and pull thin.

name: Peanut Butter Candy
author: Dustin P. Glastetter
instructions: Mix together and roll into balls. Place on wax paper. No bake.

name: Peanut Butter Fudge
author: Patty Schaefer
instructions: Cook evaporated milk and sugar over medium heat until they form a soft ball, stirring constantly, about 15 to 20 minutes. Remove milk and sugar mixture from stove and stir in peanut butter until mixed well. Pour and spread evenly into buttered cookie sheet. (Should be firm in about 5 to 10 minutes.) Combine chocolate chips, sweetened condensed milk, vanilla extract and butter. Heat in microwave for three minutes until melted; stir after each 1 minute interval. Spread chocolate mixture over fudge mixture. Refrigerate. Enjoy your homemade Reeses' Peanut butter bar!

name: Peanut Chocolate Clusters
author: S. Marie G.

ingredients.name: pkg. (6 oz.) semi sweet chocolate morsels

instructions: Combine peanut butter, butterscotch morsels and chocolate morsels in a heavy saucepan. Place over low heat and cook, stirring constantly, until melted. Stir in peanuts. Drop by rounded teaspoon onto waxed paper; chill until firm. Store in a covered container in refrigerator.

name: Peanut Clusters
author: Juanita Dannenmueller

ingredients.name: regular size jar of slightly salted peanuts

instructions: Melt almond bark in microwave until smooth. Stir in peanuts and spoon onto wax paper. Let set until firm.

name: New Orleans Pralines
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: In a 2 quart saucepan, combine the sugar, water, corn syrup and pecan halves. Mix well and bring to a boil over a medium heat, stirring often to make sure the sugar is dissolved before mixture reaches the boiling point. Continue to cook over a medium to high heat, stirring occasionally, until temperature reaches 236°. Remove saucepan containing mixture from heat and let stand until temperature of mixture cools to 180°. Add maple flavoring and begin to stir with a spoon and continue stirring until mixture becomes thicker and appears just a little lighter in color. Do not stir until mixture become too thick to pour. Using a tablespoon, dip mixture onto wax paper.

name: Rice Crispy Candy
author: Joan Drury
instructions: Melt caramels together with milk in double boiler. Mix nuts, cereal, and coconut together. Add melted caramels and mix well. Roll into small balls. Cool.

name: Chow Mein Noodle Candy
author: Helen Welter
instructions: Melt morsels in double boiler. Remove from stove. Add nuts and chow mein noodles and mix well. Dip out with teaspoon and out on waxed paper. (Use Nestles Butterscotch Tollhouse morsels.)

name: Candy Coated Pretzels
author: Charlotte Hooper
instructions: Microwave almond bark until melted. Drop in pretzels and coat well. Place on wax paper until coating is firm.

name: English Toffee
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: In a 2 or 3 quart heavy saucepan, melt the butter or margarine over a low heat. Add the sugar and lecithin and stir constantly with a wooden spoon over a medium high heat, until mixture comes to a boil. Then add the corn syrup and continue to cook over a medium heat, stirring constantly to prevent burning in the bottom, until temperature reaches 295°. Remove from heat. To the cooked mixture, add salt and nut meats and gently mix in. Then pour into a well buttered shallow pan. Smooth out with a spatula or knife to a thickness of 1/4 inch. Before toffee sets and becomes firm, cut into rectangles using a knife. Toffee can also be left unscored and broken into irregular pieces after it sets. Toffee can be left uncovered or dipped in chocolate almond bark

name: Cinnamon Candy Apples
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Pare, quarter and core apples. Mix sugar, lemon juice, water and candies in saucepan. Cook for 5 minutes to form a syrup. Add apples to syrup; cook until transparent and tender.

name: Oatmeal Pie
author: Marilyn Friend
instructions: Blend all ingredients. Pour into unbaked pie crust. Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes.

name: Angel Pie
author: Jennifer Menz, Donna Menz
instructions: Add sugar, vanilla and baking powder to beaten egg whites. Add graham cracker crumbs and pecans. Bake for 30 minutes at 350° in a greased pie pan, do not overbake. Can serve with Cool Whip.

name: Fruity Cookie Recipe Jello That Crumbles
author: Anna Rose Bles
instructions: Cream butter. Gradually add sugar and Jell-O and cream well after each addition. Add egg and vanilla and beat well. Gradually add flour mixture, mixing after each addition, until smooth. Use cookie press or drop by teaspoonful on ungreased cookie sheet. Sprinkle with Jell-O. Bake at 400° for 12 to 14 minutes or until the edges are golden brown.

name: Apple Crumb Pie
author: Janet Welter
instructions: Peel and slice apples; put in a large bowl. Add flour, sugar and spice; mix with apples. Let sit until apples get a moist look. Put in a 9 inch pie crust. Mix together 1⁄2 cup of sugar, 3/4 cup of flour and the oleo. Sprinkle on top of the apple mixture. Topping will be crumbly. Bake at 400° for 30 to 40 minutes or until golden brown.

name: Sour Cream Apple Pie
author: Linda Menz
instructions: In a large bowl beat eggs. Add sour cream. Stir in sugar, 2 tablespoons of flour, vanilla and salt. Mix well. Stir in apples. Pour into pie shell. Bake at 375° for 15 minutes. Meanwhile combine butter, brown sugar and remaining flour. Sprinkle over top of pie. Return to oven for 20 to 25 minutes or until filling is set. Cool completely.

name: Apple Pie
author: Charlotte Hooper
instructions: Peel and slice the apples. Mix remaining ingredients in bowl and pour into pie shell. Top with remaining crust. Sprinkle with sugar, bake at 400° for about 35 minutes.

name: Fruit and Cream Pies
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Place berries in pie crust. Mix together and pour over berries the sugar, flour, salt, cinnamon and cream. Bake until crust is nicely browned and filling is set. Serve slightly warm Bake in 400° oven for 35 to 45 minutes. This recipe can be used for blackberries, blueberries, raspberries, peaches and rhubarb.

name: Million Dollar Pie
author: Sara Hooper
instructions: Mix together and pour in pie shell. Refrigerate.

name: Million Dollar Pie
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Mix well milk, lemon juice, coconut and pineapple. Pour into pie shells. Top with nuts. Refrigerate.

name: Blueberry Banana Pie
author: Doris Moore
instructions: Cut butter and sugar into flour. Form 2 pie shells by pressing mixture into well buttered pie pans. Bake 425° for 10 minutes or until light brown. Cool. Beat cream cheese until creamy, add sugar and beat well. Mix in prepared Dream Whip. Slice bananas in bottom of cooled pie shells, cover with cream cheese mixture. Top center of each pie with pie filling.

name: Cherry Crumb Pie
author: Kurt Glastetter
instructions: Pour cherry pie filling into unbaked pie shell. Combine flour and sugar. Cut in butter until crumbly. Sprinkle over filling. Bake at 400° until crust is golden brown, approximately 40 minutes.

name: Crisco's Door County Cherry Pie
author: Annita Layton

ingredients.name: (16 oz.) cans pitted red tart cherries in water

instructions: For filling, drain cherries, reserving 1 cup liquid. Combine 1 cup sugar and cornstarch in medium saucepan. Stir in cherries and reserved 1 cup liquid. You will not use all of liquid. Cook and stir on medium heat until mixture comes to a boil. Boil for 1 minute. Cool while preparing crust. Preheat oven to 425°. Spoon half of cherry filling into unbaked pie shell. Bake at 425° for 15 minutes. For cream cheese layer, beat cream cheese, 1/2 cup sugar and vanilla extract in small bowl at medium speed of electric mixer until smooth. Beat in eggs until blended. Remove pie from oven. Spoon cream cheese mix- ture over cherries. Reduce oven temperature to 375°. Top with remaining cherry mixture. Return to oven for 20 minutes. Cool to room temperature. For topping, place spoonfuls of sour cream around edge of pie. Makes one 9-inch pie.

name: Cherry Cream Cheese Pie
author: Juanita Dannenmueller
instructions: Mix cream cheese, Cool Whip and powdered sugar together. Add a little milk. Pour into pie crust. Top with cherry filling. Put in refrigerator until chilled.

name: Cherry Delight
instructions: Mix crumbs, butter and sugar together. Press into 9 inch square dish and bake until brown at 350°. Let cool. Mix remaining ingredients together and spread on the cooled crust. Top with 1 can of cherry pie filling. Refrigerate to chill.

name: Cream Cheese Pie
author: Shawn Schlosser

ingredients.name: prepared pie crusts, baked and cooled
can cherry or favorite pie filling

instructions: Cream sugar and cheese together. Fold in Cool Whip and stir well. Pour into cooled pie shells and top with pie filling. Chill.

name: Chocolate Dream Pie
author: Shirley Drury

ingredients.name: pkg. Jell-O brand chocolate or other flavor instant pudding

instructions: Prepare whipped topping mix as directed on package, using 1 cup milk and 1 teaspoon vanilla, in large mixing bowl. Add remaining 1 3/4 cup milk and pudding mix. Whip, then beat at high speed for 2 minutes, scraping bowl occasionally. Spoon into pie shell. Chill at least 4 hours.

name: Chocolate Cream Pie
author: Sara Hooper

ingredients.name: (4 oz.) pkg. instant chocolate pudding mix

instructions: Mix 1 cup of milk with topping mix until fluffy. Add both pack- ages of chocolate pudding and remaining milk; beat until fluffy. Spoon into pie shell. Top with Cool Whip and chill about 3 hours.

name: Chocolate-Filled Meringue Shells with Strawberry Sauce
author: Annita Layton

ingredients.name: c. frozen non-dairy whipped topping, thawed
(10 oz.) pkg. frozen strawberries in syrup, thawed

instructions:
Heat oven to 275°. Paper-line 12 muffin cups. In small mixer bowl, beat egg whites with cream of tartar and salt until soft peaks form. Beat in sugar, 1 tablespoon at a time, until stiff, glossy peaks form. Stir in vanilla. Spoon 2 to 3 tablespoons meringue in each prepared cup. Using back of spoon or small spatula, push meringue up sides of paper cups forming well in center. Bake for 1 hour or until meringue turns delicate cream color and feels dry to the touch. Cool in pan on wire rack.
In small mixer bowl, beat cream cheese and cocoa. Gradually add powdered sugar, beating until well blended. Fold in whipped topping. This makes the chocolate filling. Spoon the filling into shells. Before serving, carefully remove paper from shells. Puree strawberries; spoon over meringues. Refrigerate leftovers.

name: Impossible Coconut Pie
author: R.G.
instructions: Heat oven to 350°. Grease deep 9 inch pie plate. Place all ingredients in blender container. Cover and blend on high speed 15 seconds. Pour into plate. Bake until knife inserted in center comes out clean, 50 to 55 minutes.

name: Custard Pie
author: Shirley Drury, Annita Layton
instructions: Beat eggs slightly with rotary beater. Then beat in sugar, salt, nutmeg, milk and vanilla. Pour into pastry lined pie pan. Bake just until a silver knife inserted into side of filling comes out clean. The center may still look a bit soft, but will set later. Bake at 450° for 15 minutes, then 350° for 25 to 30 minutes.

name: Custard Pie
author: Juanita Dannenmueller

ingredients.name: Sugar, enough to make it sweet

instructions: Mix all ingredients together and pour in pie crust. Bake at 375° until a tip of a knife come out clean.

name: Date Tart
author: Annita Layton
instructions: Sift the flour, baking powder and salt. Pour over chopped dates. Beat sugar in egg yolks and add vanilla. Fold in egg whites. Gently add date mixture. Bake at 350° approximately 35 minutes. Serve warm with whipped cream

name: Lemonade Pie
author: Ramona Bess
instructions: Put milk and lemonade in bowl, beat well. Add Cool Whip and beat again. Put in graham cracker crust and chill for 2 1⁄2 hours. Sprinkle top with graham cracker crumbs.

name: Creamy Lemon Pie
author: Vernita Bles

ingredients.name: pkg. (4 serving) Jell-O instant vanilla pudding
can (6 oz.) frozen lemonade concentrate thawed

instructions: Pour milk into a large bowl, add pudding mixes. Beat with wisk 30 seconds. Add lemonade concentrate and beat 30 more seconds. Mixture will be thick. Immediately stir in whipped topping. Spoon into crust. Refrigerate four hours or until set. Garnish with lemon slices, if desired.

name: Fresh Peach Crumble
author: Rebecca Hooper
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°. In bowl, toss peaches with granulated sug- ar and lemon juice; spread evenly in 2 quart casserole. In bowl, mix flour with brown sugar and cinnamon. Add butter, with fingers, pinch butter with mixture until crumbly. Add oats. Mix, crumble over peaches. Bake 30 minutes or until topping browns and fruit bubbles around edges.

name: Fresh Peach Pie
author: Zeta Welter

ingredients.name: Prepared pie crust or graham cracker crust
pkg. Jell-O peach or mixed fruit (3 oz.)

instructions: Place sliced peaches in pie shell. Mix water, sugar and corn- starch together and cook until clear. Remove from heat and add 1 package peach Jell-O or mixed fruit. Let cool, pour over peaches. Then whip 1 package Dream Whip according to directions on box. Add cream cheese and powdered sugar. Spread over pie.

name: Frozen Peanut Butter Pie
author: Donna Menz

ingredients.name: of an 8 oz. cream cheese, softened

instructions: Whip softened cream cheese until fluffy. Beat in powdered sugar and peanut butter. Gradually add milk, blending well. Fold in Cool Whip and freeze until firm. Garnish with additional Cool Whip or peanut butter cups.

name: Peanut Butter Pie
author: Charlotte Hooper
instructions: In saucepan combine sugar, cornstarch and salt. Gradually stir in milk. Cook and stir over medium heat until bubbly. Cook and stir 2 minutes more. Remove from heat. Stir small amount of hot mixture into beaten egg yolks. Immediately return to hot mixture. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly. Remove from heat and add peanut but- ter and vanilla. Pour into baked pie shell. Can top with Cool Whipwhen cooled.

name: Big Slice Pecan Pie
author: S.P.
instructions: Cream margarine with sugar. Add syrup, vanilla and salt. In a separate bowl, beat eggs until very light, add to first mixture. Fold in pecans reserving enough pecans for garnish. Pour into pastry shell, bake at 425° for 10 minutes. Reduce heat to 350° and bake until firm for 30 minutes.

name: Pecan Pie
author: Juanita Dannenmueller
instructions: Beat until thick the eggs and sugar. Add syrup, pecans, vanilla and butter. Mix well. Pour into unbaked pie shell. Bake at 325° for about 1 hour.

name: Pecan Pie
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Mix all ingredients together and pour in unbaked pie shell. Bake at 325° for one hour.

name: Pecan Pie
author: Cheryl Stone
instructions: Mix all ingredients and pour into pie shell. Bake at 325° for 40 to 50 minutes.

name: Pumpkin Chiffon Pie
author: Donna Menz
instructions: In a mixing bowl, beat cream cheese and sugar until smooth. Add Cool Whip and mix well. Spread into crust. In another bowl beat milk and pudding mixes on low speed until combined; beat on high for 2 minutes. Let stand 3 minutes. Stir in pumpkin and spices. Mix well. Spread over cream cheese layer. Chill.

name: Pumpkin Chiffon Pie
author: Annita Layton
instructions: Beat egg whites until stiff. Set aside. Beat egg yolks and sugars until fluffy. Add remaining ingredients. Fold in egg whites. Pour into pie shell and bake at 400° for 45 to 55 minutes. Use 9 inch pie shell. I use a bright orange flesh field pumpkin. Scoot our seeds, peel with knife and cut into chunks. Cook with small amount of water in large pot about 30 minutes. Cool, mash and drain off excess water, liquid.

name: Pumpkin Pie
author: Denise Glastetter
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°. Combine filling ingredients and pour into pie shell. Bake 15 minutes. Reduce to 350° and bake an additional 45 minutes or until knife inserted in center comes out clean.

name: Pumpkin Pie with Molasses
author: Lorena Essner
instructions: Mix ingredients in order given. Beat egg yolks and whites sepa- rately. Bake in two unbaked crusts about 40 minutes.

name: Pumpkin Pie
author: Charlotte Hooper
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°. In large mixer bowl, combine all ingredients except pastry shell. Mix well. Pour into pastry shell. Bake 15 minutes. Reduce oven temperature to 350° and continue baking 35 to 40 minutes or until knife inserted in center comes out clean. Cool.

name: Mom's Raisin Pie
author: In Memory of Ella I. Schlosser

ingredients.name: Pie shells, for top and bottom

instructions: Cover raisins with water and sugar. Bring to boil until raisins plump. Mix cornstarch with water to make a paste. Add to boiling mixture and boil until thick. Pour in pie shell and bake until done, 400° for 20 to 30 minutes.

name: Strawberry Pie
author: Donna Stamp
instructions: Cook first three ingredients until slightly thick. Remove from heat and add Jell-O. Mix and pour over strawberries. Pour into baked pie shell. Top with whipped cream, if desired.

name: Strawberry Pie
author: Rebecca Hooper

ingredients.name: pints fresh strawberries, washed and hulled

instructions: Crush strawberries. In a saucepan, blend together sugar, corn- starch and water. Add crushed berries and lemon juice. Bring to a boil; cook until mixture is clear, about 2 minutes. Then strain juice and stir in butter. Arrange remaining whole berries in baked 9 inch pie shell. Spoon glaze over berries carefully, coating each berry. Cool. Serve with whipped cream.

name: Ella's Strawberry Pie (Crust)
author: In Memory of Ella I. Schlosser
instructions: Mix all ingredients in bowl. Pat dough in pan and bake at 350° until brown.

name: Ella's Strawberry Pie (Filling)
author: In Memory of Ella I. Schlosser
instructions: Cook until thick, sugar, cornstarch, white syrup and water. Add Jell-O and strawberries. Pour into baked pie shell.

name: Strawberries Glaze Pie
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Take 1 cup of smallest berries and 1 cup water and cook slowly until berries are soft. Strain, mix together sugar and cornstarch. Add to juice and cook until clear and thick. Cool. Add powdered sugar to 3 cups large berries. Let stand for one hour. Spread 1 small package cream cheese in bottom of pie shell. Next arrange large berries in shell, topping with the cooled liquid. Chill in refrigerator. Serve with whipped cream or ice cream.

name: Diet Strawberry Pie
author: Ruth Schlosser
instructions: Bring to a boil the soda and cornstarch, add Jell-O and mix. Pour over the strawberries, mix and pour into cookie pie crust. Refrigerate.

name: Easy Frozen Strawberry Pie
author: Stella Reinagel
instructions: Mix all ingredients. Cook strawberries, sugar, cornstarch and Jell-O to boil. To seal the crust, mix 4 tablespoons of the mixture with 2 tablespoons of butter and pour over crust. Let cool. Pour remaining mixture into crusts. Refrigerate 1 to 2 hours. Garnish with whipped topping.

name: Strawberry Jello Pie
author: Revella Schlosser
instructions: Combine sugar, water, cornstarch and salt. Cook until clear. Remove from heat and add red food coloring. Add Jell-O and stir well, let cool. Put sliced berries in baked pie shell. Pour sauce over berries. Chill. Top with Cool Whip or whipped cream.

name: Vanilla Cream Pie
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Mix in saucepan the sugar, salt, cornstarch and flour. Stir in milk gradually. Cook over moderate heat, stirring constantly, until mixture thickens and boils. Boil 1 minute. Remove from heat. Slowly stir half the mixture into egg yolks and mix well. Slowly stir into the hot mixture, continue cooking for 2 more minutes. Then stir in butter and vanilla. For banana cream pie, add 3 large bananas. For coconut cream pie, add 3/4 cup shredded coconut. Can top with meringue.

name: Hawaiian Pie
author: Laurie Essner
instructions: Mix all preceding ingredients and pour into the graham cracker crusts. Chill.

name: Pie Crust
author: Irene Blattel
instructions: Mix all ingredients. Roll out between two pieces of wax paper or plastic wrap. This is enough for a double crust pie.

name: Skinny Pie Crust
author: Linda Menz
instructions: Stir milk and oil until creamy. Add dry ingredients. Mix with fork. Press to fit pan. Use any filling and bake as usual. Or bake at 350° for 10 to 12 minutes until golden brown.

name: Pie Crust
author: Shirley Drury, Sara Hooper
instructions: Mix together the flour and salt. Cut in shortening until crumbly. Sprinkle on water. Gather dough together and press into a ball. Roll to desired thickness.

name: Pie Crust Mix
author: Hazel Luebbers, Grandmother of Joan Drury
instructions: Mix altogether and store in refrigerator. One level cup of mix equals one pie crust. Add two tablespoons of ice water to one cup full of mix for one crust.

name: Meringue
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Beat whites with cream of tartar until frothy. Gradually beat in sugar, a little at a time. Continue beating until stiff and glossy. Add flavoring. Pile meringue onto pie filling, being careful to seal the edges. Bake at 400° in oven for 8 to 10 minutes.

name: Fresh Fruit Ambrosia
author: Rebecca Hooper

ingredients.name: (8 oz.) container Borden Lite-line Orange Yogurt
c. ReaLime Lime Juice from concentrate

instructions: In bowl, combine all ingredients, mix well. Chill at least 3 hours. Refrigerate leftovers.

name: Banana Pudding
author: Mrs. William (Pat) Schlosser
instructions: Line pan with vanilla wafers. Slice bananas on top. Mix pudding as directed. Fold in can milk and Cool Whip. Pour on top of bananas. Add more Cool Whip to decorate. Then top with nuts and cherries. Refrigerate and serve cold.

name: Banana Pudding
author: Charlotte Hooper
instructions: In sauce pan, combine sugar, cornstarch, and salt. Gradually stir in milk. Cook and stir over medium heat until bubbly. Cook and stir 2 minutes more. Remove from heat. Stir small amount of hot mixture into beaten egg yolks. Immediately return to hot mixture. Cook 2 minutes stirring constantly. Remove from heat and add butter and vanilla. Spread a layer of vanilla wafers and then sliced bananas in a bowl and pour 1/3 of pudding over layers Repeat layers until all is gone. Can be served warm or chilled.

name: Cottage Pudding
author: Annita Layton
instructions: Sift together into bowl the first three ingredients. Add remaining ingredients and beat well with rotary beater until smooth. Pour into greased and floured 9 inch square plan. Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 min- utes. Cut into squares, Serve warm with vanilla.

name: Bread Pudding
author: In Memory of Mrs. Lorraine Drury
instructions: Mix all ingredients together. Bake in baking dish that has been well greased. Bake at 325° for one hour.

name: Rice Pudding
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Mix all ingredients together. Put in oven and bake. Stirring sev- eral times until it thickens. If it is real thick when you mix altogether, add a little more milk. It will thicken while baking. You can add raisins, too.

name: Strawberry Vanilla Pudding
author: Shirley Drury

ingredients.name: to 5 c. angel food cake cubes
pkg. instant vanilla or lemon pudding

instructions: Put cake in 9 x 9 inch pan. Mix pudding, softened ice cream and milk until well blended. Pour over cake cubes and set. Dissolve Jell-O with water and put in frozen strawberries. Stir until it starts to jell. Pour over cake and pudding and put in refrigerator.

name: Apple Goody
author: Annita Layton
instructions: Mix together sugar and 2 tablespoons of flour and the cinnamon. Mix in apples. Place apples in greased and floured baking dish (9 x 13). Mix with pastry blender or forks the oatmeal, baking powder, brown sugar, salt, flour, butter and soda. Pour over tops of apples. Bake 30 minutes at 350°.

name: Glazed Fresh Apples
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Place sugar, water, lemon and cinnamon in a 2 quart saucepan. Bring to boiling point and boil 3 minutes. Stick whole cloves into peeled whole apples with stems attached. Drop fruit in boiling syrup. Cook 20 to 25 minutes or until tender spooning syrup over the fruit at intervals. Chill and serve.

name: Caramel Dumplings
author: Lorena Essner
instructions: Combine flour, baking powder and salt. Cut in shortening. Add milk, vanilla and 1 1⁄2 cup brown sugar. This makes the dumplings. Drop by teaspoon into hot syrup. For hot syrup in 1 1⁄2 quart sauce pan, add 2 tablespoons shortening, 1 1⁄2 cup brown sugar, boiling water and 1/8 teaspoon salt. It is best to cook in a pan which has a fitted lid cover. A transparent cover is excellent for dumpling cooking. Boil syrup gently for five minutes. Add dumplings. Cook for 20 minutes without removing cover.

name: Apple Dumplings
author: Anna Rose Bles
instructions: Make a syrup of sugar, water, cinnamon and nutmeg. Add but- ter. Pare, core and slice apples. Sift flour, salt, and baking powder. Cut in shortening. Add milk all at once, and stir until moistened. Roll 1/4 inch thick. Cut into 5 inch squares. Arrange apple slices on each square. Sprinkle generously with additional sugar, cinnamon and nutmeg. Dot with butter. Fold corners to center and pinch edges together. Place 1 inch apart in greased baking pan. Pour syrup over dumplings. Bake at 375° for 35 minutes.

name: Watermelon Ice Cream Cake
author: Michelle Hulshof
instructions: Line medium size bowl with aluminum foil. Cover foil with a thin layer of ice cream. Freeze for 1 hour. Mix chocolate chips with sherbet. Pour on ice cream. Freeze at least 24 hours. Mix food color- ing with Cool Whip. Empty contents of bowl on plate. Coat with Cool Whip. Freeze until ready to serve.

name: Blackberry Dumplings
author: Charlotte Hooper
instructions: In saucepan, cook blackberries, water, sugar and cinnamon. Bring to a boil. In the meantime, mix flour and Crisco together. Add enough water to make a soft dough. Roll dough out and cut with pizza cutter or knife like dumplings. Drop in boiling mixture. Cook until tender. Approximately five minutes. Serve hot.

name: Mom's Tempting Apple Crisp
author: Ramona Glastetter
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°. Spray a 9 x 13 inch pan with nonstick cooking spray. Peel and slice apples and spread in prepared pan. In a medium bowl, combine flour, brown sugar, oats and margarine. Mix with fork until crumbly; spoon over apples. Bake for 35 minutes or until apples are tender and bubbly.

name: Fruit Cobbler
author: St. Augustine School Cafeteria

ingredients.name: No. 2 can cherries, peaches or berries

instructions: Cream together butter and sugar. Stir in sifted dry ingredients alternately with milk. Beat until smooth. Pour in 8 x 8 inch pan. Spoon fruit over batter. Sprinkle with sugar. Pour fruit juice over top. Bake 45 to 50 minutes at 375°. In baking the batter will come to the top.

name: Peach Cobbler
author: Sister Rebecca Peters

ingredients.name: Fresh peaches, about 2 cups, sliced and sugared

instructions: Melt butter in large pan. Add sliced peaches. Mix together remaining ingredients and drop this mixture on peaches. Top with 1⁄2 cup of sugar. Bake 325° until done.

name: Cherry Coffee Cake
author: St. Augustine School Cafeteria
instructions: Sift 2 cups of flour and baking powder together. Cut in butter. Beat egg and milk together. Add to flour mixture, mix well. Pour into 15 x 10 inch pan that has been greased and floured. Cover with cherry filling. For topping, sift together 1 cup of flour and 1 cut of sugar. Cut in butter. Sprinkle over pie filling. Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes.

name: Country Apple Coffee Cake
author: S.P.

ingredients.name: oz. can Hungry Jack Refrigerated Flaky Biscuits

instructions: Heat oven to 350°. Using 1 tablespoon margarine, generously grease bottom and sides of 9 inch round cake pan. Spread 1 cup of the apples in prepared pan. Separate dough into 10 biscuits, cut into four pieces. Arrange biscuit pieces point side up over apples. Top with remaining apples. In small bowl combine remaining 1 tablespoon margarine, brown sugar, cinnamon, corn syrup and egg. Beat 2 or 3 minutes until sugar is partially dissolved. Stir in pecans, spoon over biscuit pieces. Bake at 350° for 45 minutes. Cool five minutes. Add glaze: 3 c. powdered sugar, 1/4 tsp. vanilla and 1 to 2 teaspoons of milk. Mix until smooth; drizzle over warm coffee cake. Store in refrigerator.

name: Sharen's Sour Cream Coffee Cake
author: S.M.
instructions: Cream together margarine, 1 cup sugar; add eggs and sour cream. Cream thoroughly. Sift together flour, baking soda, baking powder and salt. Add 1⁄2 of flour mixture to sour cream mixture, stir until smooth. Add remaining flour and 1 teaspoon vanilla, stir until smooth. Pour 1⁄2 batter into greased and floured pan, sprinkle with mixture of 1⁄2 cup sugar, 1 tsp. cinnamon, 1 c. chopped nuts. Pour remaining batter over cinnamon mixture. Bake 30 minutes at 325°. Glaze: Mix together powdered sugar, milk, and 1 teaspoon vanilla. Heat to dissolve and pour over hot cake.

name: Banana Split Cake
author: Zeta Welter
instructions: Mix together graham crackers, sugar, and butter and press into an oblong Pyrex pan. Beat together cream cheese, powdered sugar and butter. Spread evenly over first layer. Arrange bananas and pine- apple on second layer. Spread Cool Whip over this layer. Top with pecans and maraschino cherries.

name: Fluffy 2-Step Cheesecake
author: Rebecca Hooper

ingredients.name: prepared graham cracker crumb crust (6 oz.)

instructions: Beat cream cheese and sugar in large bowl with wire whisk or electric mixer on high speed until smooth. Gently stir in whipped top- ping. Spoon into crust. Refrigerate 3 hours or until set. Spread pie filling evenly over top of pie. Store leftover cheesecake in refrigerator.

name: Cheesecake
author: Tim Drury
instructions: Mix graham crackers, sugar and oleo and pat 3/4 of mixture in 9 x 13 inch pan. Dissolve jello in hot water. Cool. Whip Milnot. Add sugar. Whip cream cheese with the jello. Fold into the Milnot mixture. Pour on graham crackers. Top with remaining crumb mixture. Chill.

name: Cheese Cake
author: In Memory of Celena Blattel, Helen Menz
instructions: Dissolve 1 package lemon flavored Jell-O in 1 cup boiling water. Add 3 tablespoons lemon juice. Cool to room temperature. Cream together the cream cheese, sugar and vanilla. Add cooled Jell-O and mix well. Whip the chilled Milnot and fold into Jell-O mixture. Crush the graham cracker and add 1⁄2 cup melted oleo. Pack 2/3 of the mixture in the bottom and sides of a 9 x 13 inch pan, add filling and sprinkle the remaining crumbs on top. Chill several hours.

name: Mini Cherry Cheese Cakes
author: Doris Moore
instructions: Soften cream cheese to room temperature. Blend cheese, sugar, eggs and vanilla until smooth and creamy. Line muffin tins with cup- cake wrappers. Place vanilla wafer in each bottom. Fill each cup with cheesecake mixture, about 3/4 full. Bake at 325° for 20 minutes. Cool and top with your favorite pie filling.

name: Petite Cheese Cakes
author: Ramona Bess
instructions: Soften cream cheese, then add eggs, vanilla and lemon juice. Beat together until smooth. Place cupcake liners in muffin tins. Put 1 vanilla wafer in each cup. Add one large tablespoon of mixture in each cup. Bake at 350° for 15 minutes. Cool, top with pie filling and Cool Whip.

name: Refrigerator Dessert
author: Louise Alderman
instructions: Bake cake in 9 x 13 inch pan. Let cool. Make instant pudding. Put in refrigerator to set. Add pineapple to pudding right before you spread on cake. Spread pudding over cake. Spread Cool Whip over cake. Sprinkle with nuts.

name: Cheesecake Cups
author: Rebecca Hooper
instructions: Mix all ingredients together, except vanilla wafers. Place one vanilla wafer in each cupcake holder. Top with cheese mixture. Bake at 325° for 10 to 15 minutes. Cool completely and top with pie filling, cherry or blueberry.

name: Chocolate Chip Cheesecake
author: Shari Landewe
instructions: Mix cookie crumbs and butter. Press evenly on bottom of ungreased springform pan. In a large bowl, beat remaining ingredients, except chocolate chips, until smooth. Mix in chocolate chips. Pour cheese mixture over crumb mixture. Bake at 300° for 1 hour. Cover and refrigerate for at least 3 hours.

name: Chocolate Eclair
author: Beverly Essner, Denise Menz

ingredients.name: small pkg. instant French vanilla pudding

instructions: Place one layer of whole graham crackers on the bottom of a 9 x 13 inch pan. Mix pudding, Cool Whip and milk together until smooth. Pour half of the pudding mixture over the crackers. Place another layer of graham crackers over the pudding mixture. Pour the rest of the pudding mixture over the crackers. Place a third layer of graham crackers on top of the pudding mixture. Chill in the refrigerator while making the topping. Mix and melt over low heat the baking chocolate, 4 tablespoons of milk and butter. Remove from heat and quickly add powdered sugar. Stir until smooth and pour over layer of graham crackers. Store in refrigerator. Best when made a day ahead so that the graham crackers can soften.

name: Chocolate Eclair Cake
author: Pat Schlosser Jenkins

ingredients.name: pkg. (34 oz.) instant French vanilla pudding mix

instructions: Place a single layer of whole graham crackers on the bottom of a 9 x 13 inch pan. Combine pudding mix with 3 cups of the milk, sit- ting until thickened. Fold in whipped topping. Spread half the pud- ding on graham cracker layer. Add another layer of crackers. Cover with remaining pudding. Top with third layer of crackers. In a small saucepan, combine remaining ingredients. Stir over low heat just until liquified. Pour over top layer of crackers. Refrigerate at least 28 hours. May prepare two days before serving.

name: Coconut Crunch Delight
author: Theresa King

ingredients.name: (3.4 oz.) pkg. instant coconut pudding mix

instructions: In a bowl, combine the first five ingredients; press lightly into a greased 13 x 9 x 2 inch baking pan. Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes or until golden brown, stirring every 10 minutes to form coarse crumbs. Cool. Divide crumb mixture in half; press half into the same baking pan. In a mixing bowl, beat pudding mixes and milk. Fold in whipped topping; spoon over the crust. Top with remaining crumb mixture. Cover and refrigerate overnight. Garnish with strawberries if desired.

name: Maraschino Cherry Dessert
author: Karla Essner
instructions: Mix together and serve.

name: Twinkies Cake
author: Shirley Eftink
instructions: Line 9 x 13 inch pan with Twinkies, cut in half the long length, icing on top. Cook pudding according to directions; cool completely. Spread cooled pudding evenly over Twinkies. Spread sliced bananas on top. Take pineapple and Cool Whip and spread over top of cake. May sprinkle with coconut or chopped nuts.

name: Dirt Cake
author: Anna Rose Bles

ingredients.name: (3.5 oz.) instant vanilla or French vanilla pudding

instructions: Crush cookies and put half of crumbs in 9 x 13 inch pan. Mix cream cheese and butter until smooth. Mix in powdered sugar. Fold in whipped topping. In separate bowl, mix pudding, milk and vanilla. Fold cream cheese mixture and pudding mixture together. Pour into pan on cookie crumbs. Sprinkle remaining crumbs on top.

name: Four Layer Dessert
author: Juanita Dannenmueller
instructions: Mix together flour and butter. Bake at 350° for 10 to 15 minutes to make the first layer. Beat together cream cheese, powdered sugar and 1 container of Cool Whip. Add this to the first layer, after it has cooled. For the third layer, beat together pudding and milk. Finally, for the fourth layer, spread Cool Whip on top and nuts if desired.

name: Four Layer Dessert
author: Shelly Dohogne
instructions: Combine flour, oleo and pecans; mix well. Pat into 9 x 13 inch pan and bake at 350° for 15 minutes. Cool. Mix together, cream cheese, powdered sugar, and 1 cup Cool Whip. Spread this over the first layer. Chill. Mix together and beat until thick, the pudding, milk and vanilla. Spread over the second layer. Top with remaining Cool Whip and sprinkle with nuts.

name: Four Layer Cake
author: Eva Glueck
instructions: To make the crust, combine flour, butter and pecans. Press into the bottom of a 9 x 12 inch oblong pan. Bake for 15 minutes in a 350° oven. Cool. Top with a mixture of cream cheese, powdered sugar and Cool Whip. Next, stir milk, vanilla and pudding until thickened. Pour over the cream cheese layer. Let set until firm. Spread with remaining Cool Whip and top with pecans.

name: Ice Cream Dessert
author: Juanita Dannenmueller
instructions: Crush Oreo cookies and spread into 9 x 13 inch pan. Soften ice cream and spread over Oreos. For the third layer, add topping. Next, add Cool Whip, followed by a layer of nuts. Sprinkle Oreo cookies on top. Freeze before serving.

name: Ice Cream Cake
author: Helen Menz
instructions: Crush crackers and mix with butter. Save 1⁄2 cup. Press into 9x13 inch pan. Mix ice cream, pudding and milk together and pour into pan. Top with remaining crumbs. Chill.

name: Bread and Butter Pickles
author: In memory of Mary Welter
instructions: Wash cucumbers thoroughly and slice thinly, without peeling. Medium sized cucumbers about five inches long and about an inch in diameter are best. Peel onions and slice thinly. Mix cucumbers, onions, and salt. Use pure granulated salt (medium coarse). Add cracked ice and let stand 3 hours, then drain thoroughly. The ice and salt mixture helps make pickles especially crisp. Make the pickling solution and heat them to the boiling point.

name: Bread and Butter Pickles (Pickling Solution)
author: In memory of Mary Welter
instructions: Add the well drained cucumber and onions to the hot pickling solution. Heat to the scalding point, stirring to insure even cooking. Avoid over cooking pickles. Pack in clean, hot jars. Cover with the syrup and seal promptly. The turmeric gives the pickles the characteristic yellow color.

name: Pickled Okra (Addition To Each Jar)
author: Helen Kluesner
instructions: Pack clean okra in clean jars. Add other ingredients.

name: Pickled Okra (Pickling Solution)
author: Helen Kluesner
instructions: Mix ingredients and boil for 2 to 3 minutes or until dissolved. Pour the boiling solution over the okra to cover. It will darken if not covered. Seal tight. Process 10 minutes in boiling water.

name: Bananas Foster
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Slice bananas in half lengthwise. Brush with lemon juice. Melt sugar and butter in flat chafing dish or 10 inch skillet. Add bananas, saute until just tender. Sprinkle with cinnamon. Remove from heat; add liqueur and rum. Immediately ignite and baste bananas with warm liquid until flame burns out. Divide sauce and bananas over 4 servings of ice cream.

name: Irish Coffee
author: Fr. Oliver Clavin

ingredients.name: Cream, rich as an Irish brogue
Coffee, strong as a friendly hand
Sugar, sweet as the tongue of a rogue
Whiskey, smooth as the wit of the land

instructions:
In a glass, pour 1 jigger of Irish whiskey. Add strong black coffee steaming hot to within one inch of top of the glass. Add 3 cubes of sugar, or 1 teaspoon, and stir well. Over the back of a large spoon, carefully pour the whipped rich cream.
It should float on top of the coffee. (It should not be stirred into the coffee.) The hot coffee should be sipped through the cool cream.
Another name for this is Whiskey-laced Coffee.

name: Rum Slush
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Mix well and freeze. I use Cool Whip cartons. When ready to serve, pour into glass and pour 7-up or Sprite over it.

name: Amaretto Slush
author: Christine Estes

ingredients.name: (6 oz.) can frozen lemonade concentrate, thawed and undiluted

instructions: Combine sugar and water in a saucepan, stirring well. Bring to a boil, stirring until sugar dissolves. Reduce heat and simmer 15 minutes. Combine sugar mixture, lemonade and Amaretto; stir well and freeze mixture overnight. Break frozen mixture into chunks. Scoop into glasses, filling to 1⁄2 full. Add carbonated beverage; stir until slushy. Top each serving with a cherry, if desired.

name: Wine Slush
author: Marilyn Friend
instructions: Mix all ingredients together. Put in freezer and freeze.

name: Strawberry Daiquiri
author: Joan Drury
instructions: Blend strawberries, ice and grenadine together. When all is crushed, add powdered sugar and mix. If you want rum, add enough for your taste.

name: Bullfrogs
author: Charlotte Hooper
instructions: Mix all ingredients together and serve.

name: Lime-Aid
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Mix all ingredients. Serve over ice.

name: Blackberry Wine
author: Jennifer Drury
instructions: Wash and mash the blackberries, or better, run them through a food chopper. Put the mixture in a stone crock and place it in a warm place so it ferments. Stir with a wooden spoon once or twice a day. In about 5 days remove the seeds and solids by passing it through a thin cloth. Dissolve sugar in warm water and add it to the blackberry juice in a 5 gallon jug. Add water to overflowing, over the opening of the jug with 3 or 4 big grape vine leaves, weighing them down with about 4 pounds of sand tied up in cloth. In 8 or 10 weeks the wine will be ready to enjoy. Fast fermentation improves the wine.

name: Elderberry Wine
author: Jennifer Drury

ingredients.name: lb. sugar, dissolved in warm water

instructions: Wash and mash elderberries. Let ferment for 5 or 6 days. Remove solids by passing it through a thin cloth. Add the lemon juice, raisins and sugar to the berry juice in a 5 gallon jug and fill with water. Cover the opening of the jug with grape vine leaves, weighing them down with sand.

name: Grape Wine
author: Jennifer Drury

ingredients.name: Grapes, enough for 5 qt. of juice
lb. sugar, dissolved in hot water

instructions: Mash grapes and let ferment for 3 to 5 days. Draw off juice. Pour juice and sugar into a 5 gallon jug container and add water to fill jug to top. Cover jug opening with sand sack for 3 to 4 months. Draw off and rejug and seal jug with tight-fitting cork or other kind of stopper.

name: Grape Wine
author: In Memory of Anton Diebold
instructions: Mix sugar, juice and yeast. Put in jug. Fill with water. Attach 10 to 15 cent balloon. Keep airtight. Set aside for six weeks.

name: Cherry Wine
author: Jennifer Drury

ingredients.name: or 5 qt. wild cherries, mashed or unmashed
lb. sugar, dissolved in warm water

instructions: Pour cherries into 5 gallon jug and add sugar. Fill remainder of jug to overflowing with water. Cover the opening of the jug with leaves, weighing them down with sand. Place in basement for fermentation. More or less cherries than above amount will produce a darker or lighter wine, respectively.

name: Dandelion Wine
author: Jennifer Drury
instructions:
Pour water over flowers. Let stand for 24 hours. Strain and add brown sugar, yeast, juices and rinds. Put in crock and let stand until it commences to ferment. Then bottle and put corks in loosely to let it ferment. After it stops fermenting, put one raisin in each bottle and cork tight.
Red clover wine and Elderberry wine can be prepared in the same way using the blossoms of those plants.

name: Mock Champagne
author: Cheryl Stone

ingredients.name: c. grape juice or pineapple juice

instructions: Boil sugar and water for 3 minutes and cool. Add the juices and chill. Just before serving, add chilled ginger ale.

name: Russian Tea
author: Sister Dorothy Reinhold
instructions: Mix well. Keep in a covered jar. Use 2 to 3 rounded teaspoons per cup of boiling water.

name: Spiced Tea
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Mix all ingredients together. Keep in covered jar. Use 2 to 3 rounded teaspoons per cup of boiling water.

name: Instant Hot Spiced Tea
author: L.M.
instructions: Mix all ingredients, store in tightly sealed jar. To make a cup, add 1 tablespoon of mix to 1 cup boiling water.

name: Banana Whip (Sugar-Free)
author: Charlotte Hooper

ingredients.name: pkg. (4 serving size) Sugar Free JELL-O, any flavor
c. cold whole milk Ice cubes

instructions: Combine gelatin and boiling water in a blender. Blend until dissolved, about 30 seconds. Add milk and ice cubes to make 1 1/4 cups. Stir in blender until partially melted. Add banana slices; blend until smooth. Only 45 calories per serving.

name: Homemade Egg Nog
author: Ann Glueck
instructions: Mix with blender.

name: Our Breakfast Nog
author: L.M.

ingredients.name: of a 6 oz. can frozen orange juice concentrate, thawed

instructions: Place all ingredients in a blender. Cover and blend at low speed until combined. Then blend at high speed until foamy for 30 seconds.

name: White Christmas Punch
author: Germaine Robert

ingredients.name: (2 liter) bottles of lemon lime soda

instructions: Combine sugar and water. Cook over medium heat until sugar is dissolved, stirring constantly. Remove from heat. Add milk and almond extract. Let cool. Chill until ready to serve. Combine milk mixture and remaining ingredients. Put in punch bowl, break ice cream in small pieces.

name: Red Punch
author: Kelso Ladies Sodality
instructions: Mix all ingredients together and chill before serving.

name: Quick and Easy Punch
author: Charlotte Hooper

ingredients.name: (12 oz.) can frozen orange juice concentrate

instructions: Fill with water to make 1 gallon. Stir and serve.

name: Punch
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Mix all ingredients. Chill and serve.

name: Wedding Punch
author: Rebecca Hooper

ingredients.name: pt. lime, lemon or raspberry sherbet
(12 oz.) bottle ginger ale or Seven-Up

instructions: Combine pineapple juice, sherbet and 1⁄2 of ice cream. Beat until smooth. Add Seven-Up or ginger ale. Spoon remaining ice cream into punch. Serve immediately.

name: Hot Chocolate
author: Mrs. Theon L. Schlosser, Jr.
instructions: Mix together and store in tight container, To make cocoa, add of above mixture to 1 cup of hot water.

name: Diebold's Hot Spiced Cider
author: Paula Diebold
instructions:
Pour cider into large pan. Cut orange in half and squeeze some of the juice into the cider. Drop the two orange halves into the cider. Place spices in a cheese cloth and tie with a string--a tea ball also works--and drop into the cider. Simmer for 20 minutes. Do not bring to a full boil. Serve hot.
Note: Once made, you can pour it into a sanitary container and refrigerate. Then you can pour a cup at a time and heat it in your microwave.

name: Hot Apple Juice
author: Shirley Drury
instructions: Mix all ingredients except nutmeg in a Dutch oven; simmer 20 minutes. Remove and discard spices. To serve, pour into individual mugs, and sprinkle each serving with nutmeg.

name: Pink Fruit Freeze
author: Shirley Drury

ingredients.name: (1 lb. 1 oz.) cans fruit cocktail, drained

instructions: Combine softened cream cheese, ice cream, and salad dressing, mixing until well blended. Fold in fruit and nuts. Pour into 9 inch square pan. Freeze until firm. Garnish with cherries, mint and holly leaves.

name: Oreo Ice Cream
author: Suzanne Eftink
instructions: Crush package of Oreo cookies. Mix with melted butter and pat into a 9 x 13 pan. Place in freezer for 15-20 minutes to harden. Slice softened ice cream and place on top of Oreos and smooth out. Keep in freezer. Can spread caramel and pecans over the top.

name: Oreo Ice Cream
author: Kristie Slinkard

ingredients.name: (14 oz.) can Eagle Brand condensed milk
c. (1 pint) whipped cream, not topping

instructions: In a large bowl, beat egg yolks. Stir in milk and vanilla. Fold cookies and whipped cream. Line a 2 quart container with aluminum foil and pour the mixture in it. Freeze for about six hours or until frozen. Remove from foil and cut.

name: Vanilla Ice Cream
author: S.P.
instructions: In a large mixing bowl, beat eggs until foamy. Slowly add sugar and beat until thickened. Add cream, vanilla and salt; mix well. Pour into can and add milk to fill line on can and stir well. Churn in freezer about 30 minutes.

name: Ice Cream Sandwiches
author: Catrina Stone
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°. Beat egg, shortening, butter, vanilla and 1⁄2 of the cake mix until smooth. Then stir in remaining cake mix until smooth. Roll dough out and cut into any desired shape or square. Bake 8 to 10 minutes. Poke fork holes in when fresh out of oven. Put ice cream between two cookies and freeze.

name: Popsicles
author: Annita Layton
instructions: Dissolve Jello in hot water. Add remaining ingredients and mix together in pitcher. Freeze in molds.

name: Amy's Microwave Caramel Popcorn
author: Rebecca Hooper
instructions: Stir all ingredients, except popcorn and baking soda, in a micro- wave safe bowl. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring after each minute. Microwave 2 more minutes. Put popped corn in brown bag. Add baking soda to sugar mixture. Pour mixture over corn. Put bag in microwave for 1 1/2 minutes.

name: Microwave Fudge
author: Clint Estes
instructions: Sift cocoa and sugar in a large mixing bowl. Add milk and lay margarine sticks on top. Do not stir. Cook on High for 6 minutes. Remove from microwave and stir thoroughly. Add vanilla flavoring and nuts. Stir until well mixed. Pour onto buttered platter. Cool in refrigerator for 1 hour. Cut and serve. Do not double this recipe.

name: Microwave Egg Sandwich
author: C. Allen Collier
instructions: Place egg in microwave safe bowl and scramble it with a fork. Add milk or water as needed. Microwave on high for 1 minute. The egg can then be placed on bread to make a sandwich.

name: Breakfast Pizza
author: Mary Ann Lumsden
instructions: Press rolls (dough) in bottom of greased 9 x 13 pan. Beat eggs and milk with fork. Add sausage. Pour over crescent rolls. Sprinkle grated cheese on top. Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.

name: Ham and Cheese Omelet
author: Charlotte Hooper

ingredients.name: c. cubed ham, heated in microwave

instructions: Beat eggs with milk and salt and pepper. Melt butter in large skillet. Pour in eggs and cook until lightly brown on edges. Flip over, add ham and cheese. Fold in half and serve when cheese has melted.

name: Apple-Cinnamon Pancakes or Waffles
author: Ramona Glastetter

author: Martha Robert

ingredients.name: coffee mug of white canning salt (or 1 1/4 c.)

instructions: Mix thoroughly. This makes enough to cure one whole ham or pork shoulder. Use half of this for a 4 to 6 pound pork roast. Put this around outside of ham or shoulder. Take a sharp knife and push down along side of bone. Force some of the cure along bone as well as you can. Wrap in paper bag, then wrap again in cheese cloth. Store in cool place, like bottom of refrigerator or outside if cold enough, until bag becomes wet. The salt is drawing the moisture out of meat. Let sit for six weeks, then slice and fry or bake as desired. This recipe has been passed on over many generations.

name: Chocolate Cream Squares
author: Dana Gallagher

ingredients.name: lb. bittersweet chocolate, cut into 1/2 inch pieces (cake)
tsp instant espresso powder dissolved in 1/3 cup hot water (cake)
oz. bittersweet chocolate, cut into 1/2 inch pieces (filling)
oz. bittersweet chocolate, cut into 1/2 inch pieces (glaze)

instructions:
This super-rich dessert contains chocolate whipped cream between layers of bittersweet chocolate cake topped with a fudgy chocolate glaze. It's best made one 

Active: 1 hr 
Total: 8 hrs 

Step 1
Preheat the oven to 375°. Butter an 18-by-12-inch large rimmed baking sheet and line the bottom with parchment or wax paper. Butter the paper and dust with flour, tapping out any excess. In a small saucepan, combine the chocolate with the dissolved espresso and cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until melted, about 2 minutes. Let cool slightly.

Step 2
In a medium bowl, using an electric mixer, beat the egg yolks at high speed until pale, 2 to 3 minutes. At medium speed, gradually beat in 1/3 cup of the sugar. Increase the speed to high and beat until very thick and pale, about 5 minutes. Add the vanilla and the chocolate mixture and beat at low speed until blended.

Step 3
In a large bowl, using clean beaters, beat the egg whites with the cream of tartar and salt until soft peaks form. Gradually add the remaining 1/3 cup of sugar and beat at high speed until the whites are stiff and glossy. Using a large rubber spatula, fold the chocolate mixture and the flour into the whites in 2 batches, until no streaks remain. Spread the batter evenly in the prepared baking sheet. Bake for 12 minutes, or until the cake has risen and is slightly springy. Transfer to a rack and let cool.

Step 4
Run the tip of a knife around the cake and sift cocoa over the surface. Cover the cake with wax paper and top with a cutting board. Invert the cake onto the cutting board. Lift off the pan and peel off the paper. Cut the cake in half crosswise, forming 2 rectangles. Chill until firm, about 30 minutes.

Step 5
In a small saucepan, combine the chocolate with the butter and water. Cook over very low heat, stirring constantly, until melted and shiny. Scrape into a bowl and let cool. Using an electric mixer, beat the cream with the confectioners' sugar and vanilla until firm. Using a rubber spatula, fold in the cooled chocolate.

Step 6
In a small saucepan, combine the shortening with the granulated sugar and water and bring to a simmer. Off the heat, add the bittersweet and unsweetened chocolate and let stand until melted, 2 minutes. Whisk in the vanilla. Let the glaze cool until slightly thickened, about 30 minutes.

Step 7
Spread the cream filling over one half of the cake and top with the other half, cocoa side up. Press down lightly and run a cake spatula all around to smooth the edges. Pour the glaze down the center of the cake and gently spread it so that it covers the top and drizzles down the sides. Freeze the cake for 4 hours or overnight. Let stand at room temperature until just soft enough to cut. Cut the cake into 3 long strips, then cut each strip into 6 squares. Transfer to plates and serve.

Make Ahead
The cake can be frozen for 1 week.

name: Ding Dong Cake
author: Amanda Rettke

ingredients.name: oz semi sweet chocolate chopped fine- can use milk chocolate (ganache)
oz (2 cups) heavy cream, room temperature (ganache)

instructions:
Making this Dong Dong Cake was a recreation of my favorite childhood treat! Rich chocolate cake, creamy filling and a heavenly chocolate coating on the outside.
Prep Time 20 minutes
Cook Time 40 minutes
Total Time 1 hour

Instructions

CHOCOLATE CAKE
1. Sift the flour, sugar, cocoa, baking sada, baking powder, and salt into the bow! and mix until combined.
2. In another bowl, combine the buttermilk, oil, eggs, and vanilla.
3. In the bow! of a stand mixer on low speed, slowly add the wet ingredients to the dry. With mixer still on low, add the coffee and stir just to combine, scraping the bottom of the bowl with a rubber spatula.
4. Pour the batter into two 8-inch x 3-inch round prepared pans and bake for 30-40 minutes at 350°F, until a cake tester or toothpick comes out mostly clean (not wet).
5. Cool in the pans for 30 minutes, then turn them out onto a cooling rack and cool completely.

FILLING - make after Ganache, cool in refridgerator
1. Pour cold milk into a small saucepan. Before turning on the heat, whisk in flour so no lumps remain.
2. Turn heat on to medium-low and heat until mixture is thick, like a roux, stirring the whole time.
3. Remove from heat, stir in vanilla and let cool completely.
4. Cream together butter and sugar on medium-high speed, until fluffy, about 8 minutes.
5. Add in the milk mixture and beat again until mixture resembles a whipped cream.

GANACHE - make after cake comes out of oven then cool in refridgerator
1. Heat the heavy cream in a quart-sized, microwavable container and microwave for 3 to 4 minutes on high, or until it just begins to simmer. Be careful not to allow the cream to boil over. Pour the cream over the chopped chocolate and let stand for at least 2 minutes so that it can thicken.
2. (Ganache should be cool when pouring over cake)
3. When ready to pour over chilled cake, whisk the ganache until smooth and then pour. You may have some ganache left over.

name: Spinach Salad with Warm Bacon Dressing
author: Alton Brown

ingredients.name: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
oz red onion (1 small), very thinly sliced

instructions:
Total Time: 20min
Prep: 20 min

Directions

Remove the stems from the spinach and wash, drain and pat dry thoroughly. Place into a large mixing bowl and set aside

Place the eggs into an electric kettle and cover with cold water by at least 1-inch, Turn the kettle on. Once the water comes to a boil, the kettle will turn itself off. Leave the eggs in the water for 15 minutes. Remove and peel off the shell. Slice each egg into 8 pieces and set aside.

While the eggs are cooking, fry the bacon and remove to a paper towel to drain, reserving 3 tablespoons of the rendered fat. Crumble the bacon and set aside.

Transfer the fat to a small saucepan set over low heat and whisk in the red wine vinegar, sugar and Dijon mustard. Season with a small pinch each of kosher salt and black pepper.

Add the mushrooms and the sliced onion to ithe spinach and toss. Add the dressing and bacon and toss to combine. Divide the spinach between 4 plates or bowls and evenly divide the egg among them. Season with pepper, as desired. Serve immediately.
